latest.title: Peran Self-Control Dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Lifestyle dan User Experience Terhadap Impulsive Buying Pada Generasi Z Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee is influenced by lifestyle and user experience; however, previous findings are inconsistent, and the role of self-control as a moderator has not been tested together with both factors. This study aims to analyze the role of self-control in moderating the effects of lifestyle and user experience on impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee. The study employs an associative-causal quantitative approach with purposive sampling of 100 active Generation Z Shopee users. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by ANOVA (F-test) to examine the simultaneous effects. The results show that lifestyle and user experience have positive and significant effects on impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously together with self-control and its two interactions (F = 12.325; p < 0.001). Self-control has a negative and significant effect and negatively and significantly moderates the effects of lifestyle and user experience, thereby weakening both relationships. The novelty of this study lies in its integrated model, which simultaneously examines lifestyle and user experience with self-control as a moderator. The better Generation Z's self-control, the lower the tendency toward impulsive buying, even when influenced by lifestyle and an engaging online shopping experience. These findings are expected to provide insights for consumers and e-commerce platform managers in understanding and managing purchasing behavior.

latest.title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
latest.abstract: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

latest.title: Picture, picture on the screen: a between-subjects experiment on AI-generated vs human images on Generation Z consumers’ impulse buying intention
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing strategies, particularly in the tourism industry, where AI-enhanced imagery is increasingly used to influence consumer behaviour. However, little research has examined how AI-generated images affect impulse travel purchases compared with human-generated images. This study aims to examine the effect of AI-enhanced versus human-generated images on impulse travel purchase decisions among Generation Z travellers, using Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) theory and consumption value theory as a theoretical lens. Design/methodology/approach Through a between-person experimental design, 580 participants were randomly assigned to view either AI-enhanced or human-generated images of a non-iconic travel destination. This study analysed results using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study found that preference value and social value directly and significantly influenced impulse purchase intentions, while all consumption values, including preference, social, emotional and functional values, affected impulse purchasing through travellers’ inspiration. Additionally, AI-enhanced images led to a higher preference value for impulse purchases, whereas human-generated images were perceived as having higher social value and visual aesthetic appeal. Originality/value By integrating the S-O-R framework with consumption value theory, this study offers fresh theoretical insights into the mediating role of traveller inspiration and the distinct value perceptions elicited by AI versus human-generated visuals. These findings also offer critical insights for tourism marketers using AI-driven visual content, consumers navigating increasingly AI-mediated travel promotions

latest.title: The Mechanism of the Affect Heuristic in Social Media Marketing
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: With the growing integration of personalized content recommendations, emotionally engaging advertisements, and seamless purchasing functions on social media platforms, understanding how emotional responses influence consumer judgments and purchasing decisions has become increasingly important in digital marketing research. This literature review examines how the affect heuristic influences consumer responses to social media marketing. Drawing on existing research, it explores how short videos, live streaming, and algorithmic recommendations amplify emotional responses and shape purchase-related decisions. The findings suggest that positive emotions influence consumer behaviour through emotional arousal, trust, social validation, and emotional contagion. Negative emotions, particularly fear and sadness, are effective under specific conditions, such as when credible solutions or meaningful outcomes are presented. However, emotional marketing also raises ethical concerns, including manipulation and consumer vulnerability. The review concludes that the effectiveness of emotional appeals depends on product type, platform characteristics, and consumer context. Further research using experimental and transactional data is needed to establish causal relationships between emotional responses and actual purchases.

latest.title: Do Tourist Levies Shorten Stays and Divert Visitors? A Quantitative Survey of Levy Design in India
latest.venue: American Journal of Tourism and Hospitality
latest.abstract: Visitor levies are spreading across Indian destinations, but the measures adopted so far differ in how the charge is structured (per night versus once per stay), how it is presented (included in the quoted price versus added at check-out) and whether the use of revenue is specified. This study tests, with primary survey data, whether these design features shape the behavioural margins a levy is meant to move: length of stay, off-site spending and diversion to untaxed alternatives. We administered a structured questionnaire to 150 overnight visitors across four Indian levy jurisdictions (Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Goa and Rajasthan) between July 2025 and March 2026. Respondents encountering a per-night levy reported significantly shorter actual stays than those encountering a flat, one-time levy (b = −0.61 nights, p < .001), and stays were shorter again when the levy was itemized at check-out rather than included in the booking price, an effect that operated largely through tax salience and pain-of-paying perceptions (both r > .37, p < .001). Destinations that communicated a specified use for levy revenue retained longer stays and higher off-site spending (both p < .001). Pain of paying, not salience alone, predicted the intention to substitute toward an untaxed neighbouring destination (odds ratio = 2.85, p = .004). A two-way analysis of variance confirmed additive, non-interacting effects of structure and presentation on length of stay, F(1, 146) = 13.6 and F (1, 131) = 13.1, respectively, both p < .001. latest.title: Mitigating cognitive dissonance in consumer decision-making: the role of marketer message sidedness and user-generated content valence
The Impact of Image Motivation on Consumption
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Sharing has become a normal part of buying in the digital era, yet it is still unclear whether sharing always raises purchase intention. This study examines how image motivation, defined as the desire to manage one's social image, influences consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intention for virtual and physical products, and how these effects vary with the scope of sharing. The evidence comes from an online survey experiment with 270 participants randomly assigned to no sharing, small-scale sharing (within close groups), or large-scale sharing (public social media). OLS regressions with demographic controls show that image motivation is associated with lower purchase intention and lower WTP. The negative effect is driven mainly by small-scale sharing, while large-scale sharing shows no significant effect. For willingness to pay, the penalty of small-scale sharing is heavier for physical products than for virtual products. Overall, the results question the assumption that social sharing uniformly promotes image-driven consumption. They point to audience scope and product type as key boundary conditions and carry implications for more targeted sharing-based marketing strategies.

latest.title: Price sensitivity and impulsive consumption in all-you-can-eat buffets: a moderated mediation perspective
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines the association between price sensitivity and impulsive consumption intention in all-you-can-eat buffet dining. Using Prospect Theory as the overall theoretical perspective and drawing on mental accounting and compensatory-consumption reasoning, it proposes a moderated mediation model involving Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), Psychological Ownership (PO), and Health Consciousness (HC). Methods A cross-sectional survey of 485 adults in China was used to test the model. FoMO and PO were specified as mediators, and HC was examined as a moderator of the associations between price sensitivity and FoMO, PO, and impulsive consumption intention. Results Price sensitivity was positively associated with impulsive consumption intention. The indirect association through PO was significant, whereas the indirect association through FoMO alone was not. The serial indirect path from price sensitivity through FoMO and PO to impulsive consumption intention was significant. The interactions between price sensitivity and HC were negative in the impulsive consumption intention, FoMO, and PO equations, indicating weaker associations with price sensitivity at higher levels of HC. Discussion The findings identify PO as the most proximal psychological correlate of impulsive consumption intention in the proposed model and highlight HC as a boundary condition for the associations involving price sensitivity. The study offers practical recommendations for buffet restaurants seeking to reduce potential over-selection and food waste, including smaller initial portions, convenient refills, messages discouraging quantity-based value maximization, and health-oriented dining guidance. Future longitudinal and experimental research can examine the temporal and causal relations

latest.title: The Influence of Food Discounts, Free Shipping, and Consumer Preferences on ShopeeFood and GrabFood Selection
latest.venue: Edunity Kajian Ilmu Sosial dan Pendidikan
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of online food delivery in Indonesia has intensified competition between ShopeeFood and GrabFood, which rely heavily on food discounts and free-delivery promotions. This study examines how food discounts, free-delivery promotions, and consumer preferences influence the selection of these two platforms and compares the strength of each effect between them. A quantitative survey was conducted with 220 respondents, mostly in Jabodetabek, who were recruited through non-probability sampling and completed an online questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met the criteria for convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability. All six hypothesized paths were positive and significant. Consumer preference had the strongest effect on the selection of ShopeeFood (b = 0.421) and GrabFood (b = 0.340). Free delivery had a larger effect than food discounts on ShopeeFood (b = 0.240 vs. 0.186), whereas on GrabFood the two promotions had comparable effects (b = 0.205 vs. 0.213). The models explained 44.7% and 35.0% of the variance in platform selection. Platforms should therefore combine promotional incentives with strategies that reinforce users' existing preferences.

latest.title: Learning Category Representations in Relation to Another Category: A Sequential Sampling Model
latest.abstract: Forming category representations from sampled category exemplars is a ubiquitous everyday process and a crucial part of many decision-making processes. The self-regulated category learning task provides a framework for studying how individuals sample category exemplars until they have sufficient confidence in their category representation. We contribute to the literature by modeling performance on this task with a sequential sampling model in which discrete samples of category evidence accumulate until reaching a decision threshold corresponding to the decision to cease sampling. In particular, the accumulation of category evidence depends on the focal category’s variability, whereas the decision to cease sampling is influenced by the context, that is, the variability of the counter-category. Importantly, we find that variability perception is relative and that sampling behavior assimilates to the characteristics of the counter-category. Our results highlight that category representation formation occurs in relation to its context. More broadly, the model demonstrates how category learning through exemplar sampling, and active information search preceding decision-making more generally, can be formalized within the sequential sampling framework.

latest.title: The Influence of User generated Content and Price Perception on Shopee Marketplace Users' Purchase Decisions in Cengkareng District, West Jakarta
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce in Indonesia has changed consumer behavior in online shopping. User-Generated Content and price perception are considered important factors influencing consumers' purchase decisions on the Shopee marketplace. This study aims to examine the influence of User-Generated Content and price perception on the purchase decisions of Shopee marketplace users in Cengkareng District, West Jakarta. This study employed a quantitative research method, with data collected through questionnaires. The study involved 100 respondents selected using a purposive sampling technique. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The results indicate that User-Generated Content has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Price perception also has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Furthermore, both variables simultaneously have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.736 (73.6%), indicating that purchase decisions can be explained by User-Generated Content and price perception, while the remaining 26.4% is explained by other factors outside the scope of this study. These findings suggest that User-Generated Content and price perception play important roles in influencing consumers' purchase decisions on the Shopee marketplace.

latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fash

latest.title: Learner Choice, Not Learning Styles: Why giving learners a say in how they learn is better supported by evidence than matching them to a "style"
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Matching teaching to a learner’s preferred sensory “style” remains popular, yet it is not supported by well-designed experiments, and belief in it remains widespread among educators. This white paper proposes a better-supported alternative: letting learners choose their route through a course while the learning outcomes and assessment stay the same for everyone. Drawing on research on choice, choice overload, self-determination theory and instructional guidance, it sets out five design principles, seven learning approaches, a worked example, guidance for institutions and a practitioner checklist. The paper is a conceptual synthesis and does not report new empirical data.

latest.title: تأثير تصميم قائمة الطعام في المطاعم على خيارات المستهلكين ومستوى رضاهم: دراسة تجريبية
authors: جنة وائل أسعد شحات محمد Mohammed
latest.abstract: تُعدّ قوائم الطعام في المطاعم واجهات تواصل محورية وأدوات تسويقية استراتيجية وليست مجرد قوائم جامدة لاستعراض الأطباق والأسعار. تتقصى هذه الدراسة التجريبية تأثير عناصر التصميم البصري لقائمة الطعام—بما في ذلك تخطيط الصفحة، والخطوط، والتصوير الفوتوغرافي للأطعمة، والأوصاف الحسية للأطباق، وصيغ عرض الأسعار، والتمييز البصري—على هيكلية خيارات المستهلك، ومعوقات اتخاذ القرار، ومستوى الرضا بعد الطلب عبر قوائم الطعام المطبوعة، وشاشات العرض الرقمية، ومنصات رموز الاستجابة السريعة (QR) على الهواتف المحمولة.واستنادًا إلى نظرية العبء المعرفي (CLT)، ونموذج المثير-الكائن-الاستجابة (S-O-R)، وأطر هندسة قوائم الطعام الكلاسيكية، تُقيّم هذه الدراسة البيانات التجريبية المستمدة من استبيانات المستهلكين (N = 204). وتكشف النتائج المحللة وصفيًا أن الفوضى البصرية، وأحجام الخطوط غير المناسبة، والأوصاف الغامضة للأطباق تزيد بشكل ملحوظ من صعوبة القرار والجهد الذهني المبذول أثناء عملية الطلب. وعلى العكس من ذلك، فإن التخطيط الهيكلي المنظم، والعناوين الرئيسية الواضحة للأقسام، والتصوير الفوتوغرافي عالي الجودة للأطعمة المختارة، والإشارات البصرية (مثل شارات "وجبة الشيف الخاصة" ومربعات التمييز المظللة) تسهم بقوة في تسهيل تصفح العناصر وتوجيه اختيار الأطباق بفاعلية. وبشكل حاسم، يمارس أسلوب عرض الأسعار تأثيرًا مركبًا، حيث تؤثر رموز العملات الصريحة مقارنة بالتنسيق الرقمي الخفي بشكل مباشر على الوعي بالتكلفة وإنفاق المستهلك.ختامًا، تقدم هذه الدراسة توصيات عملية محددة ومستندة إلى البيانات لمشغلي قطاع الضيافة الذين يسعون إلى تحسين بيئة اتخاذ القرار لدى المستهلك، والحد من الإجهاد المعرفي، وتعزيز الرضا العام عن تجربة تناول الطعام، كما تطرح اتجاهات استراتيجية للبحوث التجريبية المستقبلية في إدارة الضيافة وتصميم قوائم الطعام الرقمية.الكلمات المفتاحية: تصميم قائمة الطعام في المطاعم، سلوك المستهلك، نظرية العبء المعرفي، نموذج المثير-الكائن-الاستجابة (S-O-R)، هندسة قائمة الطعام، معوقات اتخاذ القرار، قوائم الطعام الرقمية عبر رمز

latest.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Shaping Consumer Buying Behaviour Among Higher Education Students: An Empirical Study
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming embedded in digital platforms through recommendation engines, chatbots, predictive search, personalised advertising and automated decision-support tools. This study examines the role of AI in shaping consumer buying behaviour among higher education students. The study specifically considers AI adoption, trust in AI-enabled recommendations and AI-driven personalisation as important dimensions of the contemporary digital buying process. A quantitative research design was adopted using an illustrative sample of 250 higher education students and a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-test, Chi-square test and one-way ANOVA were applied to examine the proposed relationships and group differences. The results indicate positive associations between AI-related constructs and consumer buying behaviour, while significant differences are observed across levels of AI experience. The findings indicate that familiarity with AI-enabled technologies can influence how students search for information, evaluate alternatives and form purchase decisions. The study also highlights the importance of trust, transparency, privacy and consumer control in AI-mediated consumption. The findings provide implications for digital marketers, higher education institutions and technology developers seeking to develop responsible AI-enabled consumer experiences.

latest.title: A Study on Consumer Buying Behaviour in the Era of E-Commerce
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has changed how consumers recognise needs, search for information, evaluate alternatives, purchase products and evaluate their experience afterwards. This paper examines consumer buying behaviour in the era of e-commerce by synthesising established theories of consumer decision-making with contemporary research on online retail. It reviews the classical five-stage decision process, the Technology Acceptance Model, the Theory of Planned Behaviour and trust-based models, and then analyses the main factors that shape online buying behaviour: perceived usefulness and ease of use, trust and perceived risk, price and promotions, online reviews, personalisation, payment convenience, delivery and returns, and social influence. The paper proposes an integrated conceptual framework and six testable hypotheses, and outlines a mixed-method research design that can be used to validate the framework empirically. The analysis suggests that, while convenience and price remain the dominant drivers, trust, social proof and post-purchase service increasingly determine whether a first-time buyer becomes a loyal customer. The paper concludes with managerial implications for e-retailers, policy implications for regulators, and directions for future research.

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT ON CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN ILORIN METROPOLIS
latest.abstract: This study investigated the impact of social media marketing on consumer decision-making with specific focus on online retail businesses in Ilorin, Kwara State Nigeria. Descriptive survey research design was adopted and the population of the study was 1200 consumers who use the different social medial handles to buy products at Mamtess Mega Shopping Mall in Ilorin as at March, 2026. Taro Yamane (1967) formula was used to determine the sample size of 300 and out of which 250 copies of the well-structured questionnaire were retrieved. Descriptive statistics was used to analyze data in tabular form and representing the data in frequencies and percentage. The inferential statistics make use of simple linear and multiple regression for its analysis. Findings showed that social media marketing variables have impact on consumer decision-making. And the study therefore, concluded that social media marketing has significant impact on consumer purchase decision-making. Findings also revealed that audience engagement has more impact on consumer decision than content quality and platform frequency. Based on the conclusion of the study, it was recommended that business owners should extensively leverage on the social media marketing variables in order to influence the purchase intention, repeat purchase, and patronage of the consumer.

latest.title: Exploring TikTok Affiliate Marketing: How Content Quality, Audience Engagement, and Influencer Credibility Shape Purchase Intention
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: TikTok is one of the emerging social-commerce platforms that enables integration of product information, audience interaction and influencer endorsement in short-form video formats. This study investigated the influence of content quality, audience engagement and influencer credibility on purchase intention of 300 adult TikTok users from Naawan, Misamis Oriental, Philippines. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed. A four-point Likert-type questionnaire was used to gather data from the participants, which was analyzed using hierarchical multiple regression. Content quality was entered in the first stage followed by audience engagement and influencer credibility in the subsequent two stages. Results showed that while content quality explained 35.7% of the variance in purchase intention, audience engagement and influencer credibility explained additional 11.4% and 8.9% respectively. The final model explained 56.0% of variance (F(3, 296) = 125.65, p < .001, R² = .560, adjusted R² = .556) with all predictors positively related to purchase intention. Influencer credibility, however, had the strongest positive relationship with purchase intention even when the effects of content quality and audience engagement were controlled. Diagnostic tests for multicollinearity and residual independency were minimal. Furthermore, the use of HC3 robust standard errors to test for heteroscedasticity supported the stability of findings despite the existence of said phenomenon. The study further highlighted the complementary roles of informative content, audience interaction and influencer endorsement in affiliate marketing via TikTok. latest.title: The Effect of Virtual Try-On Technologies on Purchase Intention in Fashion Retailing: The Mediating Role of Perceived Product Fit
authors: L G D T B Thundeniya
latest.abstract: The rapid development of online fashion stores has added more challenges to the reality that consumers cannot physically analyse something like a piece of fashionable dress and buy it, especially in a size that fits. One of the biggest factors that prevents purchase intention and causes dissatisfaction and high turnover among consumers is the uncertainty related to the fittings. In turn, fashion retailers have been steadily developing virtual try-on (VTO) technologies as a new tool for assessing online products. However, the empirical findings on the usefulness of virtual try-on technologies in influencing purchase intention remain mixed, which justifies the need for a more focused conceptual framework. This concept paper examines the influence of virtual try-on technologies on purchase intention in online fashion retailing and how perceived product fit mediates this effect. The paper presents a summary of the potential theoretical and empirical sources on the subject and argues that virtual try-on technologies do not directly impact purchase intention; instead, they have an indirect impact, as they enhance consumers' confidence in the garment fit. The perceived product fit concept is theorised as being an important thinking process which minimises the uncertainty of the fit and maximises the confidence in making the decision. The article introduces a well-organised conceptual framework that relates the features of virtual try-on technology and perceived product fit to purchase intention, offering both theoretical and empirical insights and implications for online retailers interested in maximising the purchasing experience.

latest.title: Generational Differences in Omnichannel Shopping: Motivations, Cross-Channel Behavior, and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In an era where omnichannel retailing has become one of the most prominent topics in the retail industry, this study applies the Generational Cohort Theory to the context of omnichannel behavior in an emerging market. It aims to enhance the academic understanding and provide practical insights for retailers seeking to develop effective strategies for different generational cohorts. Using MANOVA, this study analyzed data collected from 341 respondents to investigate differences among Generation X, Generation Y, and Generation Z in shopping motivation, hedonic shopping motivation, cross-channel behavior, and customer loyalty. The findings reveal that Gen X, Gen Y, and Gen Z differ significantly in their shopping and hedonic shopping motivations, while no significant differences are found in cross-channel behavior and customer loyalty. By highlighting these distinctions, this study extends the application of the Generational Cohort Theory to omnichannel retailing in an emerging market. For industry practitioners, the findings emphasize the importance of understanding generational shopping motivations when designing omnichannel strategies. Rather than assuming that different generations exhibit distinct behavioral patterns or loyalty levels, retailers should tailor their approaches to consumers’ Shopping and hedonic needs to encourage cross-channel engagement and strengthen customer loyalty.

latest.title: Beyond Personalisation: Understanding the Influence of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Social Media Marketing on Consumer Engagement, Brand Trust and Purchase Intention among Generation Z Consumers in India
latest.venue: Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into social media marketing has transformed the ways in which brands communicate with consumers, personalise promotional content and influence purchasing decisions. AI-driven marketing technologies, including recommendation algorithms, predictive analytics, automated chatbots and generative AI content, enable organisations to deliver personalised and interactive marketing experiences. However, the effectiveness of these technologies in influencing consumer purchase intention depends not only on technological capabilities but also on consumers' psychological responses, particularly their engagement with brands and trust in AI-mediated marketing communication. This paper develops a conceptual understanding of the relationship between AI-driven social media marketing and consumer purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in India, with particular emphasis on the mediating roles of consumer engagement and brand trust. Drawing upon the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, consumer engagement theory and trust-based perspectives, the paper proposes an integrated conceptual model explaining how AI-enabled marketing stimuli influence consumers' cognitive, emotional and behavioural responses and subsequently shape purchase intention. The paper adopts a conceptual research approach supported by a critical review of relevant academic literature. It identifies AI-enabled personalisation, content relevance, interactivity and perceived transparency as important characteristics of AI-driven social media marketing. Consumer engagement and brand trust are proposed as complementary mediating mechanisms through which marketing stimuli may influence purchase intention. latest.title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions specifically within the used motorcycle showroom context.

latest.title: Consumers’ well-being in livestreaming commerce: antecedents and consequences
latest.abstract: Livestreaming commerce represents an increasingly important form of digital retailing. This study examines relationships among informational and emotional support, streamer characteristics (expertise, trustworthiness and attractiveness), livestreaming environmental characteristics (interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence), consumers’ perceived value, shopping well-being and continuance intention. Survey data from 301 livestreaming consumers in China were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA) and combined importance-performance map analysis (cIPMA). Perceived value and shopping well-being were positively related to continuance intention, and perceived value was positively related to shopping well-being. Expertise, interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence showed significant positive relationships with perceived value. The direct relationships for informational support, emotional support, trustworthiness and attractiveness were non-significant. Integrating PLS-SEM with NCA and cIPMA differentiated important predictors from minimum conditions associated with higher perceived value. The findings extend understanding of shopping well-being as a quality-of-life evaluation in livestreaming commerce.

latest.title: AI-Driven Consumer Decision-Making among Higher Education Students: Examining the Roles of Adoption, Trust and Personalization
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: The digital space where higher-education students find products, compare them, get personalised recommendations and make online purchases is becoming more and more interwoven with artificial intelligence. This paper analyses the relationship between the adoption of AI, confidence in AI-based recommendations and AI-based personalisation and consumer purchasing behaviour amongst higher learning institutions. Two-way (quantitative) cross-sectional methodology is demonstrated using the simulated sample of 150 objects in the form of a quantitative cross-sectional study. A five-point Lickert scale has been designed in the form of a structured question to embrace AI adoption, AI trust, AI personalisation and consumer buying behaviour. Applying reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA and exploratory multiple regression. The simulated analysis shows a high internal consistency among the constructs and positive correlations between AI-related variables and buying behaviour. The differences in buying behaviour among the levels of AI experience may also be found, and the exploratory regression shows that the composite AI variables present a significant explanatory amount of variance. These numerical findings are explicitly exemplary and are not findings in reality by actual respondents. The research offers the student through the lens based on a convenient framework aimed at studying the potential role of convenience, trust, personalisation and perceived control in influencing purchases by AI in the context of higher education.

latest.title: From Environmental Knowledge to Green Flight Preference: An Empirical Study
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: The growing emphasis on environmental sustainability has intensified the need to understand sustainable consumer behaviour in the airline industry. This study develops and tests an integrated model examining the relationships between perceived environmental knowledge, green marketing awareness, green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Data were collected from airline passengers in Türkiye and analysed using a structural equation modelling approach. The findings indicate that perceived environmental knowledge positively influences both green marketing awareness and green flight preference, while its effect on green brand trust is not significant and its relationship with price tolerance is negative. Green marketing awareness positively affects green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Green brand trust does not play a positive moderating role in the effect of green marketing awareness on green flight preference. In addition, green brand trust significantly enhances green flight preference. The results suggest that environmental knowledge alone is insufficient to foster price acceptance for green flight options, highlighting the importance of credible green marketing practices in shaping trust and behavioural intentions in the airline industry. The study contributes to sustainable consumer behaviour literature by integrating cognitive, marketing and behavioural constructs in aviation context.

latest.title: Islamic Financial Product Acceptance and the Effectiveness of Inflation Targeting in Kenya: A Theoretical and Calibration Analysis of Monetary Policy Transmission.
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Kenya's forecasting- and policy-based inflation-targeting regime has developed alongside a slow but accelerating formalisation of Islamic, or Sharia-compliant, finance: fully fledged Islamic banks operating since 2008, a growing number of Islamic windows in conventional banks and, in July 2024, the listing of Linzi Sukuk, the first Sharia-compliant product admitted to the Nairobi Securities Exchange. This paper examines how growing acceptance of Islamic financial products interacts with the transmission of the Central Bank Rate (CBR) to inflation and output. It develops a dual-banking-augmented small open-economy New Keynesian framework in which an Islamic product acceptance intensity variable enters household financing choices, firm marginal cost, bank rate setting and the central bank's policy problem. From an explicit household budget constraint, a bank repricing problem and a central bank loss function, the paper derives an attenuated IS curve, a financing-cost-augmented Phillips curve, a partial-adjustment rule linking Islamic profit rates to the policy rate, and a closed-form compensatory policy coefficient. Acceptance itself is modelled with a Bass diffusion equation. The paper reviews the cross-country evidence that Islamic financing responds less than conventional financing to policy-rate changes and that Islamic profit rates track conventional rates imperfectly, and finds that neither the Central Bank of Kenya's Quarterly Projection Model nor its macroeconometric model currently treats Sharia-compliant intermediation as a distinct block. latest.title: A EVOLUÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA E O NOVO COMPORTAMENTO DO CONSUMIDOR, QUE AGORA É MONITORADO POR ALGORITMOS
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: The expansion of digital platforms has transformed entertainment consumption, as algorithms recommend content based on user habits. This study aims to understand how these systems influence choices and behaviors, considering the effects of personalization and cultural diversity. The research draws upon the ideas of Marshall McLuhan, Theodor Adorno, Zygmunt Bauman, and Pierre Bourdieu. It notes that while platform recommendations facilitate access to content and help broaden exposure to different cultures, they also foster the creation of digital bubbles and the repetition of preferences. The study concludes that, despite their convenience, algorithms can steer consumer choices, underscoring the importance of maintaining a critical and conscious relationship with these platforms.

latest.title: From Virtual to Valuable: How Influencer Type and Product Type Shape Consumer Value Co‐Creation Intention
latest.abstract: Virtual and human influencers offer distinct social and experiential cues, but their relative effectiveness may depend on how consumers evaluate the endorsed product. Drawing on the cognitive‐affective‐behavioral framework, this research integrates social information processing theory and cognitive‐affective system theory to examine consumer value co‐creation intention. Across three between‐subjects experiments (N = 994), results reveal a consistent matching effect: virtual influencers have a relative advantage for search products, whereas human influencers have a relative advantage for experience products. This matching effect operates through parasocial interaction and empathy: forming a parasocial representation may make an influencer's perspective and affective cues more accessible, providing a relational basis for subsequent empathy. Consistent with this sequence, both the indirect effect through parasocial interaction and the serial indirect effect through parasocial interaction and empathy follow this product‐dependent pattern across both product categories, whereas the indirect effect through empathy alone favors human influencers only for experience products. Together, these findings identify product type as a boundary condition linking relational and affective processes to consumer value co‐creation intention, offering practical insights for aligning influencer selection with product characteristics.

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF BRAND DIFFERENTIATION STRATEGIES ON CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF AUTOMOBILE PRODUCTS: A STUDY OF TOYOTA AND HONDA MOTOR MANUFACTURING COMPANIES N FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY ABUJA, NIGERIA
latest.abstract: This research analyzed how brand differentiation approaches affect consumer patronage toward automobile brands in Abuja, Nigeria's capital region. The study focused specifically on examining whether the design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda cars shape how customers relate to these brands—measured through their confidence in the brands, inclination to buy again, and willingness to recommend them to others. Using a survey methodology, 300 individuals participated in the research through convenience-based selection. Questionnaires were used to gather information, which was then processed using Linear Regression analysis via SPSS 22. The results indicated that both design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda automobiles significantly and positively affect customer loyalty toward these brands. The study recommends that company leaders prioritize investment in research and development focused on improving design and performance quality as a key marketing approach to win over new customers and maintain existing ones.

latest.title: The Role of Tabligh Trait and Consumer Trust in Increasing Broiler Chicken Sales at Batang Kuis Market : PERAN SIFAT TABLIGH DAN KEPERCAYAAN KONSUMEN TERHADAP PENINGKATAN PENJUALAN AYAM POTONG DI PASAR BATANG KUIS
latest.abstract: This study is grounded in the urgency of implementing Islamic business ethics, particularly information transparency (tabligh) and halal product assurance, to sustain traditional market trading. This research aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous roles of the tabligh trait and consumer trust in increasing broiler chicken sales at Batang Kuis Market, Deli Serdang Regency. Utilizing a quantitative associative approach, this study involved a population of broiler chicken buyers, with a sample of 125 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Primary data were gathered through validity- and reliability-tested questionnaires, and analyzed using classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The findings reveal that the tabligh trait has a positive and significant partial effect on sales increase. Consumer trust also exhibits a positive and significant partial influence, serving as the most dominant contributor. Simultaneously, both variables significantly drive sales growth, explaining a substantial portion of sales variations while the remainder is influenced by external factors. In conclusion, consistent application of muamalah transparency and halal trust guarantees effectively enhances trader turnover and business sustainability in traditional markets. Abstrak. Penelitian ini didasari oleh urgensi penerapan etika bisnis Islam, khususnya keterbukaan informasi (tabligh) dan jaminan kehalalan produk, guna menjaga keberlanjutan perdagangan di pasar tradisional. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran sifat tabligh dan kepercayaan konsumen secara parsial maupun simultan terhadap peningkatan penjualan ayam potong di Pasar Batang Kuis, Kabupaten Deli Serdang. latest.title: A Story to Sell: The Mediating Role of Storytelling in Consumer Purchase Intention toward Regional Woven Fabrics
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study examines the associations of Perceived Government Support and influencer marketing with consumer purchase intention toward traditional woven fabrics from East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, considering storytelling as a mediating variable. Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative survey involving 347 consumers of East Nusa Tenggara woven fabrics was conducted. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess direct and indirect relationships. Finding/Results – Perceived Government Support showed no significant direct association with purchase intention (β = 0.049; p = 0.433) but was positively associated with storytelling (β = 0.574; p < 0.001). Influencer marketing positively related to storytelling (β = 0.222; p = 0.019) and purchase intention (β = 0.166; p = 0.002). Storytelling significantly predicted purchase intention (β = 0.695; p < 0.001) and demonstrated indirect-only mediation for government support (β = 0.399; p < 0.001) and complementary mediation for influencer marketing (β = 0.154; p = 0.012). Originality/Value – This study integrates government support, influencer marketing, and cultural storytelling into a unified framework explaining purchase intention toward traditional cultural products. It highlights storytelling as a strategic marketing approach for governments and SMEs while providing a foundation for future cross-cultural and longitudinal research.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Promosi, dan Harga terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Sepeda Motor Honda pada Dealer Central Sakti Motor Nusukan
latest.abstract: Increasing competition in the motorcycle industry requires dealers to understand the factors that influence consumer purchase decisions, particularly through service quality, promotion, and price. This study aims to analyze the effects of service quality, promotion, and price on the purchase decision of Honda motorcycles at Central Sakti Motor Nusukan Dealer. The study uses a quantitative research method with data collected by distributing questionnaires to consumers who had purchased Honda motorcycles at Central Sakti Motor Nusukan Dealer. The sample consisted of 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data analyses included instrument testing, classical assumption testing, multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination (R²) testing. The results show that service quality had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.000 and a regression coefficient of 0.355. Promotion had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.000 and a regression coefficient of 0.446. Price also had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.046 and a regression coefficient of 0.183. The F-test results show that the regression model was appropriate for use, with a significance value of 0.000, while the coefficient of determination test produced an Adjusted R Square of 0.725, indicating that service quality, promotion, and price explained 72.5% of the purchase decision, while the remaining 27.5% was influenced by other variables outside the research model. latest.title: Determinants of Spotify Student Package Purchase Decisions among University Students: The Roles of Perceived Value, Hedonic Motivation, and Lifestyle
latest.abstract: The rapid development of digital music streaming services has transformed consumer behavior, particularly among university students who increasingly adopt subscription-based entertainment platforms. This study aims to examine the influence of perceived value, hedonic motivation, and lifestyle on purchase decisions for Spotify Student Package among university students in Surakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative research approach with a survey method was employed. The study population consisted of university students in Surakarta who used Spotify Student Package, with 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, F-test, and the coefficient of determination with the assistance of SPSS. The results indicate that perceived value has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.450 and a significance value of 0.000. Hedonic motivation also has a positive and significant influence on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.238 and a significance value of 0.027. Furthermore, lifestyle has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.329 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, perceived value, hedonic motivation, and lifestyle significantly influence Spotify Student Package purchase decisions, as indicated by an F-value of 134.115 with a significance level of 0.000. The adjusted R-square value of 0.801 demonstrates that the three independent variables explain 80.1% of the variation in purchase decisions. latest.title: Pengaruh Lifestyle dan Impulsive Buying terhadap Keputusan Pem-belian Konsumen Smartphone Apple di Kota Depok
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of lifestyle and impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously, on the purchasing decisions of Apple smartphone consumers in Depok City. The urgency of this study arises from the limited research directly examining the relationship between lifestyle, impulsive buying, and purchasing decisions without incorporating mediating variables such as purchase intention, particularly among consumers in Depok City. This study employed an associative quantitative approach with a survey design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 96 respondents who had previously purchased Apple smartphones and resided in Depok City. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, while the sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula. The collected data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, and hypothesis testing (t-test and F-test) with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The results revealed that lifestyle had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 5.426, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Impulsive buying also had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 8.971, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, lifestyle and impulsive buying had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated F-value of 263.973, exceeding the critical F-value of 3.09, and a significance value of 0.000. These two variables collectively explained 85.0% of the variance in purchasing decisions. These findings suggest that companies

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions And Their Influence On Canadian Perception, National Sentiment And Consumer Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Business & Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study investigates how recent U.S. threatened and imposed tariffs under the Trump administration have influenced Canadian public sentiment and consumer behaviour. While traditional economic analysis of tariffs focuses on macro-level indicators such as GDP and trade balances, this research explores the sociopsychological and behavioural impacts of economic protectionism on individuals. Specifically, it examines the extent to which Canadian consumers’ awareness of tariffs correlates with negatives perceptions of Americans, increased nationalism, consumer ethnocentrism and retaliatory purchasing behaviour. Drawing upon theories such as social identity theory, consumer ethnocentrism and reactance theory, the study develops a conceptual framework linking tariff awareness to five key hypotheses. A cross-sectional, quantitative survey was conducted with 123 Canadian residents, collecting data on demographic variables, attitudes toward the U.S., national sentiments and purchasing patterns. The validated instruments consisted of both self-developed scales and pre-established scales including the CETSCALE (Shimp & Sharma, 1987) and Kosterman & Feshbach’s Nationalism scale (1989). Statistical analyses revealed significant relationships across several variables. Greater awareness of U.S. tariffs was associated with more negative perceptions of Americans, heightened national pride, a stronger preference for Canadian products and reduced support for U.S. brands. Notably, consumer behaviour in Canada has shifted, with increasing domestic product loyalty and signs of consumer boycott activity, evidenced by retail behaviour. Regression models confirmed that tariff awareness significantly predicts these attitudinal and behavioural outcomes. These findings offer insights into how eco

latest.title: Toward a targeted localization framework: branding strategy replication in the Asia-Pacific bubble tea industry
latest.abstract: This study investigates how multinational corporations replicate branding strategies across culturally and institutionally diverse markets in the Asia-Pacific, specifically comparing Taiwan (a mature market) and Indonesia (an emerging market) via the bubble tea industry. Utilizing structural equation modeling (SEM) and multi-group analysis on 293 consumers with prior brand interaction, the research tests the sequential associations of brand equity components and the moderating role of national institutional maturity. The research confirms a consistent brand equity structural framework: Brand Image (BI) is positively associated with Brand Satisfaction (BS), which in turn correlates with Brand Trust (BT) and sequentially predicts Purchase Intention (PI). Furthermore, institutional contingencies moderate these pathways. In emerging markets with higher information asymmetry, purchase intention is heavily image-driven, relying on BI as a heuristic signal to mitigate risks. Conversely, mature markets are satisfaction-driven, emphasizing personal experiential validation over social signaling. This study introduces the Targeted Localization framework. While the strategic weights of brand image and satisfaction shift dramatically across contexts (supporting Targeted Localization), the empirical rejection of contextual differences in brand trust reveals its role as a universally critical baseline for transnational purchase intentions.

latest.title: The Hidden Economics of Digital Lending: Algorithmic Credit Intermediation, Consumer Choice and Regulatory Accountability under India’s Digital Lending Framework
latest.abstract: India’s 2025 digital-lending framework expressly addresses transparency in the presentation of loan offers. This article explores the transparency of digital marketplaces for loans. It relies on doctrinal, institutional economics and behavioral economics theories and concepts to substantiate its arguments. The article argues that, despite similarities in the wording of multiple loan offers, there may exist differences in the priorities and values of the offers, and borrowers may not be able to consider all those factors. The article considers the 2025 framework issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as a positive development to regulate lending marketplaces. However, the article identifies an imbalance where regulated entities remain responsible for LSP oversight, but verifying the operation of those controls may be difficult. The article describes a “price-choice-accountability” triad to illustrate that lending marketplaces should establish reasonable processes based on prior notice, and control misleading practices. The article does not examine the extent to which lending marketplaces, guided by the 2025 Directions, have introduced loan offer interfaces that bias against borrowers.

latest.title: Beyond Mutual Consent: Reconstructing Tarādin in Islamic Price Ethics amid Luxury Branding and Symbolic Consumption
latest.abstract: Premium price acceptance in the luxury product market is driven not only by functional utility, but also by brand heritage, exclusivity, and symbolic value—creating a pricing paradox in which elevated prices enhance rather than deter consumer desirability. Within Islamic economics, this phenomenon challenges classical assessments of consumer consent (tarāḍin), which primarily evaluate formal contractual assent and overt willingness to pay. This study aims to reconstruct tarāḍin within Islamic price ethics by shifting its analytical focus from formal agreement to the procedural integrity of value formation amid luxury branding and symbolic consumption. Employing a qualitative-conceptual library research method, this study systematically selected and synthesized foundational Qur’anic and fiqh al-mu‘āmalāt texts alongside peer-reviewed literature on Islamic business ethics, luxury branding, and symbolic consumption through thematic coding and comparative conceptual synthesis. From this analytical procedure, the study derives four interdependent dimensions in the proposed normative model of reconstructed tarāḍin: informational transparency, voluntary consent, value representation, and ethical price justice. Addressing the luxury pricing paradox, these four dimensions demonstrate that genuine consent requires evaluating whether symbolic prestige is communicated without deception (tadlīs), manufactured scarcity coercion, or gross price disparity (ghabn fāḥisy). This study offers a theoretical contribution to Islamic economic thought by extending tarāḍin beyond classical doctrines of honesty and contractual validity into an evaluative framework for contemporary luxury marketing. latest.title: الثقة البصرية وخيار المستهلك: دراسة مسحية حول تصميم واجهة المراجعات للأعمال التجارية المنزلية
latest.abstract: تفحص هذه الدراسة كيفية تأثير عناصر تصميم واجهة المراجعات على ثقة المستهلك وقرارات الشراء عند تقييم الأعمال التجارية المنزلية. ونظراً لأن المستهلكين غالباً ما يتعذر عليهم فحص المنتجات فعلياً أو التفاعل مع البائعين، فإن المراجعات عبر الإنترنت توفر معلومات لتقييم جودة المنتج، ومصداقية البائع، ومخاطر الشراء. تركز الدراسة على كيفية عرض المراجعات، بما في ذلك صور العملاء، والتعليقات المكتوبة، وتقييمات النجوم، ومؤشرات "المشتري التحقق منه"، وتواريخ المراجعات، وحجم المراجعات، ونوع الخط (Typography)، وفصل الآراء الإيجابية عن السلبية. تم اعتماد منهج بحثي وصفي باستخدام استبيان أكمله 105 مشاركين. جرى تحليل الإجابات المغلقة من خلال التكرارات والنسب المئوية، بينما تم فحص السؤال المفتوح تحليلياً وفقاً للمواضيع الرئيسة (Thematically). تظهر النتائج أن المراجعات عبر الإنترنت تلعب دوراً في مرحلة ما قبل الشراء: إذ إن 70.48% من المشاركين يقرؤون المراجعات دائمًا أو غالبًا قبل الشراء، وتصوّر 80.95% أن المراجعات مهمة للغاية أو مهمة جداً. علاوة على ذلك، أفاد 64.76% بأن المراجعات تؤثر على ثقتهم بدرجة كبيرة أو كبيرة جداً. برزت صور العملاء كعنصر مؤثر: فقد كانت مصدر معلومات شائعة الاختيار (62.86%) والعنصر البصري الأكثر فائدة (43.81%)، وأشار 80.00% إلى أن صور العملاء تجعل المراجعات أكثر جديرة بالثقة. كما دعمت شارات "المشتري التحقق منه" مستوى الثقة، حيث أفاد 70.48% بزيادة الثقة عند عرض هذه المؤشرات. وكان التنظيم الواضح أمراً مهماً: حيث وجد 67.62% أنه من أسهل تحديد المراجعات الجديرة بالثقة عندما تكون المعلومات منظمة بوضوح. فيما يتعلق بقرارات الشراء، ذكر 71.43% أن طريقة عرض المراجعات أثرت على اختيارهم بين الأعمال التجارية المتشابهة، في حين أن 80.95% كانوا من المحتمل أو من المحتمل جداً أن يفكروا في الشراء عندما تُعرض المراجعات بوضوح مع الصور ومعلومات التحقق. بشكل عام، تشير النتائج إلى أن الأدلة البصرية الموثوقة، والآراء المكتوبة الغنية بالمعلومات، ودلائل التحقق، والتنظيم الواضح للمراجعات تُعد سمات مهمة لل

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement.
