This conceptual paper examines five key dimensions of this evolution: advanced econometric modeling with R and Python, real-time data integration via APIs, Natural Language Processing (NLP) for unstructured data, Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) and computational simulations, and democratization of big data through cloud platforms such as Google Big Query, AWS, and Snowflake. The analysis shows that undergraduates are transitioning from consumers of historical data to builders of data pipelines and forecasting models. The paper discusses implications for curriculum design, graduate employability, and research capacity in North Central Nigeria. It concludes that moving beyond visualization equips economics students with competencies required for a data-driven economy.

latest.title: Training future sustainable culinary professionals through game-based learning: development and preliminary evaluation of a carbon-reducing culinary board game
latest.abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop an educational board game that integrates carbon-reducing culinary competence and to evaluate its content validity and students’ self-reported player experiences in foodservice education. Methods Using the ADDIE instructional design model, we translated competency indicators across three dimensions (knowledge, attitudes, and skills) into game mechanics for Carbon-Reducing Culinary Helper. Experts in sustainable foodservice education, culinary instruction, board game design, and industry practice reviewed the game’s content. During playtesting, 82 undergraduate students in hospitality and culinary-related programs completed the Player Experience Inventory (PXI). PXI scores were compared between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Results Item-level content validity indices ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, indicating satisfactory content validity. The ten PXI dimensions showed high internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.893 to 0.960. Students generally reported positive player experiences. No statistically significant differences in player experience were found between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Discussion The expert ratings and positive player experiences support the game’s potential as a supplementary tool for foodservice education, education on sustainable food practices, and professional training for foodservice practitioners. The development process illustrates how competency indicators can be translated into game mechanics for sustainability-oriented foodservice education.

latest.title: Persepsi Informasi Digital, Kepercayaan, dan Niat Beli Fashion Online: Studi Komparatif Gender pada Mahasiswa
latest.abstract: Dalam belanja fesyen daring, konsumen mengandalkan deskripsi produk dan ulasan pembeli karena mereka tidak dapat mencoba pakaian atau memeriksa bahannya secara langsung. Perbedaan penilaian mahasiswa berdasarkan gender terhadap kedua sumber informasi tersebut, kepercayaan, dan niat beli masih jarang dikaji secara bersamaan. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan persepsi kualitas informasi produk, persepsi ulasan daring, kepercayaan, dan niat beli fesyen daring antara mahasiswa laki-laki dan perempuan. Analisis komparatif eksploratif menggunakan data survei potong lintang dari 566 mahasiswa aktif, terdiri atas 126 laki-laki dan 440 perempuan. Responden dipilih secara purposif dengan kriteria minimal dua kali membeli produk fesyen daring dalam enam bulan terakhir. Perbedaan rerata diuji menggunakan uji t Welch dua arah dengan koreksi Holm dan ukuran efek Hedges’ g. Mahasiswa perempuan memperoleh skor lebih tinggi pada persepsi ulasan daring (p=0,018, g=0,322) dan niat beli (p=0,035, g=0,265), dengan ukuran efek kecil. Perbedaan kualitas informasi (p=0,317) dan kepercayaan (p=0,764) tidak signifikan. Pada tingkat butir, selisih skor ulasan paling menonjol pada manfaat ulasan untuk memantapkan minat beli. Untuk niat beli, selisih terbesar terdapat pada kesediaan merekomendasikan platform kepada teman atau keluarga. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan berdasarkan gender terbatas pada aspek tertentu dalam sampel dan perlu ditafsirkan dengan mempertimbangkan ukuran efek serta cakupan indikator niat beli.

latest.title: Measuring and Evaluating Marketing Performance Using ICT Tools
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Shreya Chauhan and Ms. Kriti Khemani
latest.abstract: The journey of marketing, from a creative art to a strategic science, is perhaps most evident in how we measure its success. The tools and technologies of the Information Age have fundamentally rewritten the rules of marketing performance evaluation. For decades, the assessment of marketing's impact was retrospective, blunt, and frustratingly opaque. Success was gauged by lagging financial indicators like total sales volume or aggregate market share—final scores that revealed little about which specific plays led to victory or why a campaign resonated. This was akin to judging a play only by the final box office tally, with no insight into which scenes captivated the audience.Today, driven by the transformative power of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), this landscape has been revolutionized.

latest.title: From threat to adaptation: the psychological mechanism of AI-related cognition and experience on law students’ career indecision—an empirical test based on a moderated parallel mediation model
latest.abstract: Introduction Career indecision has become a major challenge to individuals’ vocational psychological adaptation amid technological transformation. Drawing on the cognitive appraisal theory of stress and career construction theory, this study investigates the psychological mechanisms underlying law students’ career indecision. Methods We developed and tested a moderated parallel mediation model using a sample of 1,128 students from Chinese law schools. Results The results show that the psychometric structure of the four-dimensional AI career anxiety scale is stable among Chinese law students. AI literacy/exposure experience, perceived AI substitution in the legal profession, and perceived limitations of AI legal services are the three factors that are significantly associated with career indecision. These associations are fully or partially mediated through parallel pathways involving four types of career anxiety, among which socio-technical blind-spot anxiety exhibits a particularly prominent mediating effect (with the total indirect effect accounting for 65.4% of the total effect in the “perceived limitations of AI legal services → career indecision” pathway). This finding highlights the special role that macro-level risks, such as those involving algorithmic ethics, play in the psychology of the legal profession. The results showed that there was a direct positive relationship between career adaptability and career indecision, indicating that more adaptable individuals were more sensitive to career uncertainty because of their high “concern.” Career adaptability does significantly reduce the negative effects of all four types of anxiety on career indecision, however, in each pathway. Discussion To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first attempt to empirical

latest.title: When Patients Speak More to Machines: Active Ingredients, Mechanisms, and Limitations of Mental Health Support from Large Language Models
latest.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based conversational systems are increasingly used for emotional support, self-reflection, and mental health guidance.Although these systems are neither psychotherapists nor regulated psychotherapeutic interventions, they may acquire a psychotherapylike function when users repeatedly disclose distress, seek interpretations, and act on their responses.The clinical implications of this emerging pattern of use require a conceptual framework that distinguishes general-purpose LLMs from purpose-built digital mental health interventions while recognizing that both can influence clinically relevant outcomes through different pathways.Building on contemporary psychotherapy theory, we aimed to differentiate active ingredients (e.g., fluency, immediacy, apparent personalization, perceived empathy, and low-friction disclosure) from mechanisms of change (e.g., expectancy, remoralization, cognitive reframing, affect regulation, behavioral activation, or, conversely, misplaced trust and dependency) through which these systems may produce beneficial or harmful effects.The phenomenological experiences resembling therapeutic alliance or emotional disclosure should not be equated with accountable psychotherapy, as current LLMs cannot reliably assume core clinical functions such as individualized formulation, risk assessment, rupture repair, or responsibility for treatment decisions.Further research should specifically evaluate AI-mediated mental health support using mechanism-informed and version-specific frameworks that extend beyond user satisfaction or short-term symptom change to include adverse events, dependency and impacts on subsequent helpseeking.In Europe, clearer psychological frameworks are necessary to evaluate the use of LLMs in health care govern

latest.title: Supporting, not replacing: counsellors’ and service coordinators’ perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in youth online chat counselling
latest.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored to support youth online chat counselling services (OCCS). Understanding stakeholders’ perspectives is essential to guide its effective implementation. This study explored counsellors’ and service coordinators’ perspectives on the role of AI in youth online chat counselling. Methods Sixty-two semi-structured interviews were conducted with counsellors and service coordinators from 33 non-profit OCCS across Belgium, Finland, Hungary, and Spain. Interviews were recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated into English, and analysed using qualitative thematic analysis in NVivo. Results Four key themes emerged during interviews: (1) attitudes towards AI, (2) current and (3) future applications, and (4) requirements for responsible implementation. Participants opposed AI replacing human counsellors but considered its growing role as inevitable. 6 out of 33 (18.2%) OCCS reported having incorporated a chatbot (at the time of the interview, type not specified). Participant reported current use of AI in OCCS included automated responses, suicide risk identification, and data management functions. Proposed future uses comprised intelligent routing, multilingual support, transcription, resource and referral identification, counsellor training, real-time suggestions and feedback, and documentation and reporting support. Participants emphasised the need for an AI ethical framework that included transparency and continuous human supervision. Discussion Participants viewed AI as a tool to support rather than replace human counsellors, particularly for administrative and service-delivery tasks. Although concerns remained regarding AI's limitations and potential impact on employment, participants identified opportunities

latest.title: Foreign Direct Investment Determinants in the Western Balkan: Insights and Implications for Albania
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) remains a crucial driver of economic transformation in the Western Balkans, where structural reforms, market integration, and political stability shape investment attractiveness. This study examines the determinants of FDI inflows in five Western Balkan economies: Albania, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Using World Bank World Development Indicators, pooled Ordinary Least Squares and fixed-effects (LSDV) panel regressions are applied to assess the impact of macroeconomic, demographic, and governance-related factors on FDI. The results indicate that market size, inflation, population, and political stability significantly influence FDI inflows, while government effectiveness emerges as a key institutional determinant at the regional level. To provide a country-specific perspective, Albania is further examined using time-series analysis, including unit root, Johansen cointegration, and Granger causality tests. The findings reveal a long-run cointegrated relationship between FDI and GDP, with unidirectional causality from FDI to economic growth, highlighting the importance of governance reforms and macroeconomic stability.

latest.title: Unveiling corporate digital responsibility disclosure practices in the banking sector: An exploratory analysis of CDR governance
latest.venue: The International Journal of Digital Accounting Research
latest.abstract: Corporate Digital Responsibility (CDR) has emerged as an important framework for addressing the ethical, governance, and accountability challenges associated with digital transformation. However, the current body of knowledge on CDR remains limited, particularly in the context of the global banking industry. This study explores the developing domain of CDR disclosures in the banking sector. Employing an exploratory qualitative analysis, it examines the extent and nature of CDR disclosures in the annual reports of the top 100 global banks from 2021-2023 and provides qualitative insights into how governance-related CDR aspects are disclosed, drawing from a sample of annual reports and supplementary web-based documents such as codes of conduct and customer privacy. Leveraging stakeholder theory, this study demonstrates how digital responsibility emerges as both an instrumental strategy to mitigate risks and a normative commitment to ethical digital practices, providing a foundation for future work on how ethical governance structures can be embedded into digital business models.

latest.title: The impact of Generative AI chatbots on behavioral intention in travel planning: A theory of consumption value perspective
latest.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots are revolutionizing online travel planning by transitioning travelers’ focus from merely gathering information to obtaining personalized recommendations and facilitating seamless bookings. Grounded in the Interactive Technology Acceptance Model and Consumption Value Theory, this study investigates how the attributes of GenAI chatbots, specifically personalization and anthropomorphism, alongside user traits such as self-efficacy and personal innovativeness, influence travel planning intention through perceived value. Data collected from a questionnaire survey were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that GenAI chatbot attributes (personalization and anthropomorphism) and user traits (self-efficacy and personal innovativeness) exert significant direct positive effects on perceived values. The indirect effects of anthropomorphism, personalization, self-efficacy, and personal innovativeness on adoption intentions are most pronounced through hedonic value, followed by utilitarian value, with novelty value playing the least prominent mediating role. This study enriches the theoretical understanding of AI-based customer service and provides tourism businesses with insights into enhancing GenAI’s features and shaping consumer perceptions.

latest.title: The Influence of AI-Based Marketing Strategies on Consumer Purchase Behaviour: A Study of Online Consumers in Chennai
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a central instrument of contemporary marketing, enabling firms to personalise offers, recommend products, target advertisements, converse with customers, forecast demand, and generate content at a scale and speed that manual methods cannot match. Yet empirical evidence on how these distinct AI-based marketing strategies shape the purchase behaviour of consumers in the Indian context remains limited. This study investigates the influence of AI-based marketing strategies on consumer purchase behaviour among online consumers in Chennai. Six independent variables—AI-Based Personalisation, AI-Driven Product Recommendations, AI-Powered Targeted Advertising, AI Chatbot Interaction, Predictive Marketing Analytics, and AI-Generated Marketing Content—were examined in relation to the dependent variable of Consumer Purchase Behaviour (encompassing purchase intention, purchase decision, actual purchase behaviour, repeat purchase behaviour, and brand preference). A quantitative research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 271 online consumers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, using a structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale. Convenience sampling was employed. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26 (descriptive statistics, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation and multiple regression) and SmartPLS (measurement and structural model assessment). The findings reveal that all six AI-based marketing strategies positively and significantly influence consumer purchase behaviour. AI-Driven Product Recommendations emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.319), followed by AI-Based Personalisation and AI-Generated Marketing Content. The regression model explains 85.7% of the variance in consumer purchase behaviour. The

latest.title: A INFLUÊNCIA DAS MÍDIAS SOCIAIS NO USO INDISCRIMINADO DE CANETAS EMAGRECEDORAS: RISCOS E IMPACTOS NA SAÚDE DOS USUÁRIOS
latest.abstract: A crescente exposição a padrões de beleza idealizados nas mídias sociais tem contribuído para intensificar a busca pelo emagrecimento e pela transformação corporal. Nesse contexto, os medicamentos injetáveis para perda de peso, popularmente conhecidos como “canetas emagrecedoras”, especialmente a semaglutida e a liraglutida, ganharam visibilidade nas plataformas digitais, sendo frequentemente divulgados como alternativas para alcançar resultados estéticos rápidos. O presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar a influência das mídias sociais no uso indiscriminado desses medicamentos, considerando os fatores socioculturais relacionados à construção da imagem corporal, à disseminação de informações digitais e aos possíveis riscos associados à utilização inadequada. Trata-se de uma pesquisa qualitativa, desenvolvida por meio de revisão narrativa da literatura, fundamentada em livros, artigos científicos e documentos institucionais relacionados à temática. A discussão aborda a valorização de padrões estéticos, a influência de influenciadores digitais na divulgação de medicamentos para emagrecimento, a circulação de informações nem sempre fundamentadas cientificamente e os riscos decorrentes do uso sem indicação e acompanhamento profissional. A literatura analisada aponta que a exposição constante a conteúdos que associam magreza, beleza e aceitação social pode contribuir para a banalização do uso desses medicamentos, favorecendo decisões baseadas em expectativas estéticas e informações inadequadas. Destaca-se, portanto, a importância da educação em saúde, da divulgação de informações confiáveis e do acompanhamento por profissionais habilitados, de modo que o uso desses medicamentos esteja fundamentado em critérios clínicos e na avaliação individualizada, e não apenas em padrõ

latest.title: Behavioral and psychiatric safety crises and their management in general and forensic inpatient psychiatric settings: a scoping review
latest.abstract: Introduction Behavioral and psychiatric safety crises are a central component of psychiatric inpatient care and include aggression, agitation or behavioral escalation, self-harm, and suicidality. These events occur in high-acuity environments characterized by severe mental illness, complex comorbidities, and fluctuating risk. Crisis phenomena remain conceptually heterogeneous, and their assessment and management vary across clinical settings. This scoping review aimed to map the literature on behavioral and psychiatric safety crises, their management, and reported outcomes in general and forensic or secure inpatient psychiatric settings. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, PsycINFO, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched using database-specific controlled vocabulary and free-text terms related to psychiatric inpatient settings, behavioral and psychiatric safety crises, and their assessment or management. Primary studies and review-level sources were synthesized separately using a descriptive and thematic approach. No formal critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. Results Forty-five sources of evidence were included, comprising 35 primary studies and 10 review-level sources. The literature predominantly addressed aggression, violence, and agitation, followed by restrictive practices as management responses or outcomes, while self-harm and suicidality were less frequently studied. Frequently examined approaches included structured short-term risk assessment linked to prevention planning, relational and organizational models, multicomponent restraint-reduction programs, de-escalation training, and environmental or sensory interventions. Several studies reported favorable outcomes following multico

latest.title: Prioritizing Hotel Service Improvements Using SERVQUAL and Sensitivity Analysis of Importance–Performance Classifications
latest.venue: Journal of Operational and Strategic Analytics
latest.abstract: Hotel managers need defensible priorities when service failures compete for limited operational resources. This study examines whether hotel service-improvement priorities remain consistent across individual attributes, reporting domains, and alternative importance–performance analysis (IPA) specifications. A voluntary survey at a three-star city hotel in İzmir, Türkiye, conducted from November 2025 to March 2026, yielded 411 questionnaires covering 22 paired expectation and perception items. An assessment using an adapted service quality scale (SERVQUAL) was combined with paired comparisons, effect sizes, a conservative multiplicity check, and sensitivity analysis of domain composition and IPA crosshairs. Seventeen items differed at the nominal 5% level, and at least 12 met the Bonferroni threshold for 22 comparisons. Common-area cleanliness (-1.826), room cleanliness (-1.367), equipment functionality (-1.023), and reservation accuracy (-0.810) showed the largest negative gaps. Tangibles and reliability remained improvement priorities under all four specifications examined. Excluding a broadly worded security-measures item changed the digital-services gap from -0.175 to approximately -0.315 and moved the domain into the improvement-priority quadrant. Domain expectation means ranged from 4.895 to 4.954, which restricted discrimination along the importance axis. The findings show how item-level evidence and specification checks help interpret priorities derived from near-ceiling expectations in this hotel. The analysis provides a practical basis for selecting housekeeping, maintenance, reservation, and data-handling processes for operational review, while distinguishing persistent priorities from classifications that depend on measurement choices.

latest.title: Psychotherapy 2035: Generative Ai Scenarios Psychotherapy 2035: A Technology Assessment Review of Generative AI Scenarios for Mental Health Care
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is entering psychotherapy faster than evidence, professional norms and regulation can follow, the configuration described by the Collingridge dilemma. This technology assessment review combines a narrative synthesis of PubMed and web searches (9 October 2026) with explorative scenario construction along two axes, locus of delivery and governance regime. Efficacy effects are small, short-lived and heterogeneous; blended and certified formats are better supported than stand-alone chatbots. Documented harms, including inadequate crisis responses, dependence and distress after model updates, concentrate outside clinical settings, and regulation is fragmented. Four scenarios result for 2035: augmented clinician, stepped hybrid care, consumer-companion market and regulated digital therapeutics. They will probably coexist. Governance should prioritize measures that are robust across scenarios (outcome and incident registries, crisis-escalation standards, continuity duties, protected human roles) and monitor early signposts.

latest.title: Digital Marketing in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Applications, Consumer Impact and Ethical Challenges
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has changed more in the last few years than in the previous two decades, and much of that change comes from artificial intelligence (AI). Brands now use machine learning, natural language processing and generative models to segment audiences, personalise messages, automate customer conversations and predict what people are likely to buy next. This paper examines how AI is being used in digital marketing, what benefits it brings to businesses and consumers, and what risks it creates. The study is descriptive and qualitative in design and relies on secondary data drawn from peer-reviewed journals, regulatory documents and published conceptual frameworks. Using a narrative literature review and a funnel-based analytical framework, the paper maps AI applications across the awareness, consideration, conversion and retention stages. The review finds that AI improves targeting accuracy, speed of content production, campaign efficiency and customer service availability, but that these gains depend heavily on data quality, human oversight and consumer trust. Concerns around privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency and over-automation remain unresolved. The paper concludes that AI works best as a partner to human marketers rather than a replacement, and it suggests directions for future empirical research, including primary studies in the Indian market.

latest.title: Can artificial intelligence be-with-clients? A conceptual review of the potential and limitations of conversational AI from the perspective of existential therapies
latest.abstract: Within the fast expansion of AI in the mental health sector, particularly conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) as a means of therapeutic support has developed rapidly. As far as research considers specific modalities at all, it is usually concerned with the cognitive-behavioral orientation. Thus, pertinent findings cannot easily be extrapolated to existential approaches and their concern with the existential givens. Addressing this conceptual gap, this paper examines the applicability and limitations of CAI in existential therapies. In order to integrate empirical and theoretical literature on conversational AI as a means of quasi-psychotherapy with core concepts of existential therapies, a conceptual review was conducted. Relevant literature was identified through a keyword-based search supplemented by emerging themes. The resulting material was discussed in reference to the ontological and phenomenological concepts of existential therapies. The synthesis demonstrates that CAI is able to simulate therapeutic dialogue and to present existential concepts. CAI’s tendency to epistemic closure and prefabricated options may diminish a user’s agency by externalizing the necessity to create meaning and take responsibility. These architectural obstacles could yet potentially be overcome in the future. However, pattern recognition and linguistic modelling cannot recreate actual shared experience which points towards a fundamental limitation rooted in the ontological locus of CAI rather than just at a technological shortcoming. Existential therapy relies on a shared lived experience characterized by embodied temporality, freedom, and finitude all of which AI can present, but not participate in. Given that this review focuses only on a conceptual level, future research sho

latest.title: Price sensitivity and impulsive consumption in all-you-can-eat buffets: a moderated mediation perspective
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines the association between price sensitivity and impulsive consumption intention in all-you-can-eat buffet dining. Using Prospect Theory as the overall theoretical perspective and drawing on mental accounting and compensatory-consumption reasoning, it proposes a moderated mediation model involving Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), Psychological Ownership (PO), and Health Consciousness (HC). Methods A cross-sectional survey of 485 adults in China was used to test the model. FoMO and PO were specified as mediators, and HC was examined as a moderator of the associations between price sensitivity and FoMO, PO, and impulsive consumption intention. Results Price sensitivity was positively associated with impulsive consumption intention. The indirect association through PO was significant, whereas the indirect association through FoMO alone was not. The serial indirect path from price sensitivity through FoMO and PO to impulsive consumption intention was significant. The interactions between price sensitivity and HC were negative in the impulsive consumption intention, FoMO, and PO equations, indicating weaker associations with price sensitivity at higher levels of HC. Discussion The findings identify PO as the most proximal psychological correlate of impulsive consumption intention in the proposed model and highlight HC as a boundary condition for the associations involving price sensitivity. The study offers practical recommendations for buffet restaurants seeking to reduce potential over-selection and food waste, including smaller initial portions, convenient refills, messages discouraging quantity-based value maximization, and health-oriented dining guidance. Future longitudinal and experimental research can examine the temporal and causal relations

latest.title: Emerging Trends in Entrepreneurship, Skill Development and Startups: A Research Synthesis
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
latest.abstract: The transformative role of artificial intelligence in entrepreneurial processes, the transition from knowledge transfer to capability-based skill development, and the increasing recognition of psychological and community competencies alongside technical skills are the three main trends that emerge from this paper's synthesis of recent research on entrepreneurship, skill development, and startup ecosystems. According to the report, integrated approaches that combine formal education, experiential learning, and AI-driven strategies are becoming increasingly important for company success. By combining disparate studies and providing a framework for comprehending these tendencies, this paper adds to the body of literature.

latest.title: Consensus without conversion: local economy support orientation and the sustainable development goals across three tourism stakeholder groups in Uzbekistan
latest.abstract: Preference for locally produced goods is widely proposed as a behavioural lever for retaining tourism revenue in host economies, yet the international evidence describes sharp divergence between stakeholder groups. We tested whether that divergence appears in an emerging Silk Road destination by administering three parallel instruments to residents (n = 658), tourists (n = 565) and tourism industry actors (n = 370) in Bukhara, Uzbekistan (N = 1,593). Because consumer and tourism ethnocentrism describe home-economy support by residents and domestic actors, but not international visitors’ preference for host-country products, we compared the groups on a role-independent construct, local economy support orientation. Across semantically matched items, the three groups were statistically equivalent in their preference for local over imported products, their belief in local economic benefit, and a composite orientation index (all two one-sided tests p < 0.002 within a margin of 0.20 scale points), despite 95.6% power to detect a small effect. Divergence occurred instead within groups, as an attitude-behaviour gap between normative endorsement and self-reported enacted commitment: residents’ cultural pride exceeded their economic participation (d _ z = 0.51), tourists’ local-support intention exceeded their willingness to pay a premium (d _ z = 0.17), and suppliers’ advocacy for the Sustainable Development Goals exceeded their literacy in them (d _ z = 0.30). The residents’ gap widened monotonically as occupational access to the tourism value chain declined, and infrastructure readiness predicted tourists’ willingness to pay was more strongly than any identity-related variable. Attitudinal consensus is therefore not the binding constraint on locally anchored sustainable develo

latest.title: From Replacement to Augmentation: A Human-Centered Framework for Consumer Robots
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence and related hardware and software technologies have accelerated the development of consumer robots, creating new opportunities for robots to support people in everyday life. However, advanced technology is only the foundation for achieving this goal. A complete design concept for robots aimed at ordinary consumers is also needed. This paper examines the importance of positioning consumer robots as tools for human augmentation, the reason why consumer robot interaction design should mainly use intuitive operation, and the safety issues that influence user trust and acceptance. The analysis argues that consumer robots should prioritize human augmentation rather than complete robot autonomy. This approach protects consumer control while giving users stronger capabilities. In addition, robot products can only be psychologically accepted when consumers trust them. To achieve this positioning, intuitive interaction can reduce the barriers for ordinary consumers and allow more natural interaction. Products should also provide data privacy protection, control-right protection, and safety that can be perceived by users. The significance of this paper is that it provides a consumer-centered design framework for robots aimed at ordinary consumers.

latest.title: AI-Driven Digital Marketing and Purchase Intention: An Empirical Study of Generation Z Consumers in Kerala
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Subash. K and Dr. Kalapati Madhavi
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing by enabling personalised advertisements, AI-powered product recommendations, chatbots and AI-generated promotional content. Generation Z consumers are active users of digital platforms and are frequently exposed to technology-enabled marketing practices. Their perceptions of these practices may influence their trust in online promotions, attitudes towards advertised products and purchase intentions. This study aims to examine the relationship between consumer perceptions of AI-driven digital marketing and purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in Kerala. It focuses on consumers’ perceptions of personalised advertising, product recommendations, chatbot interactions, AI-generated promotional content and the credibility of AI-driven marketing.

latest.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Programming Interfaces for Social CRM Automation: A TOE-Based Conceptual Framework
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and application programming interfaces (APIs) can connect customer messages with organisational records, but technical availability alone does not explain adoption or sustained use. This paper develops a conceptual framework for AI- and API-enabled social customer relationship management (SCRM) automation in business-to-business small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). A purposive synthesis of 17 publications dated 2022–2026 combines recent work on the Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE) framework, SCRM, SME adoption, API integration, and responsible AI. The analysis distinguishes AI interpretation, API connectivity, and organisational authorisation within a customer enquiry workflow. Five propositions explain how integration readiness, workflow ownership, external access and support, task-sensitive review, and recoverability may influence introduction and continuity. The theoretical contribution specifies where established TOE conditions operate when an inferred customer requirement becomes a shared organisational action. Jordanian industrial SMEs provide the intended context for examination, informed by recent local adoption studies. An illustrative workflow links the framework to observable practices without claiming implementation results. The paper offers a basis for qualitative examination and responsible digital innovation; its propositions remain unvalidated.

latest.title: The Influence of Food Discounts, Free Shipping, and Consumer Preferences on ShopeeFood and GrabFood Selection
latest.venue: Edunity Kajian Ilmu Sosial dan Pendidikan
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of online food delivery in Indonesia has intensified competition between ShopeeFood and GrabFood, which rely heavily on food discounts and free-delivery promotions. This study examines how food discounts, free-delivery promotions, and consumer preferences influence the selection of these two platforms and compares the strength of each effect between them. A quantitative survey was conducted with 220 respondents, mostly in Jabodetabek, who were recruited through non-probability sampling and completed an online questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met the criteria for convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability. All six hypothesized paths were positive and significant. Consumer preference had the strongest effect on the selection of ShopeeFood (b = 0.421) and GrabFood (b = 0.340). Free delivery had a larger effect than food discounts on ShopeeFood (b = 0.240 vs. 0.186), whereas on GrabFood the two promotions had comparable effects (b = 0.205 vs. 0.213). The models explained 44.7% and 35.0% of the variance in platform selection. Platforms should therefore combine promotional incentives with strategies that reinforce users' existing preferences.

latest.title: A Comparative Study on the Impact Mechanism of AI-Generated Virtual Influencers and Real Influencers on Brand Communication
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally changing the sphere of marketing communications, with virtual influencers (VIs) created with the help of AI being one of such significant changes. The paper aims at making a comparative analysis of the effects that virtual and real human influencers (HIS) create on brand communication focusing on the variables of authenticity, trust and purchase intention. Mixed-method research design was used and included both the qualitative interviews and focus groups and the quantitative surveys in order to examine the perception and responses of consumers to both types of influences comprehensively. There are results showing that human influencers have perceived superiority when it comes to authenticity and connection to emotions, but the virtual influencers have greater brand control and cross cultural appeal. Inferring deeper decoding, authenticity and credibility have been determined as the major mediating factors which influence brand attitude. These findings add value to the theoretical discussion on influencer marketing and provide strategies on the strategic level of brand selection and use of influencers. The paper stresses on the dynamism of human and algorithmic beings in marketing and suggests a reformulated approach to appreciating trust and authenticity in an AI-dominated environment.

latest.title: A double-edged sword: digitalization and nighttime activity in Chinese listed firms
latest.abstract: Extant research on enterprise digitalization has focused predominantly on performance enhancement and technological transformation while paying relatively limited attention to its implications for overtime work. By reference to nighttime satellite light data and a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies, this study examines the impact of enterprise digitalization on nighttime firm activity and the underlying mechanisms and further investigates whether overtime work is accompanied by income compensation. The results reveal that digitalization increases nighttime firm activity through two main channels: market expansion and R&D activities. In addition, digitalization increases the total revenue and average employee wages of firms, thus suggesting the existence of an income compensation effect that is associated with overtime work. Furthermore, we reveal that more positive organizational attitudes toward digitalization can effectively mitigate the increase in nighttime firm activity associated with digitalization. These findings provide new evidence concerning the labor implications of digital transformation in the context of Chinese listed companies. This study highlights the importance of improving the operational efficiency of digitalization while simultaneously protecting employees’ rights and interests, thereby promoting sustainable synergy between organizations and their workforces during the process of digital transformation in China.

latest.title: The Influence of User generated Content and Price Perception on Shopee Marketplace Users' Purchase Decisions in Cengkareng District, West Jakarta
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce in Indonesia has changed consumer behavior in online shopping. User-Generated Content and price perception are considered important factors influencing consumers' purchase decisions on the Shopee marketplace. This study aims to examine the influence of User-Generated Content and price perception on the purchase decisions of Shopee marketplace users in Cengkareng District, West Jakarta. This study employed a quantitative research method, with data collected through questionnaires. The study involved 100 respondents selected using a purposive sampling technique. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The results indicate that User-Generated Content has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Price perception also has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Furthermore, both variables simultaneously have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.736 (73.6%), indicating that purchase decisions can be explained by User-Generated Content and price perception, while the remaining 26.4% is explained by other factors outside the scope of this study. These findings suggest that User-Generated Content and price perception play important roles in influencing consumers' purchase decisions on the Shopee marketplace.

latest.title: The Bright and Dark Sides of CEO Personality in Corporate Sustainability: A Critical Review
latest.abstract: Following PRISMA, we review 47 studies on CEO traits and sustainability using the Dark Triad, Positive Self‐regard, and institutional isomorphism frameworks. Narcissism is associated with CSR engagement and greenwashing; hubris with conditional green innovation; and overconfidence with mixed CSR outcomes and greater decoupling. Machiavellianism is linked to manipulation risks, while psychopathy is negatively associated with sustainability orientation. Core self‐evaluation and related attributes generally support stakeholder‐oriented engagement. Coercive, normative, and mimetic isomorphism help explain these relationships under different governance and financial conditions. The review distinguishes substantive engagement from symbolic compliance and identifies research priorities concerning endogeneity, personality measurement, and cross‐country differences.

latest.title: How AI-powered chatbot empathy drives online repurchase intention: the mediating role of service trust
latest.venue: Denarius Revista de economía y adminstración
latest.abstract: AI chatbots are performing an increasing amount of emotional labor for online retailers. However, it is still unclear if the engineered empathetic nature of these AI chatbots can lead to increased repeat purchasing behavior and how they do so. This paper uses the stimulus-organism-response model to conceptualize AI chatbot emotional support as a stimulus, service trust as an organismic state (or internal experience), and repurchase intentions online as a response to those stimuli. Additionally, we examine the role that digital anxiety may play as a boundary condition. Using survey data from 447 Iraqi consumers who have purchased items online, we used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLSSEM) to analyze our results. The results show that AI chatbot emotional support was significantly related to service trust, which in turn was significantly related to repurchase intentions. Furthermore, trust completely mediated the positive relationship between the two variables, such that all of the effects of chatbot emotional support on repurchase intentions were carried by trust. Contrary to expectations, digital anxiety did not moderate the relationship between chatbot emotional support and trust or conditionally affect the mediation of trust; thus, the process of generating trust occurs at similar rates regardless of level of digital anxiety. Overall, the findings suggest that trust is the primary pathway by which machine-generated empathy leads to customer loyalty and also demonstrate that there are no contingency conditions associated with stimulus-organism-response theory within a developing e-commerce environment.

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation , each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs: An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other.
