Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency with organizational agility as a moderator
hot.abstract: The study focuses on understanding the moderation effect of organizational agility in the impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency in organizations intending to excel in the digital era. This study examines the association between digital HRM systems, digital transformation, and HR efficiency, considering the moderating role of organizational agility. Based on the study model, the authors proposed five hypotheses to be tested in this study. They adapted the study instrument based on quantitative descriptive approach and distributed 500 questioners to collect 385 responses. The study’s findings reveal that both digital HRM systems and digital transformation impact HR efficiency. The significant findings were that digital HRM systems (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and digital transformation (β = 0.194, p = 0.006) have a positive and significant impact on HR efficiency. In addition, organizational agility serves as a moderator in the relationship between digital HRM systems and HR efficiency (β = 0.154, p = 0.025) but has no effect on the relationship with digital transformation (β = − 0.075, p = 0.248). This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating the role of digital HRM systems and digital transformation as key organizational resources that enhance HR efficiency. It also highlights how organizational agility and digital capabilities serve as dynamic resources, contributing to an organization’s adaptability and sustained competitive advantage. The future research directions and limitations are presented at the end.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: The Role of Digital Tourism Platforms in Advancing Sustainable Development Goals in the Industry 4.0 Era
hot.abstract: The intersection of digitalization and sustainability is reshaping the tourism industry, with digital platforms playing a transformative role in optimizing travel experiences while simultaneously influencing economic inclusivity, labor dynamics, and environmental responsibility. This paper explores how Industry 4.0 technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), big data, blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT)—are integrated into digital tourism platforms, assessing their dual impact on sustainability and market structures. The study develops a conceptual framework around five key dimensions: market power and digital dependency, AI-driven automation and workforce transformation, innovation and digital inclusion, sustainability innovations, and data security and governance. While digital platforms enhance personalization, operational efficiency, and eco-conscious travel, they also reinforce economic disparities, monopolization, and regulatory challenges, raising concerns related to SDGs such as SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption, and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The study highlights the need for equitable governance frameworks to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven monopolization, algorithmic bias, and data privacy violations while ensuring digital accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on platform economics, digital governance, and sustainable tourism transformation, offering policy and managerial implications for fostering an inclusive and envi

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). hot.title: Cognitive offloading or cognitive overload? How AI alters the mental architecture of coping
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being a specialized technological tool to an intimate presence in everyday life. Smart assistants organize our schedules, predictive systems anticipate our needs, and therapeutic chatbots promise to listen when no human is available (Zhang & Wang, 2024). The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. hot.title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
hot.abstract: This study examines how different stakeholders perceive influencer authenticity, revealing the misalignments that arise when each group prioritizes different aspects of authenticity. In doing so, the authors generate new theory on influencer marketing and provide managerial insights for brands and agencies to collaborate effectively with influencers to resolve these misalignments and ultimately build and sustain influencer authenticity. Using exploratory, in-depth interviews with consumers, influencers, brand managers, and influencer marketing agencies, the study triangulates stakeholder perspectives on influencer authenticity. Specifically, it examines the misalignment among these groups through the lens of assemblage theory and explores how these misalignments may be resolved to produce successful and lasting influencer assemblages. Finally, it explores how influencer marketing agencies can help manage authenticity misalignments.

latest.title: Pengaruh Product Variation dan Influencer Marketing serta Customer Review terhadap Purchase Intention produk Make Over di Kota Samarinda
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive nature of the cosmetics industry compels companies to understand the factors that influence consumer purchase intentions. This study aims to analyze the impact of product variation, influencer marketing, and customer reviews on the purchase intention for Make Over products in the city of Samarinda. A quantitative approach was employed, with data collected via questionnaires distributed to 119 respondents selected through purposive sampling. The respondents were women aged 17 or older, residing in Samarinda, and familiar with Make Over products. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the aid of SPSS version 27. The results indicate that product variation, influencer marketing, and customer reviews each have a positive and significant partial effect on purchase intention. Furthermore, these three variables collectively exert a significant influence on the purchase intention for Make Over products in Samarinda. Consequently, product variety, influencer-based marketing strategies, and customer reviews are key factors that should be prioritized to enhance consumer purchase intention toward Make Over products.

latest.title: AI-Enabled Robust Performance-Based Budgeting: A Hybrid Neural–Optimization Approach for Smart Governance
latest.abstract: Performance-based budgeting (PBB) remains one of the most critical challenges in modern public expenditure management, particularly as governments transition toward data-driven and intelligent governance systems. Advances in artificial intelligence now allow budgeting processes to move beyond subjective estimates and toward analytical, transparent, and evidence-based decision-making. This study introduces an AI-enabled hybrid framework for PBB that integrates Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) with robust linear optimization to support smart governance and resilient resource allocation. The ANN component learns complex cost–activity relationships from historical organizational data and generates predictive estimates for future costs and cost drivers, which are among the primary sources of uncertainty in budgeting. These ANN-derived uncertainty intervals are then incorporated into a robust optimization model following Soyster and Bertsimas–Sim formulations to ensure both feasibility and optimality under uncertain conditions. The proposed hybrid model provides a transparent and intelligence-driven mechanism for allocating resources in alignment with organizational goals. The framework is validated within a major Iranian bank. Empirical results demonstrate that integrating ANN-based cost estimation with robust optimization significantly improves budget deviation indicators and enhances the accuracy, stability, and resilience of the budgeting process. The study contributes to the evolving field of smart governance by presenting a mathematically rigorous, AI-enhanced, and uncertainty-aware budgeting methodology.

latest.title: Constructing professional chef identity through talent, creativity, and popularity: Insights from professional chefs
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Theory and Research
latest.abstract: Culinary literature often treats talent, creativity, and popularity separately, despite their growing importance in contemporary gastronomy. This study examines how professional chefs integrate these dimensions in constructing their professional identities. Using a generic qualitative inquiry approach, the study conducted semi-structured interviews with 15 professional chefs and mapped their perspectives through combined deductive and inductive qualitative content analysis. The findings show that chef identity is continuously constructed through three interdependent dimensions. Talent provides the technical foundation, creativity enables aesthetic differentiation, and popularity fosters social validation and peer recognition. The study offers an empirically grounded, descriptive framework that addresses this fragmentation. It shows how chefs navigate tensions among kitchen operations, artistic expression, and public visibility, and how they translate technical craft and creative ideas into recognized social capital in a competitive, media-driven environment.

latest.title: Internalization of ESQ Values in Building Entrepreneurial Character and Work Ethic: A Study on Sasirangan MSME Entrepreneurs in South Kalimantan
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the internalization of Emotional Spiritual Quotient (ESQ) values in building entrepreneurial character and work ethic among Sasirangan MSME entrepreneurs in South Kalimantan. The study is based on the assumption that entrepreneurial success is not only determined by technical and managerial competencies, but also by emotional intelligence, spiritual awareness, and cultural values that shape business behavior. The internalization of ESQ values is considered essential in strengthening entrepreneurial resilience, integrity, discipline, creativity, and ethical work orientation among local entrepreneurs engaged in the Sasirangan industry as a cultural-based creative economy sector. This research employs a qualitative approach using the Library Research method. Data were collected from scientific journals, books, theses, dissertations, and academic documents related to ESQ, Islamic entrepreneurship, work ethic, Banjar culture, and the development of Sasirangan MSMEs. The collected data were analyzed through content analysis to identify conceptual patterns and relationships between emotional intelligence, spiritual intelligence, entrepreneurial character, and work ethic. The findings reveal that the internalization of ESQ values significantly contributes to the formation of entrepreneurial character through honesty, responsibility, discipline, emotional control, creativity, and social awareness. Furthermore, spiritual intelligence strengthens the Islamic work ethic by encouraging entrepreneurs to perceive work as a form of worship, thereby increasing motivation, perseverance, and professional integrity. Banjar cultural values such as kayuh baimbai also reinforce cooperation, solidarity, and collective responsibility among Sasirangan entrepreneurs. Th

latest.title: Analisis Peran On-Time Performance, Ketersediaan Sarana Krl, Dan Tingkat Keamanan Penumpang Untuk Meningkatkan Kepuasan Pelanggan Serta Dampaknya Pada Minat Menggunakan Kembali Commuter Line Jabodetabek
latest.abstract: The increasing use of the Jabodetabek Commuter Line has driven the need to improve public transportation service quality. This study aims to analyze the effects of On-Time Performance, facility availability, and passenger safety levels on customer satisfaction and intention to reuse, as well as to examine the mediating role of customer satisfaction. A quantitative approach was applied involving 400 Jabodetabek Commuter Line users selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that facility availability has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction (β = 0.654; p < 0.001), while On-Time Performance and passenger safety levels do not have significant effects. On-Time Performance, passenger safety levels, and customer satisfaction have positive and significant effects on intention to reuse, whereas facility availability has no direct effect. Customer satisfaction mediates the relationship between facility availability and passenger safety levels with intention to reuse, but does not mediate the effect of On-Time Performance. The findings indicate that service improvement strategies should consider the characteristics of each service attribute to enhance customer satisfaction and encourage continued service usage.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kepercayaan dan Kepuasan Pelanggan terhadap Loyalitas Pelanggan
latest.abstract: Intensifying business competition requires every company to maintain its customers through the development of strong customer loyalty. This research aims to analyze the influence of customer trust and customer satisfaction on customer loyalty. The study employs a quantitative approach with a descriptive and verificative research design. The research sample comprises 150 respondents selected using non-probability sampling with purposive sampling method. Data analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics software. The findings demonstrate that customer trust and customer satisfaction, both individually and simultaneously, have a positive and significant influence on customer loyalty. The coefficient of determination indicates that 68.9% of the variation in customer loyalty can be explained by customer trust and satisfaction, while the remaining portion is influenced by other variables not examined in this study. The research implications affirm that strengthening customer trust and enhancing customer satisfaction constitute fundamental strategies for building sustainable customer loyalty.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Marketing dan Brand Reputation terhadap Keputusan Pembelian
latest.abstract: Growing consumer awareness of environmental issues has prompted companies to implement green marketing strategies to meet sustainable needs while building positive brand reputation. This study examines the influence of green marketing and brand reputation on consumer purchase decisions. Using a quantitative approach with descriptive-verificative design, the research involved 150 respondents through purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Results demonstrate that green marketing and brand reputation have positive and significant effects on purchase decisions, both individually and simultaneously. The coefficient of determination of 72.4% indicates that both independent variables explain the variance in purchase decisions, while 27.6% is influenced by other factors. The findings confirm that combining environmentally friendly marketing strategies with credible brand reputation serves as an effective driver of consumer purchase decisions in an increasingly environmentally conscious market.

latest.title: Pengaruh E-Recruitment, Employee Branding, dan Kompensasi terhadap Intention to Apply for a Job
latest.abstract: Competition for qualified employees encourages companies to implement effective recruitment strategies through digital technology, corporate image development, and competitive compensation. This study aims to analyze the effects of e-recruitment, employee branding, and compensation on intention to apply for a job. A quantitative approach with a descriptive and verificative design was employed. The sample consisted of 250 respondents selected using a non-probability sampling technique with a purposive sampling method. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that e-recruitment, employee branding, and compensation have positive and significant effects on job application intention, both partially and simultaneously. The coefficient of determination of 78.6% indicates that the three variables explain the variation in job application intention, while the remaining 21.4% is influenced by other factors. These findings suggest that efficient digital recruitment systems, a positive corporate image, and fair, competitive compensation play important roles in increasing a company's attractiveness to prospective employees.

latest.title: Klasterisasi Karakteristik Pengguna E-Commerce Berdasarkan Profil Pengguna Menggunakan Algoritma K-Prototypes
latest.abstract: Accurate customer segmentation supports more personalized e-commerce marketing. However, the Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) model focuses on transaction history and may not fully capture shopping motivation or the share of a consumer’s spending allocated to e-commerce (Share of Wallet/SoW). This study aims to cluster e-commerce users based on transaction profiles and consumer behavior using the K-Prototypes algorithm. Data were collected from 198 e-commerce users in Palembang, Indonesia. The clustering variables included RFM, SoW, shopping motivation, and product-category preferences, while age category was used for follow-up analysis. The Elbow Method and Silhouette Score supported a four-cluster solution. The resulting personas were High-Value Promo Hunters, Routine Pragmatic Shoppers, Passive Micro-Spenders, and Urgent Big-Ticket Buyers. The Chi-square test indicated a significant association between age category and persona, with Cramér’s V of 0.274. This suggests that age is associated with shopping patterns but does not fully determine consumer profiles. The findings can inform more targeted promotions and user-experience design. The study is limited to 198 respondents from Palembang, so the findings may not represent e-commerce users in other regions.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Innovation Terhadap Purchase Intention Melalui Environmental Awareness dan Green Brand Image Pada Konsumen Muda Kopi Janji Jiwa di Samarinda
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Green Innovation on Purchase Intention through Environmental Awareness and Green Brand Image among young Kopi Janji Jiwa consumers in Samarinda. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework. Data were collected through questionnaires from 360 respondents aged 17–30 who had purchased Kopi Janji Jiwa at an outlet in Samarinda within the previous six months. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The study's novelty lies in examining Environmental Awareness and Green Brand Image as parallel mediators in a single model. The results indicate that Green Innovation positively and significantly affects Environmental Awareness, Green Brand Image, and Purchase Intention. Both mediators also positively and significantly affect Purchase Intention and mediate the relationship between Green Innovation and Purchase Intention. The indirect effect through Green Brand Image is greater than that through Environmental Awareness. These findings suggest that Kopi Janji Jiwa should strengthen environmentally friendly innovations and communicate sustainability practices transparently to build a credible green brand image and support purchase intention among young consumers.

latest.title: Pengaruh Personalisasi Rekomendasi Produk Terhadap Perilaku Pembelian Konsumen Dengan Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase Behavior, and the mediating role of Trust among Shopee users based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling, resulting in 111 eligible respondents, comprising 72.07% male and 27.93% female respondents aged 14–69 years. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results indicate that Product Recommendation Personalization has a positive and significant effect on Trust (β = 0.696; p < 0.001). Trust also has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Behavior (β = 0.719; p < 0.001). The indirect effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Purchase Behavior through Trust is also significant (β = 0.501; p < 0.001), confirming the mediating role of Trust. These findings support the S-O-R mechanism and highlight the importance of recommendation relevance and user trust in supporting online purchasing behavior.

latest.title: Pengaruh Ulasan Pelanggan Online dan Persepsi Harga terhadap Niat Beli Konsumen Sudut Kedai di Metland Transyogi
latest.abstract: A sharp increase in menu prices at Sudut Kedai, coupled with shifting customer engagement online, raises a fundamental question: do online reviews and price perception actually influence purchase intention? This study examines both factors among Sudut Kedai consumers in Metland Transyogi. Questionnaires were distributed to 120 respondents who had read online reviews of Sudut Kedai, selected through convenience sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Online customer reviews demonstrate a positive and significant effect on purchase intention (path coefficient 0.245; T-statistic 3.271; p 0.001), as does price perception (path coefficient 0.373; T-statistic 4.861; p 0.000), with an R-Square of 0.220. Credible and informative reviews build buyer trust; prices perceived as proportional to quality enhance purchase intention. Sudut Kedai needs to actively manage customer reviews and maintain fair pricing to strengthen purchase intention amid an increasingly competitive culinary market.

latest.title: Determinasi Brand Evangelism Hasil Personalisasi, Influencer–Brand Fit, Dan Perceived Authenticity Melalui Consumer Trust
latest.abstract: The emergence of social media as a marketing tool has transformed consumer behavior toward brands. This study aims to analyze the effects of personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity on brand evangelism, with consumer trust as a mediating variable. This study employs a quantitative approach through a survey of 268 social media users selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the SmartPLS software. The results show that personalization level, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust have a positive effect on brand evangelism. In addition, personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity have a positive effect on consumer trust. However, influencer–brand fit does not have a significant direct effect on brand evangelism. These findings underscore the importance of personalization, authenticity, and consumer trust in driving brand evangelism on social media.

latest.title: Faktor Penentu Keputusan Investasi Generasi Z Di Pontianak
latest.abstract: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City. The researchers distributed questionnaires to 154 respondents aged 17–29 who lived in Pontianak, had personal income, and had invested, or were currently investing, in the capital market. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS, and the measurement model met the criteria for validity and reliability. The results show that both financial literacy and media exposure have a positive and significant relationship with investment decisions, although the effect sizes are small. Because the survey was conducted at a single point in time, these findings indicate association and do not establish causation. Organizers of investment education programs for young people are advised to develop participants’ financial skills while also paying attention to their media habits.

latest.title: Peran Self-Control Dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Lifestyle dan User Experience Terhadap Impulsive Buying Pada Generasi Z Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee is influenced by lifestyle and user experience; however, previous findings are inconsistent, and the role of self-control as a moderator has not been tested together with both factors. This study aims to analyze the role of self-control in moderating the effects of lifestyle and user experience on impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee. The study employs an associative-causal quantitative approach with purposive sampling of 100 active Generation Z Shopee users. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by ANOVA (F-test) to examine the simultaneous effects. The results show that lifestyle and user experience have positive and significant effects on impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously together with self-control and its two interactions (F = 12.325; p < 0.001). Self-control has a negative and significant effect and negatively and significantly moderates the effects of lifestyle and user experience, thereby weakening both relationships. The novelty of this study lies in its integrated model, which simultaneously examines lifestyle and user experience with self-control as a moderator. The better Generation Z's self-control, the lower the tendency toward impulsive buying, even when influenced by lifestyle and an engaging online shopping experience. These findings are expected to provide insights for consumers and e-commerce platform managers in understanding and managing purchasing behavior.

latest.title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
latest.abstract: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

latest.title: The 7P Marketing Mix and Repurchase Intention in Online Footwear Shopping: The Effect of Utilitarian and Hedonic Value
latest.abstract: Encouraging customers to buy again remains a challenge for footwear brands in e-commerce. This study examines how the 7P marketing mix elements relate to utilitarian and hedonic value and how these values relate to repurchase intention. Guided by the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, survey data from 247 female consumers of Malcca who purchased through Shopee or TikTok Shop were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Product, price, and physical evidence were positively associated with utilitarian value, whereas product, promotion, people, and physical evidence were positively associated with hedonic value. Place and process showed no significant relationships with either value dimension. Both values positively influenced repurchase intention, with a larger estimated coefficient for utilitarian value. Significant indirect relationships were identified for product, price, and physical evidence through utilitarian value, and for people and physical evidence through hedonic value. Physical evidence was the only marketing mix element with significant indirect relationships through both value dimensions. These findings suggest that footwear brands should prioritize price–quality alignment, accurate product information, and effective visual presentation to strengthen functional and experiential value. The study extends the S-O-R framework by illustrating distinct value pathways associated with repurchase intention.

latest.title: Pemetaan Sosial Potensid Strategi Pengembangan UMKM Pemuda dalam Mendukung Kemandirian Ekonomi Masyarakat di Gampong Lapang, Kecamatan Johan Pahlawan, Kabupaten Aceh Barat
latest.abstract: This study aims to identify the conditions and potential of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), youth involvement, business challenges, and development strategies to support community economic independence in Gampong Lapang, Johan Pahlawan District, West Aceh Regency. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach using direct observation, interviews, and documentation. The informants consisted of the village head, a cosmetics shop owner, a coffee shop employee, and a daily necessities shop owner. The findings indicate that MSME activities in Gampong Lapang are relatively diverse, including cosmetics shops, coffee shops, daily necessities stores, and traditional snack businesses. However, youth involvement as business owners remains limited. Development opportunities include social media marketing, employment opportunities, and cooperation through local product consignment systems. The challenges include unstable consumer purchasing power, inventory management, limited business facilities, and unequal access to training and assistance. This study concludes that MSME development requires greater youth involvement, stronger digital marketing, cooperation among business actors, and continuous assistance to strengthen community economic independence.

latest.title: Content and contextual drivers of engagement in tourism and hospitality brand communities
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of internal and external antecedents on consumer engagement within social media brand communities in the tourism and hospitality sector. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a data set of Facebook (FB) brand posts from 12 airline brands over a six-month period, this study uses a two-phase mixed-methods approach comprising qualitative content analysis and multiple regression modeling. Post content was classified through message orientation and media richness, and engagement was measured through likes, comments and shares. Findings Engagement behavior was found to be significantly influenced by message orientation and media richness. Task- and self-oriented messages generated higher levels of commenting and liking, while low-rich content (image-based posts) yielded the strongest overall engagement. Firm size was shown to enhance interactive behaviors, whereas seasonality affected commenting behavior only. Furthermore, culture influenced overall engagement and moderated the relationship between post content and engagement behaviors. Finally, an interaction effect between post content and media richness was observed. Practical implications Tourism and hospitality marketers should tailor their content strategies by aligning the message orientation with audience needs, optimizing media richness for cognitive ease and maintaining consistent but context-sensitive posting. Cultural and seasonal nuances must be accounted for when designing content to maximize user engagement. Originality/value This study offers a theoretically integrated and empirically grounded model of consumer engagement in tourism-related social media communities. latest.title: Positive Outcomes of Corporate Social Responsibility for Companies and Society
latest.venue: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
latest.abstract: To explore the complicated field of corporate social responsibility (CSR), this study performs a thorough narrative review of the literature. It achieves this by clarifying the benefits that CSR could bring to society as well as to companies. According to the study, corporate social responsibility (CSR) goes beyond philanthropy and serves as an imperative strategy that improves a company's competitive advantage, reputation, and brand image. The study highlights the several benefits companies may achieve, such as enhanced staff morale, reduced risk, increased market share, and sustained financial prosperity. The article also explores the social impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR), presenting it as a driving force behind improving living standards, advancing equity, and aiding in protecting the environment. The study acknowledges that the CSR concept has flaws despite its many advantages. It highlights the significance of a conscious choice in interacting with social responsibility concerns and suggests a full review of both advantages and limitations. The study presents itself as a review of the complications surrounding corporate social responsibility (CSR), recognizing criticisms such as worries about misleading practices and the difficulties in measuring societal impact.

latest.title: Electronic word of mouth, tourist mobility networks, and attraction node position: evidence from 2019 Ctrip reviews and online travel blog networks in China
latest.abstract: Online reviews are central to tourism decision making, yet research has rarely examined whether review text is associated with the structural position of attractions in tourist mobility networks. This study matches 2019 Ctrip attraction reviews with a seasonal scenic-spot mobility network in China derived from online travel blogs. After cleaning and attraction-season aggregation, the baseline sample contains 786 attraction-by-season observations. The analysis estimates how pure-text sentiment, review volume, attribute diversity, and negative service evaluation relate to three centrality indicators: in-strength, PageRank, and betweenness. Pure-text sentiment is negatively associated with centrality, whereas review volume is positively associated with centrality across the baseline models. Negative service evaluation is generally negatively related to node position, although its stability is weaker for betweenness. Interaction models show that review volume strengthens the negative marginal association between sentiment and centrality. Seasonal analyses indicate that the negative sentiment effect is concentrated in spring, while the positive role of review volume is strongest in summer and autumn. Type heterogeneity shows the clearest joint role of review volume, review length, and attribute diversity among ancient-architecture attractions. The paper extends eWOM research from conventional performance outcomes to attraction position in mobility networks. It shows that evaluative valence and engagement volume carry distinct and partly opposing implications for network position, and that these relationships vary by season and attraction type.

latest.title: Modeling the influence of sensory overload on visitor conservation at urban heritage destinations
latest.abstract: Historic urban centers attract visitors with dense sensory richness, yet that same richness may reduce the attention tourists need for small conservation acts such as putting litter in bins or keeping to protected boundaries. Existing sustainable-tourism research explains these acts mainly through attitudes, awareness and intentions, and rarely examines the tourist’s momentary cognitive state during the visit. This conceptual paper proposes the sensory–mindfulness–stewardship (SMS) model to address that gap. Drawing on recent research on embodied experience, mindfulness, restoration and crowding in tourism, it proposes that the auditory, visual and spatial atmosphere of a heritage site may influence a visitor’s momentary mindful state (a short-lived condition of calm, present-focused attention); that this state helps explain eco-preservation behavior (small on-site acts that protect the site) beyond attitudes and awareness; and that ‘restorative cognitive pathways’ (brief, designed recovery points along visitor routes) may buffer the effect of sensory overload. Crowding, cultural distance and time pressure are treated as conditions that may strengthen or weaken these effects. Six propositions are derived (P2 has two parts). We distinguish links that have partial empirical support from those that remain theoretical, set out candidate indicators, including physiological measures as complements to self-report and observation, and outline a staged validation design. The paper is theory-building and reports no new data. Because much of the supporting evidence comes from questionnaire studies in China, the propositions are offered for testing in other regions and with other methods.

latest.title: The Effect of Product Adaptation, International Marketing Capabilities, And Competitive Advantage on the Export Performance of Indonesian MSMEs
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: The development of international trade encourages Indonesian Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their competitiveness through effective marketing strategies. This study aims to analyze the influence of product adaptation, international marketing capabilities, and competitive advantage on the export performance of Indonesian MSMEs. The research employs a quantitative approach, utilizing a survey method through the distribution of questionnaires to 100 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression to examine the impact of each independent variable on export performance. Product adaptation reflects a firm's ability to tailor its products to the needs of international markets, while international marketing capabilities refer to the capacity to manage marketing strategies across national borders. Competitive advantage describes a firm's ability to create superior value compared to its competitors. This study is expected to provide empirical evidence regarding the factors influencing export performance and contribute to the development of international marketing strategies. The findings are intended to serve as a basis for formulating policies and business strategies aimed at expanding into global markets and enhancing the sustainability of export activities for Indonesian MSMEs.

latest.title: Toward sustainable agritourism: operational insights from organic farms engaged with tourism
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how integrating organic farming with agritourism can advance sustainable rural development. By examining organic farms engaged with tourism in South Korea through an ecotourism framework, it addresses the need to distinguish genuinely sustainable, ecologically grounded agritourism models from conventional, chemical-intensive practices. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a qualitative case study approach combining in-depth interviews with operators of three organic farms and a content analysis of 38 organic farm tourism websites in South Korea. The analysis evaluates farm operations, visitor programming and rural community dynamics against core ecotourism principles, contextualized with recent agritourism literature. Findings Organic agritourism aligns closely with ecotourism by integrating low-impact farming with hands-on environmental education, biodiversity conservation and cultural preservation. Key findings highlight that tourism revenue reinforces organic land stewardship, small-scale operations foster meaningful socio-cultural and educational exchanges and participatory community collaboration enhances rural resilience and local circular economies. Five operational takeaways are identified: ecological conservation, active learning, socio-cultural sustainability, value-based economic viability and inclusive community participation. Originality/value This paper demonstrates that ecotourism serves as an effective guiding paradigm for agritourism on small-scale organic enterprises. It provides actionable operational and policy insights for agritourism operators, planners and government agencies seeking to establish replicable, value-based agritourism models that support environmental integrity, rural vitality and ethical visitor

latest.title: From story to sale: how digital storytelling shapes AR consumers' impulse shopping intention
latest.abstract: Purpose Digital storytelling has emerged as a catalyst and game changer in the transformative marketing ecosystem through integrative efforts with augmented reality. This study addresses this gap by examining how digital storytelling enhances consumer immersion and enjoyment. It also examines the impact of immersion and enjoyment on consumers' impulse shopping intention. Design/methodology/approach 391 responses were collected from active augmented reality users who had experience with brand storytelling in augmented reality. The data were analysed using a combined importance–performance map analysis (cIPMA) in partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings demonstrate that the importance of four dimensions of augmented reality digital storytelling (narrative structure, perceived aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling) significantly influences immersion and enjoyment and leads to consumer impulse shopping intention. Furthermore, necessity logic complements sufficiency logic by demonstrating that perceived aesthetics constitutes a necessary condition for both enjoyment and immersion. Theming and storytelling impose a weak bottleneck constraint solely on immersion. Additionally, enjoyment and immersion are less restrictive in practice for impulsive purchase intention. This suggests that most respondents already meet the minimum requirements. Consequently, these antecedents function more as performance-enhancing factors than as critical bottlenecks requiring immediate managerial intervention. Originality/value This study pioneers research at the intersection of augmented reality marketing and digital storytelling by demonstrating how narrative, aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling elements can shape consum

latest.title: Micro-cultural activism in slow fashion: how influencers reframe sustainable consumption on Instagram
latest.venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines the activist roles of slow fashion influencers on Instagram, focusing on how they construct and circulate sustainability narratives and reframe sustainable consumption into daily achievable practices. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative research design, analysing both visual and textual materials from the Instagram posts of slow fashion influencers. Findings The findings reveal that slow fashion influencers operate as micro-cultural activists who perform as educators, advocates and facilitators of ethical consumer practices. By voicing their concerns about workers' rights, animal welfare and textile waste, influencers make complex sustainability issues accessible while encouraging reflection on daily practices such as second-hand shopping, upcycling and recycling. Through their digital narratives, these influencers frame sustainability as an individualized moral identity project, thereby linking their personal consumption choices to lifestyle-oriented ethical advocacy. Research limitations/implications This article contributes to the literature on influencer culture and digital activism by shifting the focus away from short-term behavioural metrics towards cultural meaning-making and demonstrating how influencers use Instagram as a dynamic space for cultural activism. Social implications This paper shows how slow fashion influencers use their digital presence to cultivate environmental, social and ethical awareness among their followers by presenting accessible alternatives to conventional mass consumption. Originality/value This research contributes to the influencer marketing literature by demonstrating how activist roles are enacted through social media and how influencers provide the symbolic tools that enable cons

latest.title: Building productivity in culinary MSMEs through market orientation: the mediating role of value co-creation on marketing performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the impact of responsive and proactive market orientation on the marketing performance of culinary micro, small and medium-sized culinary enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia, positioning marketing performance as a proxy for productivity. Specifically, it explores the mediating role of value co-creation, a mechanism that has received limited empirical attention in prior research. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative survey approach involving 319 respondents, comprising managers or owners of MSMEs. To evaluate the proposed hypotheses and examine both direct and indirect (mediating) relationships, the data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. All variables were measured using previously validated measurement scales. Findings Proactive market orientation (PMO) significantly enhances value co-creation but lacks a direct effect on marketing performance; its impact is fully mediated by co-creation. Responsive market orientation (RMO) directly improves performance, and this improvement is partially achieved through co-creation. The study confirms co-creation as a pivotal mechanism linking MO to outcomes, with PMO's influence being entirely indirect and RMO's hybrid (direct/indirect). Originality/value This study advances the literature by integrating responsive and proactive market orientation with value co-creation in the context of culinary MSMEs. It highlights value co-creation as a dynamic capability that enables SMEs to translate market insights into productivity gains despite resource constraints, offering both theoretical enrichment and practical guidance for enhancing competitiveness.

latest.title: The effect of green event on environmental loyalty: moderating role of organisers' green consciousness
latest.venue: IIMBG Journal of Sustainable Business and Innovation
latest.abstract: Purpose This study assesses how organisers’ green consciousness influences the effect of green events on environmental loyalty among event-organising firms in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a cross-sectional survey design, soliciting data from 300 managers/owners of event-organising firms. The data were analysed using the PROCESS MACRO in SPSS v. 23 to help estimate the conditional relationships under the study. Findings The findings show that while green events significantly influenced environmental loyalty, organisers’ green consciousness further strengthened their effectiveness in encouraging environmental loyalty. Furthermore, dimensions of green events, such as green prices and green internal practices, had significant positive effects on environmental loyalty. Finally, organisers green consciousness significantly moderated the links between green experience, price, promotion, internal practices and environmental loyalty. Research limitations/implications Firstly, the study focused on event-organising firms in Ghana, which may limit the generalisability of the findings to other industries or geographical contexts. Secondly, the study's cross-sectional design limits the ability to infer causality between variables. Practical implications Consequently, to ensure a strong environmental loyalty to achieve sustainable development, there is the need for policy makers and event organisations to encourage green practices and events, as well as promote green awareness among event organisers to strengthen their consciousness. Originality/value The novelty of this study lies in its contribution to the green event and environmental loyalty literature, potentially as one of the first to advance the value–belief–norm (VBN) theory in this context.

latest.title: Parental influence and university choice: a marketing mix perspective from private higher education in Bangladesh
latest.abstract: Purpose In cultures with strong familial values, parents play a crucial role in shaping students’ educational choices. In the higher education context, understanding the factors influencing students’ university selection is essential. This study aims to examine the impact of parental influence and the marketing mix on students’ decision-making when choosing private higher education institutions in Bangladesh. Although marketing mix theory, social cognitive career theory (SCCT) and cultural capital theory have each informed research on university choice separately, their combined application to explain gendered, family-mediated decision-making in a collectivist developing-country context remains largely unexamined. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in SCCT, cultural capital theory and the 7Ps marketing mix framework, this study adopts a quantitative approach using data from 298 students attending private higher education institutions in Bangladesh, analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with measurement invariance, multi-group analysis and effect-size (f2, Q2) assessment. Findings The findings identify parental influence as the key determinant in university choice, particularly for female students. Female students tend to rely more on family guidance when evaluating educational quality and tuition fees, whereas male students are more independent in assessing academic programmes and financial considerations. The results also indicate that the location of the university is the least significant factor affecting students’ choices. Research limitations/implications The findings highlight the importance of incorporating socio-cultural factors, particularly parental influence, when applying the marketing mix framework in collectivist

latest.title: Investigating the dynamics between sustainability reporting and social media. A field study
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyse the interactions between sustainability reporting and social media communication, with particular attention to the actors involved, decision-making processes and strategies adopted to ensure effectiveness, consistency and transparency in sustainability communication. Design/methodology/approach The study is based on a field study conducted in the Italian agri-food sector. Data were collected through 11 semi-structured interviews with managers responsible for sustainability reporting and/or corporate communication across nine Italian agri-food companies. The analysis is guided by an integrated theoretical framework combining communication theory and stakeholder theory. Findings Sustainability reports remain the central, validated repository of sustainability information, while social media are mainly used to amplify and adapt previously approved content. Stakeholder interactions on social media are monitored and managed but do not influence the content of sustainability reports. Sustainability managers act as gatekeepers of content validity and compliance, while social media managers translate information for platform-specific dissemination. Social implications The results highlight tensions among regulatory requirements, reputational risk and increasing expectations for transparency, raising questions about the actual dialogic potential of social media to foster accessible, inclusive sustainability communication. Originality/value The study contributes to the sustainability accounting and communication literature by providing empirical evidence of limited informational circularity between sustainability reporting and social media. It advances an integrated explanation that links communication noise, stakeholder legitimacy consideration

latest.title: The call for signaling of expertise on social media: the case of food influencers
latest.abstract: Purpose A tension exists between engagement-driven platform visibility and consumers’ need for credible dietary advice with direct health implications. This research aims to examine how expertise cues help consumers identify credible food influencer content and how qualified influencers can communicate expertise effectively in social media environments. Design/methodology/approach Across six studies, the authors combine secondary analysis of 397 Instagram recipe posts from 40 qualified and non-qualified food influencers with five experiments involving 1,977 participants: US adults recruited through MTurk (Ns = 231, 309 and 284) and US undergraduates (Ns = 601 and 552). The experiments manipulate source qualifications, message design, expertise-salience cues and measure individual differences in BMI and body-esteem, to examine effects on perceived expertise, health-related outcomes and social media engagement. Findings Consumers often do not distinguish clearly between qualified and non-qualified food influencers when expertise cues are absent. Secondary data analysis shows meaningful differences in the reliability of content produced by these sources. Across the studies, making expertise salient increases perceived expertise and improves both health-related and engagement outcomes. The authors further show that combining informational and motivational message elements strengthens the effect of qualifications on perceived expertise, and that body esteem shapes consumer responsiveness to expertise signals. Research limitations/implications The findings are based primarily on Instagram-related contexts and may not generalize fully to other platforms or audience groups. Future research should examine additional platforms and broader samples. Practical implications The findi

latest.title: High-tech vs. high-touch in hospitality: finding the balance of well-being for human assets
latest.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
latest.abstract: Purpose While the technology adoption literature focuses on customer outcomes and operational efficiency, the employee experience of navigating simultaneous high-tech and high-touch demands remains theoretically underdeveloped. To address this gap, this study aims to examine how the joint optimization of technical and social systems affects employee well-being, work quality of life and behavioral outcomes and propose critical questions, future research directions and theoretical and managerial implications. Design/methodology/approach Using socio-technical system theory as an analytical lens, this paper adopts a critical theory synthesis approach to examine the integration of high-tech and high-touch service delivery and its implications for employee well-being in the hospitality context. This study advances research by providing critical comparisons and considerations for well-being in a high-tech and high-touch environment. Findings The synthesis of the relevant literature suggests that technology should not be viewed merely as an external influence, but rather as an integral social component in the hospitality workforce. Technology is deeply intertwined with the industry’s high-touch service environment, making the balance between high-tech and high-touch a dynamic and continuously evolving relationship that subtly yet significantly shapes employee well-being. Research limitations/implications This study aims to spark critical thought and future research on the new nature of hospitality work being both high-tech and high-touch and how this expanded work demands affect already overworked hospitality employees. Originality/value This research outlines future research directions and actionable steps for practitioners to consider as they implement technology into human s

latest.title: Solving Instagram Marketing Problems with Benchmarking and AHP: A Case Study of PT Biotek Agro Indonesia
latest.abstract: Many companies use Instagram for marketing, but the results are often low because accounts are managed without clear priorities or reference to proven practices. This study shows how this marketing problem can be addressed by integrating benchmarking with the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), using PT Biotek Agro Indonesia, a liquid organic fertilizer producer in Bandung, as the case study. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first application of AHP-weighted benchmarking to the Instagram management of an organic fertilizer producer. AHP weighted five criteria and fifteen sub-criteria from 30 respondents, most of whom were aged 20–25 and students. Feeds ranked first (0.260), followed by Story (0.249), Reels (0.198), Profile (0.169), and Caption (0.124); Feeds and Story differ by only 0.011, and all aggregated consistency ratios were below 0.10, although most individual respondent matrices were above this limit. These weights were used to score three competitor accounts, so EM4 Indonesia became the benchmark partner for four criteria and Bio Cycle Indo for Story. The company account had an engagement rate of only 0.21%, and gaps appeared in 14 of 15 sub-criteria. These gaps became 14 performance targets and improvement designs approved by the company management. The approach helps companies set Instagram priorities in a measurable way, although the findings reflect the preferences of a young digital audience and the effect of the designs on engagement has not yet been measured.

latest.title: Mapping word-of-mouth drivers of investors’ financial behavior: a DEMATEL analysis from an Islamic financial marketing perspective
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, prioritize and map the causal interrelationships among word-of-mouth (WOM)-related factors shaping investors’ financial behavior from an Islamic financial marketing perspective. It examines how trust, social interaction, shared vision, family and friends, expert knowledge, risk-taking, past stock performance, financial advertising and investment experience jointly shape investors’ financial decisions. Design/methodology/approach A structured literature-based factor identification process and expert validation were used to identify the relevant WOM-related factors. The Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method was then applied to analyze their direct and indirect interrelationships. Judgments from 15 academic and financial-market experts were aggregated to classify the factors into cause and effect groups and construct a causal map. Findings Relational trust, investment experience, risk-taking and social interaction are the most prominent factors in the WOM network. Relational trust, social interaction, shared vision, past stock performance and expert knowledge operate as causal drivers, whereas financial advertising, risk-taking, family and friends and investment experience are mainly influenced by other factors. The results indicate that trust-based communication and credible knowledge sources are central to investors’ learning and risk-related decisions. Research limitations/implications The study relies on expert judgments and may therefore be affected by subjectivity and contextual bias. The Islamic financial marketing perspective is interpretive; specialist Islamic-finance expertise was not documented for the panel. Future research should validate the proposed causal paths with investor survey data, compar

latest.title: Picture, picture on the screen: a between-subjects experiment on AI-generated vs human images on Generation Z consumers’ impulse buying intention
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing strategies, particularly in the tourism industry, where AI-enhanced imagery is increasingly used to influence consumer behaviour. However, little research has examined how AI-generated images affect impulse travel purchases compared with human-generated images. This study aims to examine the effect of AI-enhanced versus human-generated images on impulse travel purchase decisions among Generation Z travellers, using Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) theory and consumption value theory as a theoretical lens. Design/methodology/approach Through a between-person experimental design, 580 participants were randomly assigned to view either AI-enhanced or human-generated images of a non-iconic travel destination. This study analysed results using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study found that preference value and social value directly and significantly influenced impulse purchase intentions, while all consumption values, including preference, social, emotional and functional values, affected impulse purchasing through travellers’ inspiration. Additionally, AI-enhanced images led to a higher preference value for impulse purchases, whereas human-generated images were perceived as having higher social value and visual aesthetic appeal. Originality/value By integrating the S-O-R framework with consumption value theory, this study offers fresh theoretical insights into the mediating role of traveller inspiration and the distinct value perceptions elicited by AI versus human-generated visuals. These findings also offer critical insights for tourism marketers using AI-driven visual content, consumers navigating increasingly AI-mediated travel promotions

latest.title: Integrating Islamic principles into business theories: developing Shariah-compliant theoretical lenses for upstream halal meat supply chains, evidence from New Zealand
