FoMO and PO were specified as mediators, and HC was examined as a moderator of the associations between price sensitivity and FoMO, PO, and impulsive consumption intention. Results Price sensitivity was positively associated with impulsive consumption intention. The indirect association through PO was significant, whereas the indirect association through FoMO alone was not. The serial indirect path from price sensitivity through FoMO and PO to impulsive consumption intention was significant. The interactions between price sensitivity and HC were negative in the impulsive consumption intention, FoMO, and PO equations, indicating weaker associations with price sensitivity at higher levels of HC. Discussion The findings identify PO as the most proximal psychological correlate of impulsive consumption intention in the proposed model and highlight HC as a boundary condition for the associations involving price sensitivity. The study offers practical recommendations for buffet restaurants seeking to reduce potential over-selection and food waste, including smaller initial portions, convenient refills, messages discouraging quantity-based value maximization, and health-oriented dining guidance. Future longitudinal and experimental research can examine the temporal and causal relations

latest.title: Consensus without conversion: local economy support orientation and the sustainable development goals across three tourism stakeholder groups in Uzbekistan
latest.abstract: Preference for locally produced goods is widely proposed as a behavioural lever for retaining tourism revenue in host economies, yet the international evidence describes sharp divergence between stakeholder groups. We tested whether that divergence appears in an emerging Silk Road destination by administering three parallel instruments to residents (n = 658), tourists (n = 565) and tourism industry actors (n = 370) in Bukhara, Uzbekistan (N = 1,593). Because consumer and tourism ethnocentrism describe home-economy support by residents and domestic actors, but not international visitors’ preference for host-country products, we compared the groups on a role-independent construct, local economy support orientation. Across semantically matched items, the three groups were statistically equivalent in their preference for local over imported products, their belief in local economic benefit, and a composite orientation index (all two one-sided tests p < 0.002 within a margin of 0.20 scale points), despite 95.6% power to detect a small effect. Divergence occurred instead within groups, as an attitude-behaviour gap between normative endorsement and self-reported enacted commitment: residents’ cultural pride exceeded their economic participation (d _ z = 0.51), tourists’ local-support intention exceeded their willingness to pay a premium (d _ z = 0.17), and suppliers’ advocacy for the Sustainable Development Goals exceeded their literacy in them (d _ z = 0.30). The residents’ gap widened monotonically as occupational access to the tourism value chain declined, and infrastructure readiness predicted tourists’ willingness to pay was more strongly than any identity-related variable. Attitudinal consensus is therefore not the binding constraint on locally anchored sustainable develo

latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fash

latest.title: Exploring the potential of green waqf as an alternative instrument for climate financing
latest.venue: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the determinants of Indonesian Muslims’ intentions to donate to green waqf, an Islamic financial instrument increasingly used for climate financing. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 550 cash-waqf donors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The model extends the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) by incorporating knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness into the traditional constructs of attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control (PBC). Reliability, convergent validity and discriminant validity were confirmed. Multicollinearity and predictive relevance were also assessed. Findings The study reveals that knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness positively influenced attitudes towards green waqf donations. Attitude, subjective norms, PBC and knowledge also directly influence intentions to donate to green waqf, with knowledge emerging as the primary driver. Research limitations/implications The findings suggest that green waqf should be repositioned from traditional philanthropy as a more dedicated climate-financing instrument. This requires strengthening waqf literacy, institutional transparency, impact disclosure and seamless digital channels to translate knowledge, trust and environmental awareness into sustained donation behaviour. These implications are particularly relevant for waqf institutions (nazhirs), waqf authorities and policymakers seeking to mobilise Islamic social finance for climate action. Originality/value This study advances the green waqf literature by extending the TPB to include environmental awareness, knowledge, trust and religiosity. By using a larger and more diverse sample than previous studies, it provides a c

latest.title: The Ethic of Decency and the Antecedents of Corporate Sufficiency
latest.abstract: As the paradigm of perpetual economic growth is increasingly seen as incompatible with environmental and social sustainability, sufficiency has gained traction as an alternative organizing principle to align economic activity with socio-ecological well-being. This study advances understanding of why and how firms engage in sufficiency. We define corporate sufficiency as the practice of corporate self-restraint grounded in the imperative to operate within planetary boundaries, even at the risk of forgoing profits and growth. While prior scholarship has challenged profit maximization as a corporate guiding principle, less is known about why firms voluntarily practice self-restraint and how they enact sufficiency in an economic context geared toward growth. Through a qualitative analysis of 70 sufficiency-oriented firms, we identify three antecedents that either motivate or enable observed corporate sufficiency practices, namely responsibility, relationality, and excellence. We argue that these antecedents can be framed within the ethic of decency, which provides context-sensitive guidance for firms to deliberate on and enact self-restraint in production and consumption practices. Through the advancement of decency as an ethical framework for corporate sufficiency, this study extends and integrates sufficiency and business ethics scholarship. It challenges the instrumental logic that underpins the sustainable consumption discourse and proposes a normative framework for reconciling business conduct with the imperatives of planetary and human well-being.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Beyond Social Rejection: Recalling Social Acceptance Shifts Relative Evaluations of Hypothetical Material and Experiential Purchases
latest.abstract: Sustainable-consumption research examines how psychological and social conditions shape the value consumers assign to possessions and alternative forms of consumption. In two experiments, Polish adults were randomly assigned to recall social rejection, social acceptance, or a neutral event (Study 1: N = 144; Study 2: N = 143). Material and experiential attractiveness were assessed separately, and relative experiential preference was calculated as the difference between these evaluations. In Study 1, rejection increased material-purchase attractiveness relative to both acceptance and neutral recall. Acceptance produced stronger relative experiential preference than either comparison condition, although absolute experiential attractiveness differed significantly only between acceptance and rejection. The acceptance-related relative-preference pattern recurred in Study 2, which additionally showed greater experiential attractiveness following acceptance than neutral recall. Evidence for rejection–control differences was inconsistent across the two samples. The central acceptance-related contrasts in relative experiential preference remained significant after adjustment for post-manipulation positive and negative affect in both studies. In Study 2, the pattern also remained evident after adjustment for dispositional materialism and subjective family economic status. Across both samples, participants who recalled acceptance showed a larger difference between their ratings of the selected experiential and material offers than participants in either comparison condition.

latest.title: Generational Differences in Omnichannel Shopping: Motivations, Cross-Channel Behavior, and Loyalty
latest.abstract: In an era where omnichannel retailing has become one of the most prominent topics in the retail industry, this study applies the Generational Cohort Theory to the context of omnichannel behavior in an emerging market. It aims to enhance the academic understanding and provide practical insights for retailers seeking to develop effective strategies for different generational cohorts. Using MANOVA, this study analyzed data collected from 341 respondents to investigate differences among Generation X, Generation Y, and Generation Z in shopping motivation, hedonic shopping motivation, cross-channel behavior, and customer loyalty. The findings reveal that Gen X, Gen Y, and Gen Z differ significantly in their shopping and hedonic shopping motivations, while no significant differences are found in cross-channel behavior and customer loyalty. By highlighting these distinctions, this study extends the application of the Generational Cohort Theory to omnichannel retailing in an emerging market. For industry practitioners, the findings emphasize the importance of understanding generational shopping motivations when designing omnichannel strategies. Rather than assuming that different generations exhibit distinct behavioral patterns or loyalty levels, retailers should tailor their approaches to consumers’ Shopping and hedonic needs to encourage cross-channel engagement and strengthen customer loyalty.

latest.title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions specifically within the used motorcycle showroom context.

latest.title: Egg and Egg Product Purchasing Levels Among the Academic Community of Politeknik Negeri Jember
latest.abstract: Animal protein plays a crucial role in supporting human health and productivity. This study aimed to describe consumer characteristics, analyze the purchasing levels of eggs and processed egg products, and examine the relationship between consumer characteristics and the purchasing levels of eggs and processed egg products among the academic community of Politeknik Negeri Jember. The study employed a quantitative approach using a cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected in July 2023 through an online questionnaire using a convenience sampling technique. A total of 124 respondents were included in the study. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, multiple response analysis, Chi-Square tests, and Cramer’s V with IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results showed that respondents were predominantly aged ≤20 years (30.6%), male (53.2%), non-postgraduate graduates (51.6%), lecturers (46.8%), and had monthly incomes below IDR 2,800,000 (47.6%). Commercial chicken eggs were the most frequently consumed type of egg (95.2%), while salted eggs were the most frequently consumed processed egg product (89.1%). Egg purchasing levels were predominantly high (62.9%), whereas processed egg product purchasing levels were predominantly low (46.0%). No relationship was found between consumer characteristics and egg purchasing levels, while age was associated with processed egg product purchasing levels. The development of egg-based agribusiness should therefore focus on product diversification and age-based market segmentation.

latest.title: From dream to disillusion: How failed Entrepreneurial ecosystem shape campus aspirations through fear of failure, grit and social engagement
latest.venue: European Journal of Sustainable Development Research
latest.abstract: This study examines the impact of entrepreneurial ecosystem failures on students’ entrepreneurial aspirations, while investigating fear of failure as a mediator and social capital engagement and grit as moderating influences. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study explores how failures within the entrepreneurial ecosystem - such as the absence of mentoring, experiential learning opportunities, and institutional support - lead to reduced self-efficacy, diminished perceived behavioral control, and lower entrepreneurial aspirations among students. Using a cross-sectional survey and structural equation modeling approach, data were collected from 221 undergraduate and postgraduate students who perceived their institutional entrepreneurial ecosystem as ineffective. The findings reveal that entrepreneurial ecosystem failures significantly increase students’ fear of failure (β = 0.69, p < .001) and negatively affect their entrepreneurial aspirations (β = –0.22, p < .001). Fear of failure partially mediates this relationship, demonstrating a significant indirect effect (–0.176). Furthermore, students with higher levels of grit (β = 0.220) and stronger social capital engagement (β = 0.306) are less adversely affected, as these factors buffer the negative impact on entrepreneurial aspirations. The findings provide important implications for educators, incubation centers, and policymakers by emphasizing the need to reduce institutional barriers and strengthen student resilience through targeted interventions. This study contributes to the literature on student entrepreneurship by integrating psychological and environmental barriers and by enhancing understanding of how entrepreneurial aspirations can be restored and strengthene

latest.title: Organisational Resources, Green Service Process Innovation and Environmental Sustainability Performance in Hotels: A Critical Literature Review
latest.venue: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
latest.abstract: Hotels consume energy, water, materials and generate waste and pollution. This review critically examines how organisational resources relate to environmental sustainability performance (ESP), considering Green Service Process Innovation (GSPI) as a potential linking mechanism. Present review synthesises published theoretical and empirical studies on pollution-prevention resources, GSPI and environmental outcomes in hotel settings. A structured critical literature review was conducted using the Resource-Based View, Natural Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the environmental dimension of the Triple Bottom Line. The literature identifies environmental investment, green human resource management, management environmental commitment and green organisational culture as complementary pollution-prevention resources. These resources may support environmentally oriented changes to service routines. However, direct evidence on GSPI remains limited because many studies examine broader green innovation constructs. ESP is considered through resource efficiency performance and waste and pollution performance. The integrated resource–innovation–performance perspective offers a useful explanation of hotel environmental sustainability, but its proposed relationships require further empirical examination. The review integrates these research streams and clarifies boundaries between pollution-prevention resources, service process innovation and environmental outcomes. Hotel managers should align environmental investment with employee development, management commitment, organisational culture and process improvement to better manage sustainability related challenges.

latest.title: Place-based governance and local public procurement: engaging small and medium enterprises in low carbon, inclusive transitions
latest.abstract: Public procurement is increasingly recognised as a pivotal yet underexploited mechanism for advancing local low carbon and inclusive transitions in the United Kingdom (UK). Recent reforms, such as the Procurement Act 2023, create new opportunities for local authorities to embed environmental and social objectives into procurement processes, while enhancing the inclusion and participation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and voluntary, community and social enterprises (VCSEs). Given local governments’ responsibility for planning, transport, development and some infrastructure, local authorities are well positioned to shape place-based climate action, despite lacking a formal energy mandate. In the absence of statutory requirements, however, the extent to which carbon reporting, energy demand reduction and wider environmental criteria are incorporated into public procurement is largely discretionary, resulting in uneven expectations and support for SMEs and VCSEs across the UK. Drawing on qualitative interviews, this paper examines how the UK’s evolving local procurement practices can engage SMEs and VCSEs in these areas. Our findings reveal that public procurement is shifting from a compliance-focused function to a more relational governance mechanism that facilitates early dialogue, bidirectional learning, and potential new entry routes for SME engagement in decarbonisation. However, these developments remain uneven across place and are shaped by significant capacity disparities within both SMEs/VCSEs and local authorities alike. While procurement may encourage the normalisation of carbon reporting, our findings reveal that it also risks amplifying inequalities between regions and between SMEs with differing resources and levels of readiness. latest.title: Upholding Sufficiency-Ethical Practices: Insights from a Sufficiency-Oriented Community in Ecuador
latest.abstract: The concept of sufficiency presents a compelling alternative to the dominant paradigm of unrestrained economic growth and resource exploitation, emphasizing the importance of achieving a balance between needs and wants to ensure well-being within planetary boundaries. With intensifying ecological and social pressures, sufficiency offers not only a theoretical critique of unlimited growth but also a practical framework for moving toward sustainable lifestyles. Prior research, while examining sufficiency through practices like goods repair and seasonal consumption, has inadequately addressed the ethical grounding of these practices, despite the fact that practices are the means by which ethical principles become visible. To address this gap, this study investigates how ethical virtues serve as organizing principles for sufficiency practices, drawing on social practice theory to bridge virtue ethics and sufficiency. Utilizing qualitative data obtained from an Ecuadorian non-profit organization, we develop a process model that explains how sufficiency-ethical practices are established, formalized, disseminated and upheld. This work extends the literature on the intersection of sufficiency and ethics by providing a comprehensive exploration of organizational virtues as organizing principles for sufficiency practices and by shedding light on the potential for fostering sufficiency-oriented communities that enhance resilience, justice, solidarity and environmental stewardship.

latest.title: From Environmental Knowledge to Green Flight Preference: An Empirical Study
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: The growing emphasis on environmental sustainability has intensified the need to understand sustainable consumer behaviour in the airline industry. This study develops and tests an integrated model examining the relationships between perceived environmental knowledge, green marketing awareness, green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Data were collected from airline passengers in Türkiye and analysed using a structural equation modelling approach. The findings indicate that perceived environmental knowledge positively influences both green marketing awareness and green flight preference, while its effect on green brand trust is not significant and its relationship with price tolerance is negative. Green marketing awareness positively affects green brand trust, price tolerance and green flight preference. Green brand trust does not play a positive moderating role in the effect of green marketing awareness on green flight preference. In addition, green brand trust significantly enhances green flight preference. The results suggest that environmental knowledge alone is insufficient to foster price acceptance for green flight options, highlighting the importance of credible green marketing practices in shaping trust and behavioural intentions in the airline industry. The study contributes to sustainable consumer behaviour literature by integrating cognitive, marketing and behavioural constructs in aviation context.

latest.title: Government Policy, Organizational Responses, and Sustainable Performance: An Organizational Perspective
latest.abstract: Sustainable performance is increasingly important for enterprises operating under growing environmental, technological, and institutional pressures. Drawing on stakeholder theory and dynamic capabilities theory, this study examines an integrated model of the relationships among government policy, environmental compliance, digital adoption, innovation capability, ethical leadership, and sustainable performance. Using cross‐sectional survey data based on the organizational perceptions of 303 senior managers, board members, and business owners in Vietnam, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) to examine the proposed direct and indirect relationships. The results show significant positive associations between government policy and both environmental compliance and digital adoption, as well as between environmental compliance and digital adoption and ethical leadership. Digital adoption, innovation capability, and ethical leadership are positively associated with sustainable performance, while digital adoption has a positive relationship with innovation capability. Environmental compliance has no statistically significant direct association with sustainable performance but shows significant indirect associations through digital adoption and ethical leadership. Overall, the findings clarify how policy‐related perceptions, organizational responses, capabilities, and leadership are statistically associated with multidimensional sustainable performance in an emerging‐market context. Given the cross‐sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causal or temporal relationships.

latest.title: Assessing the Determinants of Intentions to Participate in Reverse Logistics for Environmental Sustainability
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: This paper examines the determinants of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) students' intentions to engage in reverse logistics activities, namely recycling, reuse and remanufacturing, in line with Malaysia's Circular Economy Blueprint 2025–2035. Although universities are important settings for building sustainable habits, little is known about what motivates students to take part in reverse logistics beyond recycling. This study integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Norm Activation Model (NAM) to examine both cognitive-instrumental and moral-normative influences on student participation, and explains how overlapping constructs from the two models were distinguished. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with 384 UTM students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire that measured current reverse logistics participation and six determinants: attitude, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control, awareness of consequence, ascription of responsibility and personal norm. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses were performed. Students reported high participation in reuse (M = 4.06), recycling (M = 4.01) and remanufacturing (M = 3.96). All six determinants were significantly and positively correlated with intention. The integrated model explained 63.1% of the variance in intention, with subjective norm (β = 0.283), attitude (β = 0.251) and personal norm (β = 0.244) emerging as significant predictors, while perceived behavioral control, awareness of consequence and ascription of responsibility were not significant when all predictors were considered together. latest.title: Exploring the Impact of Demographic Variables on Consumer Perception Toward Green Marketing Strategies: A Study of the FMCG Sector in India
latest.abstract: The objective of the present study is to investigate the effect of demographic variables on consumer perception of Green marketing strategies of Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) in India. The present study adopted a survey research methodology to collect data from 337 consumers in India, both online and offline, through a survey method. The main methodology used by the researcher in the present study is that of a structured questionnaire. A random sampling technique was employed to select a diverse sample for the present study. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques have been used to study the effect of demographic variables such as gender, age, income, and education on consumer perception of Green marketing strategies. The present study showed a significant difference in consumer perception of Green marketing strategies based on demographic variables. The current study highlights the importance of demographic variables while formulating effective Green marketing strategies for the FMCG sector in India. The findings of the current study are significant for businesses and policymakers to formulate effective Green marketing strategies to promote green consumers for the FMCG sector. JEL Classification: M31, Q56, D12

latest.title: What drives social entrepreneurial intention? An integrated model of cognitive, moral, and social antecedents among university students in India
latest.abstract: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the social entrepreneurial intention framework, investigates the cognitive, moral, normative, and experiential determinants of SEI among higher education students. Employing a quantitative methodology, a cross-sectional design was utilized, involving 349 postgraduate and undergraduate participants. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that opportunity recognition competency (ORC) is the most significant predictor of SEI, underscoring the importance of entrepreneurial cognition in SEI. SEI is positively correlated with social entrepreneurial self-efficacy and subjective norms, indicating the significance of perceived entrepreneurial capability and social endorsement. However, SEI does not exhibit significant associations with empathy, moral obligation, perceived sustainability values, perceived social support, perceived behavioural control, or prior experience. Notably, prior experience is indirectly linked to SEI through social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, despite its direct and total associations with SEI being non-significant. Overall, the findings suggest that opportunity recognition competency, social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and subjective norms hold greater relative importance for SEI when antecedents are evaluated concurrently.

latest.title: Sustainability in Charity Retail: Conflicts in (In)Sufficiency
latest.abstract: Sufficiency has been receiving attention as a means to achieve sustainability. Insights on how to operationalise sufficiency in practice are limited and absent in the context of ecologically constrained organisations, such as, charities. Charities are viewed as critical to sustainability due to their reuse business model; however, charity income is dropping due to the saturation of low-quality and value clothing donations generated by ever-increasing production and consumption of (ultra)fast fashion. This is placing resource (e.g. reliance on volunteer labour) and ecological (e.g. finding reuse routes) burdens on an already constrained sector, highlighting the urgency for charities to future proof the retail businesses foundational to their fundraising efforts. To address this challenge, this research adopts an ethic of sufficiency to introduce business model innovation to charity retail. Drawing on interviews and observations with charity staff, collaborating experts and consumers as donor and retail users, we examine transition to a clothing rental model offering social and ecological sufficiency. We find that the two competing ethics of: (1) sufficiency representing enough and driving deceleration and (2) insufficiency representing not enough and driving acceleration, compete for primacy. While sufficiency can counter challenges arising from insufficiency, competition between them creates contradictory pressures for the charity. This is further exasperated by a misalignment between organisation and consumer experiences of sufficiency. The theoretical and practical implications of the findings for sufficiency, charity retail, rental and consumption are discussed.

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: Environmental Practices and Household Green Purchasing Behavior among College Students
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine which domain of environmental practices significantly influenced the household green purchasing behavior of college students at a higher education institution. In this study, a quantitative, non-experimental research design using descriptive-correlational techniques was used. The Simple Random Sampling was utilized, which involved the two hundred forty-five (245) students who were officially enrolled in the second semester of the 2024-2025 school year. The contextualized questionnaire was used for data collection, and the statistical tools employed for data analysis included the Mean, Standard Deviation, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, and Linear Regression. The results showed that the level of environmental practices was high, which implied that it is often manifested and the household green purchasing behavior as high, which implied that it is often manifested by the students as well. Additionally, the study revealed a significant relationship between environmental practices and the green purchasing behavior of college students. Moreover, all the domains of environmental practices, awareness of environmental concepts, awareness of environmental issues, and practices on the need to solve environmental problems significantly influenced the household green purchasing behavior of college students. This only means that environmental practices are integral to the household green purchasing behavior of college students.

latest.title: Institutional Drivers and Constraints of Green Entrepreneurship in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030: An Integrated Analytic Hierarchy Process
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: Although there is increasing academic interest in green entrepreneurship, there are few empirical studies on the enablers and barriers of green entrepreneurship in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies. This creates a knowledge gap on how oil-dependent and resource-dependent nations can transition to sustainable business ecosystems. This study investigates the institutional, social and economic drivers and barriers to the development of green entrepreneurship in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) in the strategic context of Vision 2030. The study uses a hybrid methodological design of a SWOT-based survey of 62 civil servants working in Saudi Regional Authorities, an Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Framework (EEF) domain-mapping exercise, and a further Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) prioritization exercise with 18 experts from regional authorities, development finance institutions, and green entrepreneurship practitioners. The integrated EEF-AHP analysis shows that the domain with the highest priority weight is the Policy and Regulatory Environment (0.28), followed by Finance (0.22) and Human Capital (0.18). This suggests that institutional and financing gaps are the main systemic constraints. In the SWOT survey, the highest-rated strengths are natural resource endowments and environmentally protected areas. The highest-rated weaknesses are limited natural resource management capacity and a low level of existing green infrastructure, followed by the absence of an appropriate regulatory regime. The highest-rated opportunities are new business start-ups, better environmental quality and higher local income. latest.title: The Effect of Product Availability, Service Quality, Price Fairness and Store Trust on Repurchase Intention (A Study at Sari Jaya Tani Agricultural Store)
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of product availability, service quality, price fairness, and store trust on repurchase intention among customers of Sari Jaya Tani, an agricultural input store in Brebes Regency. A quantitative survey was conducted with 100 customers selected through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The four variables jointly had a significant effect on repurchase intention and explained 86.5% of its variance. Service quality, price fairness, and store trust each had a positive and significant effect, whereas product availability had no significant partial effect. Price fairness was the strongest predictor. The non-significant effect of product availability is discussed in relation to its overlap with store trust and the predominance of loyal customers in the sample. Agricultural input retailers should prioritize fair pricing, advisory service, and trust building while keeping stock reliable during planting seasons.

latest.title: Barriers to the Transition from Intention to Green Consumption Behavior: An Empirical Study in Ho Chi Minh City
latest.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development

Yet the persistent gap between green intention and green behavior suggests that a positive attitude and intention alone are not always enough to produce sustainable consumption. This study therefore examines the factors that shape green purchase intention and green consumption behavior, and analyzes the conditions that can either facilitate or hinder the translation of intention into actual consumer behavior in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Specifically, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study tests the effects of attitude (ATT), subjective norm (SN), and perceived behavioral control (PBC) on green purchase intention (GPI); the effect of GPI on green consumption behavior (GCB); the mediating role of GPI; and the moderating roles of price sensitivity (PS) and green product availability (PA). The study adopted a mixed-methods design. A preliminary qualitative phase was conducted through interviews and group discussions with 13 consumers to refine and finalize the observed variables. The quantitative phase was carried out through a face-to-face survey of consumers aged 18 and above who had lived in Ho Chi Minh City for at least six months and were involved in their household's purchasing decisions. Of the 400 questionnaires distributed, 354 valid responses were retained for analysis, corresponding to a response rate of 88.5%. The data were processed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 24.0. latest.title: From Organizational Strategy to Sustainable Consumption: An Integrated NRBV–TPB Model of Green Market Orientation and Organic Food Choice
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Global environmental pollution, problems associated with food safety, and growing awareness about health issues have raised the demand for sustainable consumption; however, the uptake of organic foods has been relatively low in developing countries such as Bangladesh. In this conceptual research, an integrative theoretical model is proposed that links attitude to behavior in organic food consumption by connecting organizational-level green marketing strategies and consumer psychology. Grounded in natural resource-based view (NRBV) and theory of planned behavior (TPB), the model takes green market orientation as the strategic antecedent, which affects consumer attitude toward sustainability and, in turn, organic food consumption. It is posited that consumer attitude toward sustainability acts as the mediating variable between green market orientation and organic food consumption; environmental concern works as the moderating variable for all three direct relationships in the model. Theoretically, this study offers a novel multilevel integration of NRBV and TPB in the sustainable food consumption research area. Practically, it emphasizes the role of genuine green marketing in forming consumers’ sustainability attitudes and organic food consumption in emerging markets. latest.title: Decoding the Relationship between Organizational Culture and Workplace Happiness in India: An Empirical Investigation
latest.abstract: Sustainable Development goals initiated by the United Nations Organizations (UNO) have made it vital for survival and growth organizations to modify and revamp the ways in which they used to conduct business. Circular Economy is an economic system focusing on reducing, reuse and recycling [1]. Thus, sustainability is the focal point for achieving and implementing CE principles. Organizations cannot be expected to immediately transition and adopt CE principles. The adaptation and transformation need to be accompanied by changing organization culture and practices. The study undertaken is an attempt to implore the impact and analyze the vital relationship between Organizational Culture (OC) on Workplace Happiness (WPH), This is done with a view to suggesting strategies for organizations to create an inclusive culture at workplace. The research uses a methodology of exploratory nature and employs a questionnaire to collect responses from professionals employed in IT sector in the North India region. Responses were collected from a sample consisting of 250 respondents through Google Forms and face-to-face interaction. The collected data was analyzed using SPSS 23.0, through application of descriptive statistics and regression analysis. The results reveal that workplace happiness is largely and in a positive manner impacted by the culture prevalent at the workplace. Thus, bringing forth the role that an inclusive and positive culture plays in enhancing the well-being and satisfaction of employees. Moreover, to accomplish this need of the hour is to invest in a value-based culture which goes in line with the expectations and aims for which an employee comes to the workplace. latest.title: Aplicação da internet das coisas na logística reversa: um estudo de caso em inovação e sustentabilidade na economia circular
latest.abstract: A crescente necessidade de aumentar a eficiência dos sistemas de logística reversa e promover práticas alinhadas aos princípios da economia circular tem impulsionado a adoção de tecnologias digitais capazes de ampliar a rastreabilidade, o monitoramento e a otimização operacional dos fluxos de resíduos. Nesse contexto, a Internet das Coisas (IoT) destaca-se como uma tecnologia habilitadora da transformação digital aplicada à gestão sustentável de recursos. O presente estudo analisa os efeitos da implementação de dispositivos e sensores IoT na logística reversa de cartuchos e toners de impressoras pertencentes ao setor eletroeletrônico. Para tanto, foi conduzido um estudo de caso único em uma empresa de gestão ambiental sediada no estado de São Paulo, utilizando abordagem de métodos mistos baseada em quatro entrevistas semiestruturadas com profissionais técnicos e na análise documental de oito relatórios e registros operacionais referentes ao período de janeiro a dezembro de 2024. Os dados foram examinados por meio de triangulação de fontes, codificação temática e verificação documental dos indicadores operacionais. Os resultados demonstram que a utilização dos sensores permitiu reconfigurar as rotas de coleta, reduzindo a frequência semanal de viagens de quatro para duas operações (-50%), sem comprometer o volume médio coletado, mantido em aproximadamente 80 kg por semana. Observou-se ainda uma redução estimada de cerca de 2.600 km percorridos anualmente e uma economia aproximada de 520 litros de diesel por ano, resultando na diminuição das emissões associadas ao transporte. latest.title: Assessing environmental indicators for green supply chain success using a structured decision-making framework: a case study of the ceramic industry
latest.abstract: Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) provides an integrative platform to reduce environmental harm across production systems. This study applies an integrated CRITIC–ARAS multi-criteria decision-making framework to evaluate and prioritize environmental indicators for green supply chain management in the ceramic industry, using the Amin Meybod Tile and Ceramic Factory in Yazd, Iran, as a real-world case study. Environmental criteria were first identified and weighted using the CRITIC method, which quantifies the relative importance of criteria based on contrast intensity and information entropy. These weighted factors were then used to rank the mining sites using the ARAS method. The results indicate that Waste Recycling, Noise Pollution, Waste Level, Gas Emission Levels, and Green Transportation practices are the most influential indicators driving green supply chain performance in the case study. To show the stability of the proposed framework, the results were compared with those obtained from WASPAS, TOPSIS, and MOORA methods, and a high level of consistency in rankings confirmed the stability and reliability of the CRITIC–ARAS approach. The study concludes by offering practical green management strategies and operational recommendations aligned with the identified environmental priorities. The findings contribute theoretically by extending hybrid MCDM applications to resource-intensive industries and practically by providing managers with a structured tool and actionable insights for industries aiming to integrate sustainability principles into supply chain design and resource procurement.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement . Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector . The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior: role of credibility, perceived authenticity, and sustainability
hot.abstract: Introduction Social media advertising is a crucial factor for predicting consumer behavior. Further credibility, authenticity, and sustainability of social postings enhance consumer purchase intentions in general and online shopping in particular. This empirical study investigated the impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior and the role of credibility, perceived authenticity and sustainability. The study also investigated the mediating effect of trust in the relationship between social media advertising and consumer behavior. Methods To measure the impact of the social media advertising effect on consumer behavior, eight reflective constructs, namely, credibility, sustainability, perceived authenticity, social media advertising effectiveness, satisfaction, purchase intentions and perceived value, were assessed. For the mediation analysis, consumer behavior was modeled as a higher-order construct with three sub-dimensions: satisfaction, perceived value and purchase intentions. Furthermore, the construct social media effectiveness is also modeled as a higher-order construct with four sub-dimensions: credibility, sustainability, authenticity and social media advertisement effectiveness. The data were collected from active social media users who engage in brand advertising and online shopping. A total of 500 valid responses were subjected to exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling. Results and discussion The SEM results reveal that constructs credibility and sustainability are strong predictors of consumer behavior in the context of social media advertising effectiveness. The mediating variable of trust partially mediated the relationship between social media effectiveness and consumer beh

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Influencers’ Credibility Effect on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Intention
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: In the evolving world of influencer marketing, Artificial Intelligence (AI) influencers are creating significant impact and transforming the approach to brand promotions on social media platforms. In recent times, many popular brands have partnered with AI influencers to engage with their social media audiences. AI influencers have become popular as a novel method for brands to increase customer engagement and create purchase intention, but there is a scarcity of research on this emerging trend of marketing. The AI-based virtual influencers effect on consumer engagement and purchase intention remain largely unexplored. This study used a questionnaire-based survey method and 414 responses were collected. The result from the research shows that credibility, informative value and human-likeness are the major factors influencing consumer engagement purchase intention towards brands promoted through AI-based virtual influencers. The attractiveness and entertainment value of AI influencer’s social media posts affect consumer engagement but exhibit no effect on purchase intention. Theoretical and managerial recommendations related to AI influencers’ marketing are presented.

hot.title: The Evolution of Digital Tourism Marketing: From Hashtags to AI-Immersive Journeys in the Metaverse Era
hot.abstract: This study examines how social media platforms influence tourism marketing strategies, consumer perceptions, and travel behaviors, addressing their sustainability implications. It aims to evaluate the current state of research on social media in tourism marketing, identify dominant trends, assess empirical evidence of impact, and critically highlight research gaps. The analysis focuses on three core marketing outcomes: destination image, travel intention, and user engagement—and includes a section examining sustainability considerations across environmental, sociocultural, and economic dimensions. The study uses a systematic critical review of 147 peer-reviewed academic articles published between 2015 and 2025, combined with a meta-analysis of 38 quantitative studies that report statistical effect sizes. The meta-analysis uses a random-effects model to compare the influence of different platforms and study contexts. Moderator variables include geographic region, platform type, and methodological design. Findings show that social media marketing has a statistically significant positive effect on destination image (Cohen’s d = 0.61), travel intention (d = 0.54), and user engagement (d = 0.43). The analysis also reveals geographic bias, limited research on emerging platforms, and a lack of longitudinal and ethical inquiry. Findings suggest that tourism researchers and marketers may have to adopt more context-sensitive, interdisciplinary, and ethical approaches. Critical sustainability concerns emerge, including “overtourism”, cultural commodification, digital inequities, and algorithmic biases.
