But the symbolic imagery of nature in cosmetics advertising that is created through Instagram has not been adequately studied from the point of view of eco-imagism. This study explored the representation of nature in the Instagram ads of selected international cosmetic brands and the meanings created in these ads concerning beauty, naturalness, sustainability, authenticity, and environmental responsibility. The study used an interpretivist approach and the main analytical framework was Eco-imagistics. Ten advertisements were used, and ten international cosmetic companies' official Instagram accounts were used to purposively select an advertisement. Natural or environmental elements visible in the advertisement such as plants, flowers, fruits, water, landscape, botanical ingredients, natural colours, and ecological textures, were used to help determine the advertisements that were selected. The results identified that nature was always presented visually as purity, freshness, nourishment, health, authenticity and ecological value. The advertisements were analysed through the visual composition, botanical imagery, natural materials, lighting, textures and other visual elements related to nature. The study also revealed that nature was not only used as a decorative but also as a key visual element that brands used to create their brand image as environmentally friendly. The advertisements tended to idealize and commodity nature, making ecological harmony an aesthetically pleasing element of consumer culture.

latest.title: Innovation as a Strategic Tool for Customer Retention among Small and Medium Enterprises in Kano State
latest.abstract: This study investigates innovation as a strategic tool for customer retention among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Kano State, Nigeria. The objectives were to examine the effect of product innovation, assess the influence of service innovation, and evaluate the impact of process innovation on customer retention. Employing a survey research design, primary quantitative data were collected from 387 owners and managers of SMEs across manufacturing, trading, and service sectors. Multiple regression analysis revealed that all three innovation dimensions positively and significantly affect customer retention (p < 0.001), collectively explaining 52.4% of the variance, with service innovation exhibiting the strongest effect (β = 0.346), followed by product innovation (β = 0.337) and process innovation (β = 0.209). These findings shows innovation's multidimensional role in enhancing customer loyalty in resource-constrained settings. Recommendations include prioritizing service and product innovations, investing in process improvements, and advocating for government and industry support through training, financing, and technology access to bolster SME innovation capabilities and long-term customer retention.

latest.title: Marka Havalılığı İle İlgili Yapılmış Çalışmaların Sistematik Literatür Taraması
latest.abstract: Günümüzün yoğun rekabet ortamında işletmeler için yalnızca markalarının sunduğu fonksiyonel faydalara odaklanmak yeterli olmamakta, aynı zamanda tüketicilerin duygularına hitap ederek onlarla güçlü bağlar kurmak da önemli hâle gelmektedir. Bu doğrultuda marka aşkı, marka tutkusu, marka bağlılığı, marka yakınlığı, marka güveni, marka özdeşleşmesi, marka otantikliği gibi tüketicilerin markalara yönelik duygusal değerlendirmelerini yansıtan marka ile ilgili unsurlar ön plana çıkmış ve tüketici davranışları açısından sıklıkla araştırılan kavramlar hâline gelmiştir. Bu noktada son yıllarda karşımıza çıkan güncel konulardan biri de marka havalılığıdır. Bu çalışmanın temel amacı, marka havalılığı ile ilgili yapılmış makalelerin yıllar, dergi, ülke, atıf, yöntem, ana kütle türü, örneklem büyüklüğü ve çalışılan değişkenler açısından sistematik literatür taraması yöntemiyle inceleyerek Türkçe literatürde oldukça az çalışılan bir konu olarak dikkat çekmek ve mevcut araştırma boşluklarını ortaya koyarak gelecekteki çalışmalara zemin hazırlamaktır.

latest.title: AREAS OF CRAFT BRAND–CONSUMER INTERACTION IN THE DIGITAL ENVIRONMENT
latest.venue: Scientific Notes of Taurida National V I Vernadsky University Series Economy and Management
latest.abstract: The relevance of research into craft brand marketing is determined by the specific characteristics of craft food products, whose consumer value is shaped not only by their functional attributes but also by their uniqueness, authenticity, local origin, production characteristics, and direct connection between the producer and the consumer. The current state of the craft food market and the specific features of craft brand development in the context of digitalisation have been identified. Differences between conventional marketing of food enterprises and craft brand marketing have been revealed, manifested in a shift in emphasis from production scaling, standardisation, and mass communication towards product uniqueness and authenticity, locality, personalised interaction, and community building around the brand. The marketing mix model for craft food products has been improved by developing the basic «4P» concept into an adapted «7P» model, with the content of its elements specified in accordance with the specific characteristics of craft products and the digital environment. The effectiveness of digital interaction between a craft food brand and its consumers is determined not only by the reach of its digital audience but also by the brand’s ability to provide a consistent and interconnected consumer experience across all stages of consumer-brand contact. This creates the conditions for deeper consumer engagement, the development of trust, the formation of brand attachment, and the establishment of long-term relationships with consumers. The presence of craft food brands and the specific features of their interaction with consumers on Instagram have been examined. The main forms of digital interaction have been identified and systematised, including informational, emotio

latest.title: Closing the Knowledge Gap: How Moral Obligations, Perceived Benefits, and Dispositional Greed Shape Influencer Advertising Code Compliance
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has outpaced regulatory enforcement and has increased the risk of noncompliance through misleading promotions and inadequate sponsorship disclosures. This study investigates whether and how enhancing influencers’ advertising code knowledge affects their intentions to comply with advertising regulations. Specifically, it examines whether increased knowledge enhances compliance intentions, whether this relationship is mediated by moral obligations and perceived benefits, and whether dispositional greed moderates these mediating pathways. Across four studies, involving 1,082 U.K.-based social media influencers, we employed diverse research designs. Study 1 uses a single-session pre–post design (N = 154); Study 2 adopts a two-wave pre–post design (N = 213); Study 3 applies a third-person, between-subjects design (N = 228); and Study 4 employs a randomized experimental design (N = 487). The findings reveal that greater advertising code knowledge significantly increases influencers’ intentions to comply. This effect is mediated by stronger moral obligations and heightened recognition of the compliance benefits. Furthermore, dispositional greed moderates the influence of knowledge on both moral obligations and perceived benefits. These findings highlight the importance of targeted education and training that build influencers’ advertising code knowledge as a lever for strengthening ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.

latest.title: Conceptualising customer online social experience (COSE) – A qualitative enquiry
latest.venue: Journal of Global Scholars of Marketing Science
latest.abstract: Despite growing academic interest in online customer experience (OCE), the notion of customer online social experience (COSE) remains underexplored in academic literature. The purpose of this paper is to conceptualise COSE and identify the main components of COSE, its antecedents and consequences in omni-channel retailing context. Drawing on social presence and social response theories, it examines how social mechanisms embedded in digital channels shape customer experiences. Using a qualitative approach, data were gathered from 24 in-depth interviews and capturing 30 narratives which were subsequently analysed thematically using inductive and deductive coding. Two main dimensions of COSE have been revealed: perceived social presence and social affiliation. Omni-channel management (OCM), comprising channel functionality and channel integration, emerges as a critical enabler of COSE. As a result, COSE influences customers’ responses such as repurchase intention and referral behaviour. This paper makes significant contribution to OCE literature by theorising the social dimension of online experience and the COSE process itself across interconnected channels. This paper also provides managerial guidance about how to leverage OCM and social stimuli to create more social online experiences and develop brand–customer relationships.

latest.title: La cultura visual en redes sociales y la percepción del cliente en el comercio digital: análisis desde una empresa peruana del sector biomédico
latest.venue: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual
latest.abstract: Este estudio analiza la relación entre el uso de redes sociales como canal de ventas y la percepción del cliente en una empresa peruana del sector biomédico. Desde un enfoque cuantitativo, se identificaron asociaciones significativas entre los recursos visuales empleados (colores, imágenes, diseño gráfico) y dimensiones clave de la experiencia del cliente, tales como la percepción del servicio, la fidelización, la identidad de marca y la interacción simbólica en entornos digitales. Los hallazgos sugieren que las redes sociales, más allá de su función comercial, operan como entornos visuales de comunicación que configuran la imagen de marca y contribuyen a enriquecer la relación entre empresa y consumidor en contextos digitales.

latest.title: Virtual influencers’ impact on brand ethicality and brand trust: a systematic review and future research directions
latest.abstract: Virtual influencers (VIs) are reshaping brand–consumer relationships, yet the psychological and ethical implications of delegating brand agency to non-human entities remain theoretically fragmented. This paper synthesizes the literature on antecedents of brand trust and brand ethicality in VI and related AI-mediated brand contexts and examines how, and under what conditions, the two judgments converge or diverge. A PRISMA-guided systematic quantitative literature review of 81 articles from Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO (published up to March 2025) combined bibliometric and qualitative thematic analysis. Drawing on communication models and persuasion theory, the proposed integrative framework groups brand trust antecedents into source, message, receiver, relational, brand, and contextual factors. Grounded in ethical decision-making theory, stakeholder theory, and responsible AI literature, brand ethicality drivers are categorized into transparency, accountability, privacy, data ethics, social responsibility, moral AI agency, algorithmic fairness, and commercial ethics. The primary theoretical contribution, the “digital persona paradox,” integrates brand trust and brand ethicality into a single tension between technological efficiency (pro-synthetic force) and perceived authenticity (anti-synthetic force) that arises when brands delegate persona-level agency to synthetic social actors. Evidence-supported findings are distinguished from the authors’ inferences and from claims advanced for future testing. A future research agenda is offered.

latest.title: TOURIST CHARACTERISTICS AS DETERMINANTS OF DESTINATION EXPERIENCE: EVIDENCE FROM SERBIA
latest.venue: PEOPLE International Journal of Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Tourists’ socio-demographic and travel-related characteristics, such as travel companion or previous visits to the destination, play an important role in tailoring tourism offering to attract specific tourist segments. The principal aim of the present research was to examine whether differences exist in tourists’ perception of emotional experience, destination personality and place attachment. The study sample consisted of Serbian tourists who visited the coastal tourist destination of Paralia, Greece. A total of 304 respondents participated in the survey research, which was conducted in July 2019, and the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) was employed to test the research hypotheses. The main findings indicated that female tourists expressed higher levels of emotional experience, perceived the visited destination through the prism of personality traits to a greater extent, and developed stronger place attachment compared to their male counterparts. Also, statistically significant differences across the investigated constructs were identified based on respondents’ age, education level, occupation status, monthly income, and previous visits to the destination. The practical implications of these findings are discussed in the paper.

latest.title: Modeling Digital-Green Support Systems for Sustainable Franchise Performance: The Interplay of Relational Quality and Management Participation
latest.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
latest.abstract: The simultaneous pressures of digital transformation and sustainable development are reshaping franchise governance, yet limited empirical research has examined how digital, environmental, and reputational resources jointly contribute to sustainable performance, particularly in emerging markets. This study develops and tests an integrated framework explaining how Green Franchising (GF), Digital Franchising (DF), and Brand Reputation (BR) influence Sustainable Franchise Performance (SFP), with Relationship Quality (RQ) serving as a relational mechanism and Franchise Typology (FT) capturing heterogeneity across franchise systems. Drawing on agency theory, resource scarcity logic, signaling theory, social exchange theory, the resource-based view, the natural-resource-based view, and contingency theory, the study conceptualizes sustainable franchise performance as a multidimensional outcome encompassing operational, market, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 314 franchise owners and managers directly involved in operating food and beverage (F&B) franchise outlets in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The results show that GF (β = 0.246, p < 0.001), DF (β = 0.231, p = 0.001), and BR (β = 0.425, p < 0.001) significantly strengthen RQ, while RQ has a substantial positive effect on SFP (β = 0.493, p < 0.001). BR also directly improves SFP (β = 0.187, p = 0.010). In contrast, the direct effects of GF and DF on SFP are not statistically significant, suggesting that green and digital support resources do not automatically translate into sustainable performance but depend substantially on

latest.title: Is AI (Failure) Here to Stay? An Examination of Stability Attributions, Customer Responses, and Repurchase Intentions
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly integrated into customer-facing financial services, particularly within the wealth management industry where firms rely on AI-driven systems for portfolio recommendations, fraud detection, customer communication, and financial advising support.While these technologies offer efficiency, they also introduce new forms of service failure that may alter how customers evaluate firms regarding trust, satisfaction, and frustration.Existing service failure and recovery literature has extensively examined customer responses to human-caused failures; however, comparatively less research has explored how consumers cognitively and emotionally process service failures caused by AI systems.More specifically, little attention has been given to whether customers perceive AI failures as temporary incidents or as indicators of broader systemic instability within the firm.This study seeks to examine customer responses to human-and AI-caused service failures in the wealth management industry through the lens of Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), Construal Level Theory (CLT), and Attribution Theory.Specifically, a research model is developed to investigate how perceptions of service failure severity influence attributional stability, defined as the extent to which consumers perceive a failure as ongoing, permanent, and likely to recur over time.The model further examines how stability attributions affect trust, firm satisfaction, frustration, and repurchase intentions following service failures involving either human or AI error.

latest.title: Pengaruh Strategi Social Commerce terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen pada Platform TikTok Shop
latest.venue: JEMBA JURNAL EKONOMI MANAJEMEN BISNIS DAN AKUNTANSI
latest.abstract: The growth of social media has changed consumer shopping behavior through social commerce, particularly on the TikTok Shop platform, which integrates digital content, social interaction, and online transactions. This study aims to analyze the effect of social commerce strategy on consumer purchase decisions on TikTok Shop in Pangkalpinang City. A quantitative explanatory approach was used with a survey method through an online questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale. The sample consisted of 97 respondents selected by purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and simple linear regression. The results show that social commerce strategy has a positive and significant effect on consumer purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.000, a regression coefficient of 0.198, a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.467, and a coefficient of determination of 21.8%. These findings indicate that social commerce strategies implemented through social interaction, live streaming, consumer reviews, community recommendations, and content creators can improve consumer purchase decisions on TikTok Shop.

latest.title: The Role of Influencer PR in Communicating Ethical Values in the Beauty Industry: A Comparative Study of Nano-Ambassadors at Tropic Skincare and Individual Beauty-Related Micro-Influencers
latest.abstract: Ethics has become central to beauty brands’ communication strategies, yet, existing research offers limited insight into how different influencer types convey ethical values and how their strategies shape consumer perceptions. This study addresses these gaps by comparing Tropic Skincare’s ambassadors and independent micro-influencers. These two categories operating under distinct arrangements. A mixed-methods approach was employed. Qualitative text analysis of 28 social media posts was conducted using NVivo, focusing on ethical messaging, sponsorship disclosure, and personal narrative strategies. A quantitative questionnaire survey (N=298) was analysed through SPSS to examine consumer perceptions of trust, authenticity, and purchase intention. The findings reveal clear strategic divergence. Ambassadors prioritize brand-aligned consistency and explicit disclosure, while micro-influencers emphasize personal storytelling and relational authenticity. This study advances PR research by identifying trust as the central mechanism linking ethical communication to consumer outcomes, challenging conventional assumptions about the nano- and micro-difference. It offers practical guidance for brands on influencer selection, disclosure strategies, and content design to strengthen ethical messaging effectiveness.

latest.title: Gender stereotypes and portrayals in advertising: implications for emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals in advertising shape early-stage emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults. It positions gendered advertising as both a branding issue and a responsible-marketing concern in youth-oriented marketplaces. Design/methodology/approach A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 159 valid responses from a Vietnamese sample concentrated mainly in the younger age segment; 83.6% of respondents were aged 14–26. Skincare and automobile advertising stimuli were used to manipulate stereotype congruity and the gender of the focal protagonist. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings Both gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals significantly influence emotional brand attachment across the experimental conditions. Emotional brand attachment, in turn, positively predicts brand sacredness and its three dimensions: communitas, supremacy and mesmerization. The findings are interpreted as immediate relational and symbolic responses within a youth- and young-adult-oriented sample, not as evidence of fully matured brand attachment or sacredness. Originality/value This study contributes to young-consumer and gender-in-advertising research by extending attention from proximal persuasion outcomes to early relational and symbolic brand outcomes. It clarifies the conceptual distinction between gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals and explains how these cues may shape early-stage attachment and sacredness-related perceptions among young consumers and young adults. The findings also offer responsible-marketing implications: although gendered portrayals may strengthen consumer–brand

latest.title: Marketing verde digital y lealtad hacia las marcas: evidencia de consumidores de Guayaquil
latest.abstract: La sostenibilidad y la digitalización han transformado la forma en que las marcas comunican sus compromisos ambientales y construyen relaciones con los consumidores. En este contexto, esta investigación analiza la relación entre el marketing verde digital y la lealtad hacia las marcas en consumidores de Guayaquil. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, no experimental y de corte transversal, con una muestra de 106 consumidores mayores de 18 años, seleccionados mediante muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia. La información se recopiló mediante un cuestionario estructurado con escalas Likert de cinco puntos y se analizó mediante modelos de ecuaciones estructurales por mínimos cuadrados parciales (PLS-SEM) utilizando SmartPLS 4. Los resultados muestran una relación positiva y estadísticamente significativa entre el marketing verde digital y la lealtad hacia las marcas (β = 0,687; t = 13,369; p < 0,001). El modelo explicó el 47,2 % de la varianza de la lealtad hacia las marcas (R² = 0,472). Estos resultados sugieren que la comunicación ambiental creíble, la transparencia y las estrategias sostenibles desarrolladas en entornos digitales se relacionan con una mayor lealtad hacia las marcas. El estudio aporta evidencia empírica sobre esta relación en un contexto urbano latinoamericano y plantea implicaciones para la gestión de estrategias digitales orientadas a la sostenibilidad.

latest.title: Opulent and Environmentally Responsible?: Brand‐ and Consumer‐Related Factors Shaping Consumer Responses to Sustainable Product Innovation Signals by Luxury Brands
latest.abstract: Academic Summary Luxury and environmental sustainability often appear fundamentally at odds: luxury derives its value from exclusivity, symbolic aspiration, and resource‐intensive craftsmanship, while sustainability demands restraint, reduced environmental impact, and responsible production. Yet luxury brands such as LVMH and Gucci are increasingly introducing sustainable product innovations, seeking to align with evolving consumer expectations and regulatory demands. For consumers, this creates a genuine tension: does a sustainably produced luxury personal good elevate its desirability, or quietly erode what makes it special in the first place? Despite the urgency of this question for both consumers and brands navigating the luxury‐sustainability interface, research on consumer responses to sustainable product innovation in luxury personal goods remains limited. Drawing on signaling and cue‐diagnosticity theory, this study examines how, why, and when consumers respond to luxury brands'' environmentally sustainable product innovation. Across a pilot and three main experimental studies, it explores consumer responses to sustainability signals, particularly considering skepticism surrounding the sustainability–luxury interface. Results show that consumers have more positive attitudes, higher purchase intentions, and greater willingness to recommend luxury brands engaged in sustainable versus conventional product innovation. This effect is partially mediated by consumers' feelings of specialness, a proximal, state‐like psychological mechanism. Moreover, transparency as a brand‐level signal and socially responsible consumer behavior as a consumer‐level characteristic strengthen the effectiveness of sustainable product innovation signals. These findings advance understanding

latest.title: Emotional Branding: A Comprehensive Literature Review
latest.venue: International Journal Of Applied Management And Economics
latest.abstract: Emotional branding (EB) has evolved from a practitioner-driven marketing (MKTG) philosophy mainly into a substantial stream of academic inquiry that examines how brands cultivate deep, affect-laden bonds with consumers that extend beyond functional attributes and rational appeals. This article offers a comprehensive review of the EB literature, synthesizing conceptual, theoretical, and empirical contributions published between 2005 and 2026. The review first traces the conceptual evolution of the construct, from Gobé's (2001) foundational manifesto to more recent operationalization grounded in brand attachment, brand love (BL), & brand resonance. Then, it examines the theoretical foundations that underpin this specific field, including brand relationship theory (BRT) (Fournier, 1998), attachment theory (AT), self-congruence theory (SCT), and consumer culture theory (CCT), before mapping the antecedents and outcomes of EB identified across qualitative, quantitative, and bibliometric studies. Drawing on evidence from diverse cultural and sectoral contexts, including Jordan, Indonesia, Italy, and the United States, the review demonstrates that EB consistently & positively predicts brand loyalty, brand attachment, customer satisfaction, & purchase share, while also carrying risks such as the emergence of doppelgänger brand imagery when emotional narratives are perceived as inauthentic. This review is concluded by identifying persistent gaps in the literature, particularly regarding cross-cultural generalizability, the measurement of EB as a multidimensional construct, and the paucity of longitudinal and experimental designs, and it proposes a research agenda to address these gaps. latest.title: Effect of Augmented Reality Marketing Strategies on Consumer Brand Performance of Hotels in South-South Nigeria
latest.venue: British Journal of Management and Marketing Studies
latest.abstract: The study examined the effect of augmented reality marketing strategies on consumer brand performance, using a case study of hotels in South-South Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from customers of hotels in Edo and Delta States, targeting a population of 312 regular guests. Using Taro Yamane's formula, a sample size of 175 was determined, and purposive sampling was employed to select respondents with AR marketing experience. A structured questionnaire was used as the research instrument. Reliability was confirmed using the test-retest reliability method. Data analysis utilized descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that interactive product demonstration (ß = 0.330, P < 0.05), virtual product placement (ß = 0.406, P < 0.05), and telepresence (ß = 0.166, P < 0.05) positively affect customer brand performance. The study concludes that augmented reality marketing strategies significantly enhance consumer brand performance in the hospitality industry. These strategies create immersive and engaging experiences that allow customers to interact with hotel offerings in a more personalized and meaningful way. The study recommended that hotels should integrate telepresence features, such as virtual tours and live customer interactions, to create a sense of connection and accessibility, further strengthening customer engagement and satisfaction.
