latest.title: Analisis Pengaruh Pemberian Diskon, Bundling Product, dan Kualitas Konten Melalui TikTok terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten melalui TikTok terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda secara parsial. Teknik pengambilan sampel yang digunakan adalah non probability sampling dengan jenis purposive sampling. Responden yang digunakan sebanyak 90 sampel. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner melalui Google Form dengan instrumen pengukuran menggunakan skala likert 1-5. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menggunakan regresi linier berganda dengan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) untuk mengolah dan menganalisis data. Pengujian meliputi uji instrument, uji asumsi klasik, uji koefisien determinasi (R2), dan uji t. Hasil penelitian menunjukan bahwa seluruh variabel independen diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap variabel dependen keputusan pembelian secara parsial. Dengan demikian, semakin baik diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten yang ditawarkan melalui TikTok, maka semakin tinggi pula keputusan pembelian konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda.

latest.title: Small Payments, Big Habits: Mental Accounting and Premium Subscription Decisions Among Young Digital Consumers
latest.venue: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering Management & Applied Science
latest.abstract: Freemium business models invite users to try a free service and later upgrade to a paid tier. Because premium fees are usually small and recurring, they may be evaluated in isolation rather than as part of total spending, a pattern explained by Thaler's theory of mental accounting. This study examines how mental accounting shapes the freemium-to-premium decisions of young consumers. Primary data were collected through a structured Google Forms questionnaire from 102 respondents (convenience sampling) who use digital subscription platforms, and analysed using percentage analysis, rank analysis, weighted average scores and chi-square tests. Most respondents were young (86.3% under 24), students (72.5%) and low-income (52.9% earn below ₹5,000 a month). Subscriptions were largely classed as entertainment expenses (58.8%), and 56.9% found ₹99–₹199 plans affordable. Respondents upgraded mainly to avoid advertisements (53.9%), and rank analysis placed better quality first among upgrade motives, with discounts last. Free trials were the most influential offer. Yet 29.4% did not compare subscription costs with any other spending, only 13.7% always monitored their subscriptions, and 23.5% reported auto-renewal as causing extra spending or budget problems. The findings suggest young users are value-conscious but monitor their subscriptions inconsistently, with implications for both consumers and service providers.

latest.title: Beyond Cashless Convenience: Understanding Financial Literacy, Cyber Fraud Vulnerabilities, and UPI Security Practices in the Modern Economy
latest.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital payment technologies has transformed retail commerce in India, positioning the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) as the primary transaction architecture across campuses and commercial markets. However, high operational usage does not necessarily equate to comprehensive financial capability or cybersecurity hygiene. This study examines the personal financial literacy competencies, cyber fraud vulnerabilities, and UPI security practices of retail consumers and micro-merchants based on a primary empirical survey of 120 respondents in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, utilizing a descriptive research design and structured bilingual questionnaires. The sample encompassed undergraduate students (61.7%), salaried young professionals (25.8%), and local micro-retailers (12.5%). The findings reveal near-universal formal banking inclusion (95.0%) and high daily UPI adoption (90.8%), yet expose critical cognitive and behavioral deficits: 78.3% of respondents budget irregularly or never, 51.7% cannot differentiate capital preservation (saving) from capital growth (investing), and 36.7% harbor the dangerous misconception that a UPI PIN is required to receive incoming funds. Furthermore, while 81.7% have been targeted by fraudulent communication and 36.7% have experienced fraud directly or through close contacts, 71.7% are completely unaware of the National Cybercrime Helpline 1930 or the critical 'Golden Hour' fund-freezing protocol. An overwhelming 88.4% expressed active demand for structured, peer-led safety workshops. The study concludes that sustainable digital financial inclusion requires shifting focus from transactional onboarding to practical, peer-led behavioral education, automated application safeguards, and prominent institutional dispute escalat

latest.title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions specifically within the used motorcycle showroom context.

latest.title: The Influence of Price and Facilities on Housing Purchase Decisions at Pasirjati Indah Regency, Bandung Regency
latest.abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: This study examines how prospective homebuyers’ perceptions of price and facilities influence their purchasing decisions at Pasirjati Indah Regency, Bandung Regency. Background Problems: Between 2020 and 2023, unit sales at this housing project fell from 88% to 35% of the target. A preliminary survey of 25 prospective buyers suggested possible concerns about price affordability and facility quality, but these descriptive ratings cannot establish the cause of the decline. Novelty: Earlier studies of price and facilities as predictors of housing purchase decisions report inconsistent effect sizes across local markets. This study tests both predictors, individually and jointly, in a single local market with a sharp sales decline, and reports their relative contribution to the purchasing decision. Research Methods: A quantitative survey was carried out with all 89 prospective buyers who visited or inquired at the sales office (total sampling). Questionnaire data were converted to an interval scale and analyzed with multiple linear regression in SPSS, after classical assumption tests. Finding/Results: Price (b = 0.383, p = 0.007) and facilities (b = 0.592, p < 0.001) each had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, and together they explained 32.5% of the variance (F = 20.678, p < 0.001). Facilities contributed more than price. Conclusion: Appropriate pricing and well-functioning facilities both matter for purchasing decisions, with facilities weighing more in this market. Developers should address financing affordability and visible facility quality together. The findings offer practical guidance for housing developers.

latest.title: Pengaruh persepsi harga dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian melalui citra merek pada Uniqlo Pekanbaru
latest.abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh persepsi harga dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian, baik langsung maupun melalui citra merek, pada konsumen Uniqlo di Kota Pekanbaru. Fokus ini dipilih karena konsumen fesyen semakin selektif dalam menilai harga, kualitas, dan citra merek sebelum membeli. Desain/metodologi/pendekatan – Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan kerangka stimulus–organisme–respons (S-O-R). Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner daring skala Likert 1–5 dari 105 responden yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling (berdomisili di Pekanbaru, berusia minimal 17 tahun, dan membeli produk Uniqlo minimal sekali dalam satu tahun terakhir). Kecukupan sampel diperiksa dengan analisis power dan metode inverse square root. Analisis memakai SEM-PLS (SmartPLS 4.0), dengan validitas diskriminan diuji melalui kriteria Fornell–Larcker, cross-loading, dan heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), serta common method bias diuji dengan uji Harman dan VIF kolinearitas penuh. Temuan – Model pengukuran valid dan reliabel (loading factor 0,754–0,893; AVE 0,675–0,785; composite reliability 0,905–0,930). Seluruh HTMT di bawah 0,90, tetapi pasangan citra merek–keputusan pembelian (0,859) melampaui 0,85. Uji common method bias tidak menunjukkan bias yang serius. Persepsi harga (β = 0,424) dan kualitas produk (β = 0,524) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap citra merek. Persepsi harga (β = 0,348), kualitas produk (β = 0,327), dan citra merek (β = 0,394) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Citra merek memediasi secara parsial pengaruh persepsi harga (0,167) dan kualitas produk (0,206) (seluruhnya p < 0,001). Model menjelaskan 69,0% varians keputusan pembelian dan 50,6% varians citra merek. Keterbatasan penelitian – Penelitian terbatas pada

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Promosi, dan Harga terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Sepeda Motor Honda pada Dealer Central Sakti Motor Nusukan
latest.abstract: Increasing competition in the motorcycle industry requires dealers to understand the factors that influence consumer purchase decisions, particularly through service quality, promotion, and price. This study aims to analyze the effects of service quality, promotion, and price on the purchase decision of Honda motorcycles at Central Sakti Motor Nusukan Dealer. The study uses a quantitative research method with data collected by distributing questionnaires to consumers who had purchased Honda motorcycles at Central Sakti Motor Nusukan Dealer. The sample consisted of 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data analyses included instrument testing, classical assumption testing, multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination (R²) testing. The results show that service quality had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.000 and a regression coefficient of 0.355. Promotion had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.000 and a regression coefficient of 0.446. Price also had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a significance value of 0.046 and a regression coefficient of 0.183. The F-test results show that the regression model was appropriate for use, with a significance value of 0.000, while the coefficient of determination test produced an Adjusted R Square of 0.725, indicating that service quality, promotion, and price explained 72.5% of the purchase decision, while the remaining 27.5% was influenced by other variables outside the research model. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that service quality, promotion, and price had positive and significant effects on the purchase decision of

latest.title: Determinants of Spotify Student Package Purchase Decisions among University Students: The Roles of Perceived Value, Hedonic Motivation, and Lifestyle
latest.abstract: The rapid development of digital music streaming services has transformed consumer behavior, particularly among university students who increasingly adopt subscription-based entertainment platforms. This study aims to examine the influence of perceived value, hedonic motivation, and lifestyle on purchase decisions for Spotify Student Package among university students in Surakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative research approach with a survey method was employed. The study population consisted of university students in Surakarta who used Spotify Student Package, with 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, F-test, and the coefficient of determination with the assistance of SPSS. The results indicate that perceived value has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.450 and a significance value of 0.000. Hedonic motivation also has a positive and significant influence on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.238 and a significance value of 0.027. Furthermore, lifestyle has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.329 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, perceived value, hedonic motivation, and lifestyle significantly influence Spotify Student Package purchase decisions, as indicated by an F-value of 134.115 with a significance level of 0.000. The adjusted R-square value of 0.801 demonstrates that the three independent variables explain 80.1% of the variation in purchase decisions. These findings highlight that students’ decisions to subscribe to digital music

latest.title: Pengaruh diskon dan gratis ongkos kirim terhadap keputusan pembelian di E-commerce shopee (studi kasus kepada masyarakat kelurahan Cengkareng Barat Jakarta Barat)
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of location and promotion on apartment purchasing decisions in Alam Sutera, specifically regarding PT Citra Anugerah Propertindo. The study employs a quantitative statistical method, with data collected through observation, interviews, and questionnaires. The study population consists of customers at Century 21 Victory. A non-probability sampling technique—specifically convenience sampling—was used, with a sample size of 76 respondents determined via the Slovin formula. Hypothesis testing involved both partial tests (t-test) and simultaneous tests (F-test). The results indicate a positive and significant influence of location on purchasing decisions, evidenced by a calculated t-value of 7.416 (exceeding the critical value of 1.993) and a significance level of 0.000 (< 0.05). Conversely, promotion did not have a significant partial effect on purchasing decisions, as shown by a calculated t-value of 1.513 (below 1.993) and a significance level of 0.000 (< 0.05). The F-test results show a calculated F-value of 146.851 (exceeding the critical F-table value of 3.12) with a significance level of 0.000 (< 0.05), indicating that the third hypothesis (Ha3) is accepted. Thus, it can be concluded that the variables of Location (X1) and Promotion (X2) simultaneously influence the purchasing decision (Y) for apartments in Alam Sutera marketed by PT Citra Anugerah Propertindo.

latest.title: Pengaruh Lifestyle dan Impulsive Buying terhadap Keputusan Pem-belian Konsumen Smartphone Apple di Kota Depok
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of lifestyle and impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously, on the purchasing decisions of Apple smartphone consumers in Depok City. The urgency of this study arises from the limited research directly examining the relationship between lifestyle, impulsive buying, and purchasing decisions without incorporating mediating variables such as purchase intention, particularly among consumers in Depok City. This study employed an associative quantitative approach with a survey design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 96 respondents who had previously purchased Apple smartphones and resided in Depok City. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, while the sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula. The collected data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, and hypothesis testing (t-test and F-test) with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The results revealed that lifestyle had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 5.426, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Impulsive buying also had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated t-value of 8.971, exceeding the critical t-value of 1.986, and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, lifestyle and impulsive buying had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a calculated F-value of 263.973, exceeding the critical F-value of 3.09, and a significance value of 0.000. These two variables collectively explained 85.0% of the variance in purchasing decisions. These findings suggest that companies

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: The Effect of Product Availability, Service Quality, Price Fairness and Store Trust on Repurchase Intention (A Study at Sari Jaya Tani Agricultural Store)
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of product availability, service quality, price fairness, and store trust on repurchase intention among customers of Sari Jaya Tani, an agricultural input store in Brebes Regency. A quantitative survey was conducted with 100 customers selected through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The four variables jointly had a significant effect on repurchase intention and explained 86.5% of its variance. Service quality, price fairness, and store trust each had a positive and significant effect, whereas product availability had no significant partial effect. Price fairness was the strongest predictor. The non-significant effect of product availability is discussed in relation to its overlap with store trust and the predominance of loyal customers in the sample. Agricultural input retailers should prioritize fair pricing, advisory service, and trust building while keeping stock reliable during planting seasons.

latest.title: Digital Payments and Consumer Spending Behaviour: Examining the Role of Convenience, Promotional Incentives and Impulse Buying in Urban Nepal
latest.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
latest.abstract: Digital payment services have increasingly transformed consumer purchasing practices and financial transactions in Nepal. This study examines the implications of digital payment services for the spending patterns of urban consumers, focusing on perceived convenience, promotional incentives, impulse purchasing, perceived overspending, expenditure monitoring and household savings. The study adopts a quantitative, cross-sectional research framework involving a structured questionnaire designed for 400 adult digital-payment users across eight majors urban centers in Nepal. The analysis examines consumer spending behaviour through descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, group comparisons, chi-square tests and multiple linear regression.

latest.title: Barriers to the Transition from Intention to Green Consumption Behavior: An Empirical Study in Ho Chi Minh City
latest.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
latest.abstract: pace, helping consumers translate positive environmental intentions into actual green consumption behavior has become increasingly important, particularly for advancing responsible production and consumption. Yet the persistent gap between green intention and green behavior suggests that a positive attitude and intention alone are not always enough to produce sustainable consumption. This study therefore examines the factors that shape green purchase intention and green consumption behavior, and analyzes the conditions that can either facilitate or hinder the translation of intention into actual consumer behavior in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Specifically, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study tests the effects of attitude (ATT), subjective norm (SN), and perceived behavioral control (PBC) on green purchase intention (GPI); the effect of GPI on green consumption behavior (GCB); the mediating role of GPI; and the moderating roles of price sensitivity (PS) and green product availability (PA). The study adopted a mixed-methods design. A preliminary qualitative phase was conducted through interviews and group discussions with 13 consumers to refine and finalize the observed variables. The quantitative phase was carried out through a face-to-face survey of consumers aged 18 and above who had lived in Ho Chi Minh City for at least six months and were involved in their household's purchasing decisions. Of the 400 questionnaires distributed, 354 valid responses were retained for analysis, corresponding to a response rate of 88.5%. The data were processed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 24.0. Scale reliability and construct validity were assessed through Cronbach's Alpha and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), including standardized factor loadings, composite relia

latest.title: Beyond Mutual Consent: Reconstructing Tarādin in Islamic Price Ethics amid Luxury Branding and Symbolic Consumption
latest.abstract: Premium price acceptance in the luxury product market is driven not only by functional utility, but also by brand heritage, exclusivity, and symbolic value—creating a pricing paradox in which elevated prices enhance rather than deter consumer desirability. Within Islamic economics, this phenomenon challenges classical assessments of consumer consent (tarāḍin), which primarily evaluate formal contractual assent and overt willingness to pay. This study aims to reconstruct tarāḍin within Islamic price ethics by shifting its analytical focus from formal agreement to the procedural integrity of value formation amid luxury branding and symbolic consumption. Employing a qualitative-conceptual library research method, this study systematically selected and synthesized foundational Qur’anic and fiqh al-mu‘āmalāt texts alongside peer-reviewed literature on Islamic business ethics, luxury branding, and symbolic consumption through thematic coding and comparative conceptual synthesis. From this analytical procedure, the study derives four interdependent dimensions in the proposed normative model of reconstructed tarāḍin: informational transparency, voluntary consent, value representation, and ethical price justice. Addressing the luxury pricing paradox, these four dimensions demonstrate that genuine consent requires evaluating whether symbolic prestige is communicated without deception (tadlīs), manufactured scarcity coercion, or gross price disparity (ghabn fāḥisy). This study offers a theoretical contribution to Islamic economic thought by extending tarāḍin beyond classical doctrines of honesty and contractual validity into an evaluative framework for contemporary luxury marketing. Because this framework represents a proposed normative model derived from conceptual synthesis, fut

latest.title: EFFECTS OF CONTENT MARKETING, SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING, AND PRODUCT QUALITY ON GLAD2GLOW PURCHASE DECISIONS AT NUSA BEAUTY STORE, NORTH ACEH MUARA BATU
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting Research Utility Finance and Digital Assets
latest.abstract: This study examines the partial effects of content marketing, social media marketing, and product quality on the purchase decisions of Glad2Glow products at Nusa Beauty Store, Muara Batu, North Aceh. Primary data were collected from 110 consumers selected through purposive sampling, using questionnaires distributed directly and through Google Forms. The instruments were tested for validity and reliability (Cronbach’s Alpha) and the data were checked with classical assumption tests (multicollinearity, heteroscedasticity, and normality). Multiple linear regression, the coefficient of determination, and t-tests were run in SPSS version 27. The results show that content marketing has no significant effect on purchase decisions (t = −0.363 < 1.659; sig. = 0.717). In contrast, social media marketing (t = 2.795; sig. = 0.006) and product quality (t = 3.099; sig. = 0.002) have positive and significant effects. The model explains 18.4% of the variation in purchase decisions (adjusted R²). Retailers should therefore prioritize interactive social media activities and consistently maintain product quality, while improving the informational value of their content.

latest.title: The Influence of Brand Image and Price Perception on Online Purchase Decisions on the Shopee Application in the North Cikarang Area
latest.venue: Majapahit Journal of Islamic Finance and Management
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of brand image and price perception on online purchase decisions among Shopee users in North Cikarang, Bekasi Regency. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used, employing multiple linear regression to estimate the direction and magnitude of the relationships. Using purposive non-probability sampling based on the Cochran formula, 100 respondents who had transacted on Shopee within the past six months and resided in North Cikarang were recruited via an online Likert-scale questionnaire. All instrument items for brand image, price perception, and purchase decision were valid and reliable, with Cronbach's Alpha values above 0.70. Classical assumption tests indicated that the regression residuals were normally distributed, free from multicollinearity, and free from heteroscedasticity. The regression results showed that brand image (B = 0.348; β = 0.321; t = 4.104; p < 0.001) and price perception (B = 0.601; β = 0.605; t = 7.740; p < 0.001) each had a significant positive effect on purchase decision. Simultaneously, both variables significantly predicted purchase decision, F(2, 97) = 168.531; p < 0.001, explaining 77.7% of the variance (R² = 0.777; adjusted R² = 0.772). Price perception showed a relatively stronger association than brand image based on standardized coefficients. These findings suggest that Shopee's platform reputation and consumers' evaluation of price fairness jointly play an important role in shaping purchase decisions, although the cross-sectional design and purposive sampling limit causal and probabilistic generalization.

latest.title: Determining the Effects of the 4Ps on Impulsive Mobile Shopping among College Students in Chengdu, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to determine the significant effects of the 4Ps marketing factors on impulsive mobile shopping among college students in Chengdu, China. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative approach using a cross-sectional survey questionnaire was employed. Data were collected from 500 college students who had experience using and purchasing from mobile shopping platforms. Purposive, quota, and convenience sampling techniques were used for data collection. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) were employed for data analysis and hypothesis testing. Results: Five out of seven hypotheses were supported. Product Marketing demonstrated the strongest effect on Satisfaction (β = 0.698), followed by Promotional Marketing (β = 0.138) and Price Marketing (β = 0.137). Place Marketing and Innovativeness did not significantly affect Satisfaction. Satisfaction significantly influenced Perceived Trust (β = 0.624), which in turn strongly affected Impulsive Mobile Shopping (β = 0.753). Conclusions: The findings extend the application of the 4Ps marketing theory to mobile commerce and highlight the critical role of trust in enabling impulsive purchasing behavior. The study provides valuable insights for mobile shopping platforms and marketers to prioritize product quality, develop effective promotional and pricing strategies, and build customer trust to enhance impulsive mobile shopping among college students.

latest.title: Brand Preference and Purchase Intention for Japanese Mobile Phones Among Middle-Aged Consumers in Chengdu
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study investigates the key determinants of brand preference and purchase intention for Japanese mobile phone brands among middle-aged consumers in Chengdu, China. Guided by the Theory of Reasoned Action (TRA) and Brand Equity Theory (BET), a conceptual framework was developed to examine the relationships among seven latent constructs: Brand Trust, Brand Image, Perceived Price, Perceived Quality, Advertising Value, Brand Preference, and Purchase Intention. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted, yielding 500 valid responses from residents aged 40-59 in the Jinjiang, Qingyang, and Jinniu districts with prior experience using Japanese mobile phones. Rigorous validity and reliability tests (IOC ≥ 0.6; Cronbach’s α ≥ 0.7) confirmed the measurement instrument’s psychometric soundness, and data were analyzed via Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to test hypothesized causal links. Results reveal that Brand Trust, Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and Advertising Value significantly enhance Brand Preference, which strongly predicts Purchase Intention. Theoretical contribution: This study enriches consumer behavior theory by integrating TRA and BET to unpack the mechanism of brand preference formation and purchase intention among middle-aged Chinese consumers, a understudied demographic in cross-cultural brand research. Managerial implications: The findings provide actionable strategies for Japanese mobile phone firms to optimize brand positioning in the Chengdu market, including prioritizing brand trust-building, refining brand image localization, and adjusting pricing and advertising strategies to align with middle-aged consumers’ preferences.

latest.title: Adaptive Pricing and Consumer Trust Enhancement to Sustain a Padang Culinary MSME: A Community Engagement Program for Air Talago
latest.abstract: Culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises face simultaneous pressure from raw-material price volatility, intense competition, changing consumer expectations, and the need for transparent digital communication. This community engagement article presents an integrated program for Air Talago, a Padang-food MSME in Serang. The proposal-based baseline identifies two connected priorities: the absence of a data-informed adaptive pricing system and the need to strengthen consumer trust through hygiene, halal assurance, consistent taste, service, and transparent information. The program applies participatory action research and asset-based community development. Activities include cost-of-goods calculation, competitor and customer review, value-based pricing, limited bundling and time-based offers, transparent price communication, hygiene and service procedures, recipe standardization, digital review management, simple bookkeeping, and monitoring. Evaluation is designed around a baseline, practical training, demonstrations, checklists, and follow-up indicators such as menu cost sheets, price lists, positive reviews, customer questions, and available transaction records. The article contributes an integrated community-engagement framework in which adaptive price decisions and consumer trust are developed together to support the continuity of a local culinary MSME.
keywords: culinary micro, small and medium enterprises

latest.title: Strengthening MSME Digital Marketing through Google Business Profile and Social Media Content Optimization: A Community Engagement Program for Air Talago
latest.abstract: Many local food micro, small, and medium enterprises still depend on walk-in customers and word-of-mouth promotion, which limits their digital discoverability and market reach. This community engagement article presents an integrated digital marketing program for Air Talago, a Padang-food microenterprise in Puri Anggrek, Serang. The program responds to three baseline challenges: incomplete local business information, irregular social media activity, and the absence of simple digital marketing governance. A participatory design combines initial observation, interviews, digital-channel auditing, practical training, mentoring, and outcome monitoring. The intervention consists of Google Business Profile creation or claim, information completion, product and location documentation, review-management training, social media profile improvement, content-pillar development, a one-month content calendar, and a simple operating procedure. Evaluation uses a completion checklist, pre-test and post-test, practical demonstrations, and platform insight indicators. The program contributes a practical model that links local search visibility, content communication, and partner capability rather than treating account creation as the final outcome. It is designed to improve the partner’s ability to manage digital marketing independently and continuously.

latest.title: Regulatory compliance and behavioural drivers of fintech adoption for financial inclusion in India
latest.venue: American International Journal of Humanities Arts and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Financial technology (FinTech) has widened access to payments, credit and insurance and supports financial inclusion and sustainable development, yet adoption remains uneven because users weigh digital trust and perceived risk against convenience. Research on the behavioural determinants of adoption and research on FinTech regulation have developed separately, so the way regulatory compliance shapes user behaviour is poorly explained. This study examines how regulatory compliance and behavioural attributes influence the adoption of FinTech services in India. It employs a qualitative, integrative literature synthesis with thematic content analysis of 67 secondary sources, comprising 57 scholarly publications, five official and institutional publications and five Indian statutes, of which 41 were published between 2024 and 2026. The results show six dominant theoretical lenses and eight recurring behavioural attributes: digital trust, perceived risk, financial and digital literacy, financial self-efficacy, loss aversion, herd behaviour, overconfidence and mental accounting. Of the 15 studies in the synthesis matrix, 10 include trust or perceived risk, whereas only three include government or regulatory support explicitly. India's compliance architecture rests on four regulators and six legal instruments covering payment authorisation, electronic transactions, anti-money laundering, digital identity, personal data protection and digital lending. The findings suggest that regulatory compliance acts as institutional assurance that works indirectly, by raising digital trust and lowering perceived risk, and is not a direct driver of adoption. Literacy and self-efficacy strengthen this pathway, while loss aversion weakens it. Two of the four propositions are supported and two a

latest.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ADVANCE SELLING PARTIAL PRICE AS A STRATEGY TO ENHANCE HOTEL ROOM PURCHASE DECISIONS IN BATAM CITY
latest.abstract: This study examines the role of sales promotion and price in shaping the effectiveness of Advance Selling Partial Price (ASPP) and its implications for hotel room purchase decisions in Batam City. It also explores whether ASPP effectiveness mediates the relationship between these marketing factors and purchasing decisions. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, the study collected primary data through questionnaires administered to guests who had booked rooms at hotels rated three stars or higher in Batam. Respondents were selected through purposive sampling, and the relationships among variables were assessed using a partial least squares structural equation modeling approach. The reported findings indicate that sales promotion and price have positive and significant associations with ASPP effectiveness. ASPP effectiveness, in turn, has a positive and significant relationship with hotel room purchase decisions. The study also reports a mediating role for ASPP effectiveness in the relationships between sales promotion, price, and purchasing decisions. These findings suggest that early-booking arrangements with partial payment options can be more attractive when supported by appealing promotional offers and competitive pricing. From a managerial perspective, the combined use of promotion, pricing, and advance selling may support consumers’ willingness to reserve rooms earlier while helping hotel operators manage demand and strengthen market competitiveness. The study contributes to discussions of service marketing and hotel revenue management in the context of Batam’s competitive accommodation market.

latest.title: Determination and Comparison of Service Quality with Customer Satisfaction of the Urban Sports Industry in Surabaya
latest.venue: Greenation International Journal of Economics and Accounting
latest.abstract: Although urban sports clubs in Surabaya are expanding rapidly, comparative studies examining service quality across different sports branches remain scarce. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, this study investigated how service quality shapes member satisfaction and compared performance across five Surabaya sports clubs based on 114 purposively selected active members. Data were evaluated through multiple linear regression and one-way ANOVA. Jointly, all five SERVQUAL dimensions strongly predicted member satisfaction (F = 239.669, p < 0.001) and accounted for 91.7% of total variance (Adjusted R² = 91.3%). On an individual level, Empathy (B = 0.645, p < 0.001) and Assurance (B = 0.192, p = 0.012) emerged as the primary positive drivers. In contrast, Tangibles (B = 0.026, p = 0.677), Reliability (B = 0.018, p = 0.765), and Responsiveness (B = 0.064, p = 0.436) showed non-significant partial effects owing to strong inter-dimension overlap (VIF = 4.727–9.801). Cross-club ANOVA comparisons further revealed meaningful differences in overall service quality (F = 3.248, p = 0.015) and member satisfaction (F = 3.369, p = 0.012), with Great Grace Futsal achieving the highest score and PB Darmaiksha the lowest. JEL : L31; L83; Z21.

latest.title: A Weber Fraction Explanation of Consumers’ Perceptions of Price
latest.abstract: Relying on well-accepted theories of human perception, this article offers a theoretically more accurate explanation of how consumers perceive and react to price information. Consistent with the vast amount of research on this topic, this research considers that consumers assess posted prices by comparing them to internal references. However, unlike the traditional approach, which theorizes that consumers’ responses are related to the raw numerical discrepancy between the two stimuli, this research explicitly incorporates the notion that in order to be sensed, perceived discrepancies must be greater than subjective minimums as outlined by Weber’s law. A comparison of the traditional approach versus the proposed framework reveals that explicitly incorporating subjective Weber fractions and just noticeable differences (JND) leads to a richer explanation of how consumers perceive prices. Theoretical and practical implications are also discussed.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF BRAND IMAGE, PROMOTION, AND PRICE ON THE PURCHASING DECISION NETWORK SERVICES AT PT. JARINGAN REGISTRI INDONESIA
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive internet network service industry requires companies to understand the factors influencing consumer purchasing decisions. PT Jaringan Registri Indonesia faces challenges such as customer fluctuations, increasing churn rates, and competition with other network service providers. This study aims to analyze the influence of brand image, promotion, and price on purchasing decisions for network services at PT Jaringan Registri Indonesia, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach using multiple linear regression analysis through instrument testing, classical assumption tests, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that brand image, promotion, and price partially have a positive and significant influence on purchasing decisions. Furthermore, these three variables simultaneously have a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with the ability to explain 80.3% of the variation in purchasing decisions. The strength of this study lies in examining three integrated marketing factors within the context of the competitive internet network service industry, providing a more comprehensive understanding of consumer behavior compared to studies that only examine one or two marketing variables. This research provides practical implications for companies in developing strategies to improve brand image, enhance promotional effectiveness, and optimize price perceptions in order to increase customer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF SERVICE QUALITY, PRICE AND CUSTOMER TRUST ON PURCHASING DECISIONS FOR GRANITE AT DEKOR ART GATOT SUBROTO
latest.venue: Bulletin of Engineering Science Technology and Industry
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine and analyze the effect of service quality, price, and consumer trust on purchasing decisions for Galileo granite at Dekor Art Gatot Subroto, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach using an associative research design. The population consisted of consumers who had purchased Galileo granite at Dekor Art Gatot Subroto, with a sample of 100 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires, while the data analysis techniques used multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results showed that service quality had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.531, a t-value of 7.082, and a significance value of 0.000. Price had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.186, a t-value of 2.764, and a significance value of 0.007. Consumer trust had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.486, a t-value of 7.547, and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, service quality, price, and consumer trust had a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions, with an F-value of 125.533 and a significance value of 0.000. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.791 indicates that service quality, price, and consumer trust explain 79.1% of the variation in purchase decisions, while the remaining 20.9% is explained by other factors outside the research model.

latest.title: Building Customer Loyality for Marning Corn in Bulukumba: The Impact of Brand Image, Service Quality, and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions and Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
latest.abstract: Marning corn products, typical food, and souvenirs from the Bulukumba district are packaged simply without complete product information. Yet by integrating well-designed packaging with clear and relevant product information that can improve product quality, brands can improve the overall consumer experience, build trust, and foster long-term loyalty. This research aims to analyze the direct and indirect influence of brand image, service quality, and product quality on purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction on consumer loyalty to making corn. The research method used quantitative analysis with structured interview techniques using a sample of corn buyers in Bulukumba Regency. The data analysis used is structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis using the AMOS application. The research results show that consumer satisfaction and brand image have a significant direct influence on loyalty. Brand image and service quality have an impact on purchasing decisions. Product quality, service quality, and brand image influence consumer satisfaction. Meanwhile, the variables of service quality and production quality do not have a significant effect on consumer loyalty through purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction as intervening variables of brand image, service quality, and production quality. Increasing income in the Morning Corn business can be achieved by prioritizing brand image, service quality, and product quality so that later it can increase the number of buyers and increase consumer loyalty. Keywords: Customer loyalty, buying decision, customer satisfaction, brand image, service quality, product quality and marning corn.

latest.title: Social media, brand image, and price perception as predictors of purchase decisions: Evidence from kopi kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia
latest.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
latest.abstract: This study examines whether social media, brand image, and price perception are associated with the purchase decisions of Kopi Kenangan consumers in Manado, Indonesia, a regional market in which prior findings for this brand are mixed. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 100 customers, recruited through purposive sampling offline and online, was analyzed with multiple linear regression. Social media and brand image were positively and significantly associated with purchase decisions, with effects of comparable and moderate size. Price perception showed no significant association, and its confidence interval included zero, so no direction of effect can be inferred. Together, the three predictors explained about one quarter of the variance in purchase decisions. The study provides jointly estimated effects, confidence intervals, and effect sizes for three commonly studied predictors in an Eastern Indonesian city. Informative social media content and a consistent brand image are associated with purchase decisions, whereas the study offers no evidence for or against a price-perception association. Non-probability sampling, a single time point, self-reported data, and modestly reliable price and purchase-decision scales limit generalization.

latest.title: Financial Literacy Calibration and Retail Investor Behavior on Digital Trading Platforms: A Literature Review
latest.abstract: The number of young retail investors in Indonesia has surged while capital market literacy remains low, making the role of financial literacy in curbing investor bias a central issue in financial management. This article maps evidence on financial literacy, self-confidence, and retail investor behavior on digital trading platforms and proposes a conceptual framework. An integrative literature review was conducted on 29 sources: 18 empirical or analytical studies, seven reviews or meta-analyses, two theoretical or methodological references, and two contextual data sources. The synthesis shows that the role of literacy in reducing bias is not uniform because it depends on the type of bias and on how literacy is measured; confidence in one's own knowledge can raise market participation as well as trading intensity; and platform design shapes behavior, especially among investors with low literacy. As a conceptual contribution, the article proposes a Literacy–Confidence–Platform (L-K-P) framework centered on the calibration gap between objective literacy and confidence, accompanied by six testable propositions. Future research should combine objective literacy tests with actual transaction data and field experiments on investment platforms in Indonesia.

latest.title: Pengaruh Online Customer Review Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Sepatu Dengan Brand Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna E-Commerce di Kabupaten Tangerang
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh online customer review terhadap keputusan pembelian sepatu, pengaruh online customer review terhadap brand trust, pengaruh brand trust terhadap keputusan pembelian, serta peran brand trust dalam memediasi hubungan online customer review dan keputusan pembelian pada pengguna e-commerce di Kabupaten Tangerang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis asosiatif. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner daring dengan skala Likert lima tingkat. Sampel berjumlah 105 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis data dilakukan dengan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) menggunakan SmartPLS. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa online customer review berpengaruh positif terhadap brand trust (β = 0,581; p < 0,001) dan keputusan pembelian (β = 0,245; p = 0,001). Brand trust juga berpengaruh positif terhadap keputusan pembelian (β = 0,619; p < 0,001). Pengaruh tidak langsung online customer review terhadap keputusan pembelian melalui brand trust bernilai positif dan signifikan (β = 0,360; p < 0,001). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa brand trust berperan sebagai mediator dalam hubungan antara online customer review dan keputusan pembelian sepatu. Meskipun demikian, hasil evaluasi validitas diskriminan dan model fit menunjukkan beberapa hal yang perlu diperhatikan dalam interpretasi hasil penelitian.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Perceived Value, Consumer Engagement, and Purchase Intention in Virtual Influencer Marketing: The Role of Source Credibility and Generational Cohort
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: As virtual influencers gain popularity, understanding the factors driving consumer responses is essential. However, limited research explores how perceived value (informativeness, entertainment, novelty, and incentives) and consumer engagement influence purchase intention. Perceived value is a key predictor of consumer behavior, while consumer engagement enhances perceived value and marketing effectiveness. Additionally, the moderating roles of source credibility and generational cohort remain underexplored. This study examines these relationships through a survey of 331 Chinese Generation Y and Z consumers, analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that informativeness, entertainment, and incentives positively influence purchase intention, while novelty has a negative effect. Consumer engagement drives purchase intention and enhances perceived value. Source credibility and generational cohort moderate these effects. When source credibility is low, novelty reduces purchase intention, while incentives increase it. High source credibility makes consumer engagement more influential. Informativeness enhances purchase intention among Generation Y, whereas Generation Z is more influenced by consumer engagement. This study extends research on advertising value and consumer engagement, offering insights for brands optimizing virtual influencer marketing strategies across different consumer segments.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als

hot.title: Do Consumers Perceive Impulsive Buying and Pain of Payment? E-Commerce Transactions Using Pay Later, E-Wallet, and Cash-On-Delivery
hot.venue: Gadjah Mada International Journal of Business
hot.abstract: This study investigates how modern payment options, pay-later, e-wallets, and COD affect online shopping behavior, specifically on impulsive purchases and the feeling of regret after spending, known as the pain of payment. While numerous studies have individually assessed the impact of these payment modalities, there was a paucity of research examining the combined effect of these three contemporary payment methods within experimental frameworks. This study also examines whether buying groceries or fashion items influences these behaviors. The research involved 162 consumers divided into 6 groups based on the type of payment method (pay-later, e-wallet, cash-on-delivery) and type of products (grocery and fashion). The study found that the chosen payment method has no significant impact on impulsive buying behavior. However, customers are more likely to purchase fashion items impulsively than groceries. The pay-later option, especially for fashion items, led to the most impulsive buying and the strongest feeling of payment regret. On the other hand, using COD for fashion items was the least popular, and e-wallets generally led to lower overall spending. The study also found that people spend more time shopping for groceries than fashion. Both thought processes and emotions influenced the decision to buy. Interestingly, paying with COD helped improve self-control and reduce negative feelings. Based on the control theory of self-regulation, this research provides insights into managing spending and achieving customer financial goals, highlighting the connection between payment options, impulsive buying, and consumer well-being.

hot.title: The role of robo-advisors in behavioural finance, shaping investment decisions
hot.abstract: This study focuses on using artificial intelligence-driven financial robo-advisors in the investment decision-making domain by retail investors. Based on heuristic and prospect theory, the researcher aims to examine how AI-powered financial robo-advisors (AIPFRA), through their perceived interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretation and structural assurance, influence retail investors’ loss aversion and overconfidence biases, ultimately enhancing robo-advisor usage in investment decision-making. Using purposive sampling, data from 461 retail investors were collected and analysed through structural equation modelling using SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that, except for structural assurance, robo-advisors’ perceived personalisation, interactivity, autonomy and algorithm transparency substantially mitigated investors’ overconfidence and loss-aversion biases, enhancing robo-advisor usage for investment decision-making. The study highlights the significance of financial literacy in moderating the relationship between biases and the use of robo-advisors. The study contributed by extending Heuristic and Prospect Theories to the AI-driven robo-advisor investment ecosystem. The study comprehensively explains how AI-powered robo-advisor design features impact investor psychology and adoption by bridging behavioural biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence with technology mechanisms like interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretability and structural assurance. The results can help financial institutions implement user-centric advisory tools and help fintech developers create more bias-aware robo-advisors.

hot.title: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce: A literature review and research agenda
hot.abstract: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce (LSC) is an emerging phenomenon characterized by spontaneous, unplanned purchases driven by real-time social interactions. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking consensus on antecedents, theoretical perspectives, and outcomes. This fragmentation hinders theoretical development and accumulation of knowledge of this research stream. To address these issues, this study provides a systematic review of impulse buying in LSC, synthesizing key research trends, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we propose an integrative framework that consolidates antecedents, psychological mechanisms, and outcomes of impulse buying within LSC. This comprehensive synthesis clarifies existing inconsistencies and offers structured avenues for future research. For practitioners, our framework identifies critical platform features, streamer attributes, and consumer characteristics that influence impulse buying, enabling more effective strategies and responsible practices in LSC.

hot.title: Decomposing Brand Loyalty: An Examination of Loyalty Subcomponents, Product Price Range, Consumer Personality, and Willingness to Pay
hot.abstract: Brand loyalty is widely recognized as a key driver of consumer behavior, significantly influencing their willingness to pay more for preferred brands. This study explores the relationship between brand loyalty, its components, willingness to pay, consumer personality traits, and product price range. A tailored online survey involving participants aged 18 to 60 revealed a strong positive correlation between brand loyalty and increased willingness to pay. The findings also underscore the influence of Conscientiousness and Energy on brand loyalty, alongside the moderating effect of product price range. Specifically, habit-based loyalty dominates low-priced, routine purchases, while higher-priced decisions involve deeper cognitive-affective evaluations. These insights offer valuable guidance for enhancing customer satisfaction and optimizing brand profitability.

hot.title: The Impact of 7Ps Green Marketing Mix on Customer Commitment and Willingness to Pay a Premium Price: Evidence from Vietnam
hot.abstract: As consumers prioritize environmental issues and sustainable development, using green elements in marketing strategy has become valuable. This research examines how the 7Ps green marketing mix influences customer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price for green products, focusing on the role of green brand loyalty, association, and perceived quality. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 571 young Vietnamese consumers reveals that different green 7Ps components exert distinct effects on green consumer-based brand equity (CBBE). While prior research largely focuses on green product, price, place and promotion, limited attention has been given to green human factors, process, and physical evidence, which this study addresses. The findings of this study not only confirm the significant influence of green CBBE dimensions on consumer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price but also enriches the green marketing and consumer behavior literature. Moreover, these provide practical strategies for businesses and policymakers in emerging markets to effectively leverage green marketing, strengthen consumer commitment, implement premium pricing strategies, and contribute to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: Impulsive Buying Tendencies and Personality: Cognitive and Affective Aspects
hot.abstract: Impulsive buying is a growing problem in modern society with significant financial and psychological consequences, and it is necessary to examine the mechanisms underlying it. Understanding the mechanisms driving this behavior is crucial. Impulsive buying consists of two key aspects: a cognitive aspect, characterized by a lack of planning and reflection, and an affective aspect, involving emotional responses that can occur before, during, or after a purchase. This study aims to explore the relationship between personality traits, as measured by the HEXACO model, and tendencies toward impulsive buying. Specifically, it examines how the HEXACO traits differentially predict the cognitive and affective components of impulsive buying tendencies. Data were collected from a sample of 420 students, with 32 excluded due to incomplete responses, resulting in a final sample of 388 students (155 men, 233 women) with an average age of 22.8. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that HEXACO personality domains significantly predicted overall impulsive buying tendencies. As expected, Honesty–Humility and Conscientiousness were negatively associated with impulsive buying, while Emotionality and Extraversion positively predicted impulsive buying tendencies. Moreover, Honesty–Humility, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion significantly predicted the cognitive component of impulsive buying, while Honesty–Humility and Emotionality were significant predictors of the affective component. These findings suggest the importance of educating individuals, from an early age, on the negative consequences of impulsive buying, effective money-saving strategies, and the principles of mental accounting.

hot.title: Anthropomorphism in artificial intelligence: a game-changer for brand marketing
hot.abstract: The expansion of brands adopting artificial intelligence services with human characteristics, such as chatbots, has revolutionized digital marketing strategies, transforming how companies reach and engage customers. This technological innovation is reshaping digital interactions between companies and consumers, offering a more personalized and efficient experience. This study explores the influence of chatbot anthropomorphism on customer engagement and purchasing decision-making with brands that use this artificial intelligence service. Data from a questionnaire with 1319 participants was analyzed using partial least squares method. Chatbot anthropomorphism has a more positive influence on purchasing decision-making when this relationship is mediated by customer engagement. In turn, customer involvement also has a positive influence on decision-making. The results emphasize that for a greater influence of the chatbot's anthropomorphism on purchasing decision-making, the customer must first be engaged with the chatbot. This research illuminates a new path in the domain of AI-enabled brand interactions, showing the distinct influence of anthropomorphism in chatbots on customer satisfaction, trust and loyalty, thus revolutionizing traditional paradigms of consumer-brand engagement and decision-making processes. By exploring the intricate dynamics between customer engagement with anthropomorphized chatbots and purchasing decisions, this study breaks new ground, offering unprecedented insight into the transformative potential of human-like chatbot interactions in shaping consumer behavior and brand relationships.

hot.title: Buy Now, Pay Later: Impact of Installment Payments on Customer Purchases
hot.abstract: “Buy now, pay later” (BNPL) installment payments allow customers to pay for purchases in a series of interest-free installments over a short period of time. This research provides novel insights into how customer adoption of BNPL installment payments impacts spending. The authors leverage customer-level transaction data before and after the introduction of a BNPL installment payment service at a large U.S. retailer. A difference-in-differences analysis indicates that the adoption of BNPL installment payments is associated with (1) an increase in purchase incidence and (2) larger purchase amounts. These effects are statistically and economically significant over time. Moreover, this increase in spending is greater for smaller- (vs. larger-) basket shoppers and for shoppers who relied more heavily on credit (vs. debit) cards before adoption. Three preregistered experiments show that BNPL installment (vs. lump sum) payments increase spending by reducing perceived financial constraints. Specifically, BNPL installments alleviate perceived financial constraints by reducing perceived costs and facilitating budget control. These findings highlight the substantive role of BNPL installment payments in shaping purchase behavior and provide important implications for the management of BNPL payment schemes.

hot.title: The push-pull-mooring model of consumer service switching: a meta-analytical review to guide future research
hot.venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice
hot.abstract: Purpose For nearly 2 decades, the push-pull-mooring (PPM) model has been used frequently by scholars to explain consumers’ service switching intention and behavior. However, heterogeneity and incomparability between PPM model studies are prevalent issues: The chosen predictor variables, their categorization, their measurement, reported effect sizes, and effect directions vary considerably. By addressing these issues, the present meta-analytical review enables future researchers applying the PPM model to identify relevant variables and use valid measurements. Design/methodology/approach Based on 148 empirical studies employing the PPM model, the variables used to predict consumers’ service switching intention and behavior, their frequency of use, their categorization into push, pull, and mooring factors, and their measurement are assessed. The effect sizes and directions of the relationships between these variables and consumers’ service switching intention and behavior are analyzed using meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Additionally, the predictive capacity of this model and the influence of moderators are assessed. Findings Among the 148 empirical studies, 382 different independent variables were used. The three most frequently used and distinctly categorized independent variables are dissatisfaction (push), alternative attractiveness (pull), and switching costs (mooring). Overall, 152 unique sources were cited to measure these variables and the dependent variables. Dissatisfaction and alternative attractiveness increase switching intention, which positively affects switching behavior, while switching costs decrease switching intention. The model explains 30% of the variance in switching intention and 31% of the variance in switching behavior. Originality/va

hot.title: From perceived green product quality to purchase intention: the roles of price sensitivity and environmental concern
hot.abstract: Purpose This research seeks to address the existing gaps in the literature by rigorously investigating the influence of consumers’ perceived green product quality (PPQ), price sensitivity to green products (PRS) and environmental concern (ENC) on their intention to purchase green products (GPI) within the context of green circular economies. Furthermore, the study will explore the role of PRS as a mediator and ENC as a moderator by applying the price-expectancy model (PEM) and social exchange theory (SET). Design/methodology/approach The purposive sampling technique was employed to analyse 412 online survey responses from consumers, utilising partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings indicate a positive relationship between PPQ and PRS and PRS and GPI, contradicting the hypothesised negative associations. This suggests that as consumers become increasingly price-sensitive, they perceive green products to possess higher quality without diminishing their purchase intentions. Additionally, PPQ is positively associated with GPI, implying that enhanced perceptions of quality directly contribute to an increased intention to purchase green products. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that while ENC moderates the relationship between PPQ and PRS, its practical significance is limited. Practical implications This research emphasises to marketers that they should prioritise quality features while addressing PRS, particularly for environmentally concerned consumers, which can effectively shape consumers’ GPI. Originality/value This study’s originality lies in its integration of PRS and ENC within green consumerism. This offers valuable insights into green marketing and provides marketers with practical strategies to tackle the challenge

hot.title: Perceived Price Fairness as a Mediator in Customer Green Consumption: Insights from the New Energy Vehicle Industry and Sustainable Practices
hot.abstract: This paper explores how to promote consumer identification and acceptance of green products in the field of sustainable consumption and green marketing. Specifically, this paper examines how green factors affect consumers’ willingness to purchase new energy vehicles (NEVs) and focuses on the mediating role played by perceived price equity in this process. It is found that consumers’ green self-identity, green product experience, and green product innovation have a significant positive impact on their willingness to purchase NEVs, while perceived price fairness plays an important mediating role in this process. When consumers perceive that the pricing of NEVs is fair, they are more inclined to purchase them. Through the analysis of China’s new energy vehicle market, this paper puts forward suggestions to optimize the promotion strategy of green products from the perspective of price fairness, with a view to providing theoretical support and practical guidance for relevant enterprises. As China is the world’s number one country in terms of NEV ownership, studying its market consumption willingness not only reveals the unique characteristics of the Chinese market but also provides lessons and references for the future development of the new energy vehicle market in other countries, which is of great exemplary significance.

hot.title: Obstacles and opportunities for sustainable consumption: A comprehensive conceptual model, literature review, and research agenda
hot.abstract: Meaningful shifts in consumption habits are essential to mitigate climate change and reduce global environmental degradation. Yet, despite the climate urgency and growing consumer concerns, the widespread adoption of sustainable behaviors has proven difficult. Why is this the case? How has the growing interdisciplinary field of sustainable consumption contributed to this debate? And where are the knowledge gaps? Guided by a comprehensive conceptual model, this article (a) delves into the key market, individual, and s ocietal obstacles that hinder consumers from adopting more environmentally sustainable behaviors, (b) explores how practitioners and policymakers can help consumers minimize or circumvent these deterrents, and (c) highlights the pressing gaps in the literature, offering a roadmap for advancing our understanding of how to promote sustainable practices across the consumer journey—from search and purchase to usage and disposal.

hot.title: Drivers of Purchase Intentions of Generation Z on Eco-Products
hot.abstract: Concerns about environmental protection and sustainable consumption increased among Generation Z, as a consequence of more perceived risks emerging in the context of climate change and depletion of natural resources. The aim of the present research was to identify the main factors that influence the intention to purchase eco-products among the young generation. Quantitative marketing research was carried out on a sample of 269 Gen Z. The research results proved that purchasing intention for eco-products is strongly influenced by the perceived quality of environmentally friendly products, consumer consciousness about eco-products, perceived value of green products, and consumer trust in ecological products.
